papers.title: Autocatalytic order controls bistability in a conservative kinetic model of relational event progression
papers.summary: This version supersedes earlier versions and develops the three-class model of v1 into a closed, conserved network. On a relational view, the Universe is the happening of events rather than a container for them. A kinetic model gives this dynamical form: events are sorted as future, now or past; future events combine reversibly into now events; a now event meeting past events is activated and completes irreversibly into past events, which are renewed for future use. Past events thus catalyse their own production in a closed network conserving a weighted event count. We give a complete mass-action and bifurcation analysis. Conservation fixes the stoichiometry uniquely. When one past event participates in each activation, progression ignites softly at a transcritical threshold and no fold can arise, for every completion yield. When two participate cooperatively, the progressing branch folds: a past-rich attractor coexists with a past-poor state and ignition needs a finite perturbation. Cooperative order creates memory; nonequilibrium asymmetry only sets how hard it is to undo, strict one-way latching being a singular limit of hysteresis. In a partially reversible network where only renewal is reversible, two stable interior states coexist while activation and completion stay strictly one-way. The work is theoretical and does not derive time or its arrow: relational ordering and local irreversibility are assumed. As stated postulates, events are parcels of energy, the budget is conserved energy, and the activated class is the activated complex of transition-state theory. Around each cycle both the budget and the event number are conserved; at steady state the composition is stationary while energy is concentrated and dispersed locally, and whether entropy production vanishes globally is posed as a hypothesis.

papers.title: Causal analysis of inner and outer motions in near-wall turbulence
papers.summary: In this work, we study the causality of near-wall inner and outer turbulent motions. The inner motions are defined as the self-sustained near-wall cycle, and the outer motions as those living in the logarithmic layer exhibiting footprints on the near-wall region. Causal inference with three typical methods is performed, \emph{i.e.} transfer entropy, information flow, and SURD (synergistic--unique--redundant decomposition of causality). The causal inference methods are first applied to several canonical problems to illustrate their abilities, including a linear problem, a non-linear problem, and a low-dimensional model of near-wall turbulence. It is demonstrated that all three methods can produce consistent causal findings. Furthermore, we study the causalities between the inner and outer turbulent motions in a channel flow using the three methods with an improved inner-outer decomposition method. It is revealed that both the inner and outer motions are causally self-sustained, supporting the self-sustaining mechanism of turbulent motions at all scales. We also find that there are top-down and bottom-up causalities between the outer motions and their near-wall footprints owing to the dynamical coherence of inclined large-scale turbulent motions. More interestingly, pressure is identified to play an active role in the inner-outer causalities and may act as a bridge in linking the inner and outer turbulent motions.

papers.title: Nonlinear eigenvalue algorithm for $GW$ quasiparticle equations
papers.summary: The use of the Green's function in quantum many-body theory often leads to nonlinear eigenvalue problems, as the Green's function needs to be defined in the energy domain. The GW approximation method is one typical example. In this article, we introduce a method based on the FEAST eigenvalue algorithm for accurately solving the nonlinear eigenvalue G0W0 quasiparticle equation. Based on the FEAST contour integral method for nonlinear eigenvalue problems, the energy (eigenvalue) domain is extended to the complex plane. An analytic continuation is introduced to the calculation of the GW self-energy to carry the imaginary parts of both Green's functions and FEAST contour quadrature nodes. Calculation results for various molecules are presented and compared with the more conventional graphical solution approximation method and spectral functions method. It is confirmed that the highest occupied molecular orbital from the Kohn-Sham (and Hartree-Fock) equation is very close to that of GW, while the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital shows noticeable differences.

papers.title: An Approximate-Master-Equation Formulation of the Watts Threshold Model on Hypergraphs
papers.summary: In traditional models of behavioral and opinion dynamics on networks, researchers suppose that interactions occur between pairs of individuals. However, in reality, social interactions also occur in sets of three or more individuals. A common way to incorporate such polyadic interactions is to study dynamical processes on hypergraphs, in which interactions can occur between any number of the individuals. A major current effort is to generalize popular dynamical processes from graphs to hypergraphs. One important model is the Watts threshold model (WTM), which describes a simplistic social spreading process and was extended recently by Chen et al. from dyadic networks (i.e., ordinary graphs) to polyadic networks (i.e., hypergraphs). In the present paper, we extend their discrete-time model to continuous time by using approximate master equations (AMEs). By employing AMEs, we are able to very accurately model the mean behavior of the continuous-time system. We reduce the high-dimensional AME system to a system of three coupled ordinary differential equations without any detectable loss of accuracy. This much lower-dimensional system is computationally faster to solve numerically, and it is also easier to interpret. We linearize the reduced AME system and derive a cascade condition, which allows us to determine when a large spreading event occurs. We then examine our reduced AME system on a contact hypergraph of a French primary school and on a hypergraph of computer-science coauthorships. We find that our full and reduced AME systems give reasonably good descriptions of the mean time-dependent fraction of active nodes in the polyadic WTM dynamics on these empirical networks.

papers.title: Breakdown of sequential tunnel ionization in ultrashort electromagnetic pulses
papers.summary: We consider double ionization of one- and two-dimensional atomic systems modeling neutral helium, xenon and the negative bromine ion in intense low-frequency electromagnetic fields. By solving numerically the two-electron time-dependent Schr{\"o}dinger equation under conditions which exclude recollisions, we demonstrate that while for pulses of a few tens of femtoseconds duration and longer the sequential single-electron approximation perfectly describes the ionization dynamics, for pulses as short as few femtoseconds this picture breaks down entirely, and the electron-electron interaction suppresses the rate of ionization by roughly one order of magnitude.

papers.title: Multi-resolution training-enhanced Kolmogorov-Arnold networks for physics-informed learning of PDEs with multi-scale features
papers.summary: PDE problems with multi-scale features present significant challenges in scientific computing. While conventional deep learning methods based on multi-layer perceptrons exhibit spectral bias in resolving multi-scale features, physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold networks mitigate this issue through their architectural design and show advantages in representing multi-scale physical fields. On the other hand, insights from information bottleneck theory suggest that high-resolution sampling is important for capturing multi-scale behavior, but this requirement often leads to increased computational cost. To address this issue, we propose a simple yet effective multi-resolution training-enhanced Kolmogorov-Arnold network framework, which trains the model sequentially or alternately at different resolutions. The proposed framework is validated on various forward and inverse PDE problems with multi-scale features. Numerical results indicate that this training strategy effectively reduces computational cost without sacrificing accuracy, thereby enabling the efficient solution of complex multi-scale PDE problems in both forward and inverse settings.

papers.title: Taylor dispersion and large-deviation structure in stagnation-point flows without homogenisation
papers.summary: We study the long-time dispersion of a passive scalar in linearly accelerating flows whose strain rate $v(\eta)$ varies transversely: the axially strained flow in a porous tube with wall injection, and radially strained stagnation-point flows over a wall (Homann and von K\'arm\'an flows). Exponential stretching outpaces cross-sectional diffusion, so the scalar never homogenises across the section and classical cross-sectional averaging fails. Instead, in the logarithm of the stretched coordinate the problem becomes a Taylor dispersion problem, with mean log-stretching rate $U=\Lambda'(0)$ and log-space diffusivity $D=\tfrac{1}{2}\Lambda''(0)$: Taylor dispersion emerges without homogenisation, and only because the strain varies transversely. A Mellin-transform analysis, based on the principal eigenvalue $\Lambda(q)$ of the transverse advection-diffusion operator augmented by $qv$, gives the large-time structure in terms of the log-speed $x=\ln|\boldsymbol\xi|/t$, where $\boldsymbol\xi\in \mathbb R^d$ denotes the stretching directions ($d=1$ axial and $d=2$ radial). Essentially all the scalar mass lies in a log-normal bulk at $x=U$, flanked by forward and rear large-deviation tails with mass density $e^{-I(x)t}$, where $I(x)$ is the rate function (i.e., the Legendre transform of $\Lambda(q)$) Behind the rear tail, below $x_*=\Lambda'(-d)<U$, a plateau independent of $\boldsymbol\xi$ decays at the rate $-\Lambda(-d)$. It carries the highest concentrations but only a fraction $e^{-I(x_*)t}$ of the mass. A thin transition zone joins the plateau to the rear tail. For uniformly strained flows, as in the Burgers vortex, all regions collapse onto a single Gaussian.

papers.title: Generalized Time-Reversal for Pulse Control in Diffusive Media
papers.summary: Time-reversal symmetry allows waves to retrace their paths through complex media and refocus at their origin. However, incomplete capture and reversal of scattered waves often limit pulse recovery. We address this challenge for spatially extended sources by introducing a generalized time-reversal framework, which identifies the optimal source pattern as the one that maximizes the energy of the waves that are captured and reversed. We experimentally verify it in a two-dimensional diffusive waveguide, showing the peak transmitted power at the recovery time is doubled over standard time-reversal. Internal spatiotemporal dynamics, reconstructed from frequency-resolved measurements, reveal a ``loading and firing" process in which energy accumulates within the medium and then is released abruptly. Time-reversing this burst enables deep energy delivery into the scattering medium. Generalized time-reversal opens new possibilities for short-pulse control in scattering media, with applications ranging from optogenetics to random laser amplification.

papers.title: The Weakly-Nonlinear Admittance at Open Ends of Two- and Three-Dimensional Acoustic Waveguides
papers.summary: We formulate a weakly-nonlinear exit condition for open ends of acoustic waveguides; to our knowledge this is the first time a general acoustic open end has been analysed outside the linear regime. The formulation neglects mean flow, vortex separation, and viscous effects. The resulting admittance boundary condition, and its weakly-nonlinear counterpart, extend recent weakly-nonlinear modelling of curved ducts (Jensen & Brambley 2026, arXiv:2503.11536) to include open ends. We approximate free space by considering the open-ended duct to be enclosed within a much larger hard-walled concentric duct; within the larger duct, the smaller duct exit is modelled as an acoustic discontinuity. Importantly, the superposition principle is unneeded, allowing the model to be applied in the nonlinear regime. The exit condition can be calculated without needing to solve the full problem in either the outer or inner ducts, making it numerically efficient. The exit condition is validated in the linear regime by comparison to Wiener-Hopf solutions of the duct end correction, and a novel nonlinear end correction is proposed; we find that both non-plane waves and nonlinearity cause the end correction to vary significantly from Rayleigh's classical 0.6 radii result. A number of numerical illustrations are then discussed, demonstrating nonlinear effects, sound radiating from curved ducts, sound radiating from an exponential horn (representative of brass instrument bells), and the harmonic effects of the open end on in-duct resonances. The model has potential applications to sound in woodwind and brass instruments. Matlab source code is provided in the supplementary material.

papers.title: Design and Implementation of a 25-Yr Pseudoprospective Earthquake Forecasting Experiment in China (AoyuX)
papers.summary: Forecast models in statistical seismology are commonly evaluated using log-likelihood (LL) scores for the full distribution $P(n)$ of earthquake counts. However, fat tails and out-of-range observations (realized counts exceed all simulations) can bias model rankings. We develop a tail-aware framework that estimates cell-wise $P(n)$ using adaptive Gaussian kernel density estimation and compares three treatments of out-of-range counts: power-law extrapolation, a fixed minimum probability, and exclusion. Using the AoyuX platform, we conduct a 25-year (2000--2023) month-by-month pseudoprospective experiment in the China Seismic Experimental Site. We compare an epidemic-type aftershock sequence model with a homogeneous background, ETAS$\mu$, with a spatially heterogeneous variant, ETAS$\mu(x,y)$, across six spatial resolutions and five magnitude thresholds, using 100,000 simulations per forecast window. Count distributions follow power laws, $P(n) \sim n^{-(1+a)}$, with $a \approx 1.02 \pm 0.23$, yielding a productivity exponent $\alpha = 0.83 \pm 0.19$ for $b = 0.85 \pm 0.002$. Model rankings depend on tail treatment: power-law extrapolation is theoretically justified and empirically most robust, whereas occasional advantages of the fixed-probability approach in coarse, low-magnitude settings are attributable to noise. Cumulative information gain shows that ETAS$\mu(x,y)$ outperforms ETAS$\mu$ in data-rich configurations, especially for $M_t = 3.0$--$3.5$ and whole-region tests. Positive mean information gain is concentrated where earthquakes with $M \geq 5$ occurred, whereas stochastic fluctuations dominate data-poor settings. A coefficient-of-variation analysis distinguishes genuine upward trends from noise. The framework supports statistically grounded evaluation of earthquake forecasting models.

papers.title: Isolating Balanced Ocean Dynamics in SWOT Data
papers.summary: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides two-dimensional sea surface height anomaly (SSHA) maps at unprecedented resolution, but its signal is a combination of balanced meso- and submesoscale turbulence, unbalanced motions such as internal waves, and small-scale noise. Interpreting the meso- and submesoscale flow features captured by SWOT requires careful isolation of the balanced signal. We present a statistical method to do so in regions where internal tides make a negligible contribution to the SSHA signal, such as western boundary current regions and the Southern Ocean. Our method assumes Gaussian statistics as a Bayesian prior for both the balanced flow and the remainder of the signal, and we infer their respective covariance functions by fitting parametric models to the observed SSHA wavenumber spectrum. Using these inferred covariance functions, we perform a Bayesian inversion to produce swath-aligned SSHA maps that isolate the balanced signal and fill the nadir gap. We evaluate the method using synthetic data from a high-resolution simulation with realistic SWOT-like small-scale noise added. Comparisons with the underlying model data show that our inversion successfully removes the unbalanced small-scale signal while preserving meso- and submesoscale eddies, fronts, and filaments down to a spatial feature scale (the inverse angular wavenumber) of about 6 km in the subtropical Northwest Atlantic region used for illustration. This comparison also demonstrates that the posterior uncertainty is a reliable estimate of the error. While our focus is on balanced dynamics, the balanced extraction can be extended to include tides, internal waves, and non-Gaussian priors.

papers.title: Effects of the Coriolis force on the coherent structures in conventionally neutral atmospheric boundary layers
papers.summary: It is well known that the Coriolis force due to Earth's rotation can induce wind veer in the mean flow velocity of an atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), but much less is known about its effects on turbulent coherent structures. In this work, large-eddy simulation (LES) is employed to investigate the effects of the Coriolis force on the characteristics of turbulent coherent structures in the conventionally neutral atmospheric boundary layers (CNBL). Variation of the Coriolis force is realized by changing latitude or geostrophic wind speed. We found that the Coriolis force causes distinct deflection of coherent velocity structures to the geostrophic wind direction, which is not aligned with the direction of either the mean wind or the mean shear. When a relative structure deflection angle is plotted against a relative local wind veer angle, a universal relationship between them can be established regardless of latitude or geostrophic wind speed. Moreover, we also studied the effect of the Coriolis force on the inclination of large-scale turbulent structures. It is found that the inclination angle in the surface layer varies under different conditions, which is probably due to the deflection of turbulent structures caused by the Coriolis force.

papers.title: Inverse-Designed Superchiral Hot Spot in Dielectric Meta-Cavity Toward Ultra-Compact Enantioselective Detection
papers.summary: Chiral nanophotonic structures have garnered considerable interest in recent years due to their potential to enhance the efficacy of chirality-sensitive biomolecular detection. Designing metaplatforms to enhance chiroptical signals under linearly polarized excitation is particularly appealing due to the minimal chiral background and the ease of controlling excitation polarization. Here, a novel two-step inverse design scheme for dielectric lossless metasurfaces with superchiral hot spots is proposed. The method extends the local density of field enhancements for non-chiral fields into the chiral regime and significantly surpasses previous enhancements in superchiral field generation. It has been demonstrated that by leveraging the excitation of high quality factor modes with small mode volumes, it is theoretically possible to convert linearly polarized plane waves into a superchiral hot spot with record-high enhancement in the near-field optical chirality up to 10^4. A prototype is successfully implemented using advanced nanofabrication technologies. The optical characterization of the prototype demonstrates a 10^2-fold enhancement in optical chirality. The findings of this study unveil novel prospects for chiral spectroscopy with ultra-compact devices, underscoring the role of machine learning and physics-based inverse design in the development of cutting-edge, functional photonic structures.

papers.title: Racket Kinematics and Ball Performance During the Forehand Reverse Flick: A Pilot Comparison With the Backhand Flick in Table Tennis
papers.summary: Background Following changes in table tennis ball materials, offensive returns have become more important for initiating sustained topspin offense. However, using the backhand flick (BF) to return forehand short balls often increases the difficulty of recovery and continuity, revealing a technical gap. This study preliminarily verified a novel forehand short return technique, the forehand reverse flick (FRF), and analyzed its similarities and differences with the BF. Methods Four elite athletes completed seven consecutive days of FRF specific training. Infrared motion capture and ultra-high-speed cameras were used to collect data on racket kinematics, movement duration, and ball performance. Results The success rate of the FRF increased steadily, reaching 86%. Racket trajectories of the two techniques were highly similar along the X (r = 1) and Y (r = 0.99) axes but differed along the Z (r = -0.04) axis. Racket and ball velocities were comparable between techniques, whereas the FRF showed lower resultant acceleration (approximately 265.57 m/s) and required about 0.03 s more for movement duration. Ball velocity was comparable between techniques, for the ball spin, the FRF generated lower spin (approximately 76.61 r/s) about 64% of the BF value (approximately 120.13 r/s). The highest participant mean spin rate reached 93 r/s, about 77% of the BF mean. Conclusion Overall, the FRF was found to have favorable learnability and training value, with potential for further optimization and competitive application.

papers.title: Generalized Formulation to Predict Rossiter Modes for Subsonic to Hypersonic Flow
papers.summary: This paper describes the development of a generalized, physics-based theoretical model for estimating Rossiter modes for flow over rectangular cavities for regimes ranging from subsonic to hypersonic without requiring a priori knowledge of the detailed cavity-flow dynamics. This model addresses the issues with the Heller Bliss model, which despite incorporating compressibility effects, shows increasing deviations from experimentally measured Rossiter modes above Mach 3. The proposed model exploits the fact that the acoustic propagation speed governing the Rossiter feedback mechanism depends on the excitation and relaxation of internal energy modes. To account for these effects, an effective temperature is constructed from estimated post-shock conditions and used to evaluate an effective speed of sound, which is then used in the Rossiter relation to calculate the Strouhal number. The Strouhal numbers predicted by the model are compared with available experimental and high-resolution two-dimensional numerical simulations (conducted as a part of this study) from Mach 2 to Mach 9; our results agree very well with these datasets, thus supporting the conclusion that thermodynamic energy-mode participation and relaxation can alter the acoustic feedback timescale governing cavity oscillations. The formulation therefore provides a physics-based estimate of Rossiter-mode frequencies without requiring prior CFD or experimental characterization of the detailed cavity-flow dynamics.

papers.title: A Level Set Method on Particle Flow Maps
papers.summary: Accurate interface tracking is central to numerical simulations involving moving boundaries, including multiphase flows, free-surface dynamics, phase-change problems, and other interface-driven processes in computational mechanics. Although level set methods provide a flexible implicit representation of evolving interfaces, their grid-based advection and reinitialization procedures often introduce numerical diffusion, volume loss, and degradation of thin or highly curved structures. This paper introduces a Particle Flow Map Level Set (PFM-LS) method that addresses these limitations by transporting interface geometry through particle-carried bidirectional flow maps. In contrast to particle level set methods that use particles mainly as corrective markers, PFM-LS uses particles as primary carriers of level-set values, gradients, and Hessians within a narrow band around the interface. The method combines long-range flow-map transport, high-order particle-grid reconstruction, adaptive particle control, and a hybrid particle-grid redistancing scheme to preserve both signed-distance consistency and sub-grid geometric features. Numerical benchmarks in two and three dimensions, including topology-change tests, chamfer and Hausdorff shape-error metrics, and coupling to an incompressible free-surface flow solver, show that PFM-LS achieves strong volume preservation, high shape fidelity, and near fourth-order convergence, outperforming a broad range of existing level set and reference-map-based methods.

papers.title: Stellarator island divertor shape optimization for reduced peak heat fluxes
papers.summary: An automated algorithm to construct island divertors for stellarators is presented and used to find divertors that meet heat load requirements determined by material limits. The algorithm uses just two initial conditions: two starting coordinates on the island separatrix chosen by the user. We leverage the simplicity of the algorithm to explore the divertor parameter space in a fixed magnetic equilibrium. Heat loads are approximated using the field line diffusion model implemented in the \texttt{FLARE} code. Divertor solutions that satisfy heat load requirements while maintaining a high power fraction captured are found using a parameter scan and a Bayesian optimization routine. The optimization finds divertors that perform the same as the parameter scan, but with a 75\% reduction in computational cost. The resulting divertors satisfy heat load requirements across varying cross-field heat diffusivities. Optimization over various islands in the equilibrium shows that it is easiest to find divertors that satisfy heat flux requirements for low-elongation islands. This algorithm presents a simple parameterization for island divertors and facilitates further physics and optimization studies.

papers.title: Temporal patterns of preferences through Wikipedia editing in different languages
papers.summary: Temporal editing patterns on Wikipedia provide a computational lens on cultural dynamics across linguistic communities. We analyse a decade of editorial activity (2001--2010) in eleven Wikipedia language editions and apply hierarchical clustering to two representations of collective behaviour: a static one, based on the thematic composition of each edition, and a temporal one, based on its weekly activity cycle within each thematic category. For the temporal representation we compare two normalisations: one retains only the shape of the weekly cycle, and the other combines it with thematic composition. The linguistic communities exhibit distinct circadian and weekly editing rhythms. Some groupings are recovered by both representations and by both activity metrics (edits and editors), most notably Russian and Chinese, whereas others, such as German and French, emerge only from temporal activity rhythms. Temporal information thus reveals structure that thematic composition alone does not, which points to time as a relevant and often neglected dimension in cross-cultural analyses of digital trace data, and in studies that use online platforms as proxies for collective cultural behaviour.

papers.title: Observational Indistinguishability and the Beginning of the Universe
papers.summary: Can we infer whether all of physical reality began to exist? Several novel results are offered suggesting a negative verdict. First, two necessary (but not necessarily sufficient) conditions are offered for a cosmic beginning. Second, I discuss three theorems which show that, in a wide range of spacetimes, observers cannot infer the global structure of their spacetime; one of the three shows that spacetimes satisfying a condition necessary for a cosmic beginning are observationally indistinguishable from spacetimes which do not satisfy that condition. Next, I offer two extensions to the aforementioned theorems. The two extensions show that, in an equally wide range of spacetimes, observers cannot collect sufficient data to determine whether the application conditions for the class singularity theorems are satisfied or whether their spacetime satisfies the two necessary conditions for a cosmic beginning. Lastly, a reply is offered to the objection that the skeptical consequences of the aforementioned theorems can be overcome with induction. Importantly, all past singular dust FLRW spacetimes are observationally indistinguishable from counterparts which, while sharing a number of important local properties, either do not include a singularity to the past of every point or else do not have the sort of time ordering intuitively required for a cosmic beginning.

papers.title: Enhanced Seismicity Monitoring in the Rapid Scientific Response to the 2025 Santorini Crisis
papers.summary: We used a deep learning workflow to enhance earthquake detection during the 2025 seismic unrest between Santorini and Amorgos islands to track the evolution of the crisis in near real-time. We analysed the continuous seismic waveforms daily (1/2 - 3/3/25) as the crisis unfolded. Our analysis enhanced the earthquake catalogue from around 4,000 to 80,000 earthquakes. The enhanced catalogue allowed this international expert group to identify the volcanic-tectonic character, clearly revealing burst-like, spasmodic seismicity swarms, which is a pattern associated with fluid-driven processes from early stages of the crisis. Detailed moment tensor inversions in early events characterised by a significant non-double couple component indicated the involvement of magmatic or high-pressure hydrothermal fluids driving the unrest. Concurrent DL-enhanced tomography efforts identified a third, deep magmatic reservoir beneath Anydros Islet, consistent with pressure-driven processes. To date, volcanic-tectonic swarms in which >200 earthquakes of ML > 4 occurred within only a few weeks, largely within episodic bursts of seismicity, have not been observed elsewhere.

papers.title: LLM-DR: An On-Demand Delivery Simulation Framework for Studying Heterogeneous Rider Behavior and Collective Mobility with Persona-Grounded Large Language Model Agents
papers.summary: On-demand delivery platforms are computational social systems in which dispatch rules and repeated rider actions jointly shape service and urban mobility. Riders choose whether to reject offers, accept one order, or bundle several orders; assignments then change their availability and other riders' opportunities. Modeling this feedback requires empirical rider heterogeneity, shared-order interaction, and road-network execution to be represented together. Delivery optimization and large language model (LLM) mobility generation provide useful foundations, but leave this combination insufficiently examined. We develop Large Language Models as Delivery Riders (LLM-DR), an agentic simulation framework for benchmarking rider policies under a common order stream and dispatch protocol. Persona-grounded LLM agents provide a reference implementation, using empirical profiles, local observations, short-term memory, and route-tool estimates to propose order actions. The environment resolves assignment conflicts, constructs pickup and drop-off sequences, and executes tool-supported routes. Analysis of 9,025 Beijing orders and a sample of 2,508 routed delivery waves identifies four rider personas. A controlled single-day reconstruction places 60 agents, equally distributed across personas, in an observed stream of 8,656 orders. Persona groups complete 16-30 orders per rider, with average bundle sizes of 1.116-2.212. Distributional comparisons retain several empirical persona orderings in order volume, bundling, and routed-wave distance. Fleet-level outcomes show displaced demand, service-occupancy, and completion peaks, alongside a shared central service core and differentiated spatial reach. These results connect data-derived rider strategies to executable action chains and collective mobility patterns within a shared computational social system.

papers.title: Recognition of Nanoparticle and Microdroplet Parameters in Levitating Microdroplets of Suspension by Speckle Image Analysis Using Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.summary: Retrieving suspension parameters from light scattered by a suspension microdroplet is a difficult inverse problem because the recorded optical pattern is shaped by droplet morphology and by perturbations of the internal optical field introduced by the dispersed phase. Here we demonstrate experimental, data-driven recognition of microdroplet and nanoparticle-suspension parameters from laser speckle images recorded for individual levitated suspension microdroplets. We confined slowly evaporating TiO$_2$ nanoparticle suspensions in diethylene glycol in a linear electrodynamic quadrupole trap and classified their speckle patterns using a convolutional neural network (CNN). The CNN was trained and tested to recognize droplet diameter, nanoparticle mass concentration, and nanoparticle diameter, first separately and then in simultaneous two- and three-parameter tasks. The CNN recognized droplet diameter most robustly, with an estimated accuracy of approximately 6% on independent test data. Nanoparticle concentration required sufficiently separated classes. Nanoparticle-diameter classes were also recognized, although particle-size effects were coupled to changes in particle number at fixed mass concentration. We demonstrated simultaneous three-parameter classification across 27 classes. As an exploratory out-of-distribution test, we applied a CNN trained on single-component suspensions to dual-component suspensions containing two nanoparticle diameters. The CNN retained meaningful predictive capability, especially at higher concentrations, although robust decomposition of mixed nanoparticle populations was not achieved. These results show that speckle images of single levitated suspension microdroplets contain sufficient information for CNN-based multi-parameter recognition and support further development of speckle-based optical diagnostics for complex microdroplet and aerosol-like systems.

papers.title: Mortality of ultra-thin LGADs and PiN diodes from high energy deposition
papers.summary: Low Gain Avalanche Diodes are prime candidates for high-resolution timing applications in High Energy Physics, Nuclear science, and several other fields. Operating these devices in high-radiation environments presents various hazards, including the risk of their permanent degradation or destruction caused by effects such as Single Event Burnout. Studies using minimum ionizing particles found a greatly reduced Single Event Burnout risk by operating below a bias voltage corresponding to an average electric field of 12 V/$\mu$m - however, as high energy particle colliders produce a wide energy spectrum of radiation, it is crucial to understand this phenomenon and other possible damage mechanisms at energy deposition levels greater than those of minimum ionizing particles. This was achieved by pre-irradiating LGADs and PiN diodes with active thicknesses of 20, 30, and 50 $\mu$m up to 1.5 $\times$ 10$^{15}$ $\mathrm{n_{eq}/cm^2}$, and exposing them to beams of protons and heavy ions (C, O, Fe, Au) at the BNL Tandem van de Graaff accelerator. Several mortality categories were observed, defined by different electrical and mechanical damage signatures. This furthers our understanding of permanent radiation damage of silicon devices, crucial towards mitigating Single Event Burnout and other damage mechanisms to safely operate future detectors.

papers.title: Aggregation, breakup, and size-dependent transport in a turbulent channel flow with cohesive particles
papers.summary: Due to attractive inter-particle forces, cohesive particles suspended in turbulence undergo a complex process of aggregation, breakup, and restructuring. Despite a growing body of knowledge on the ``flocculation'' of cohesive granular materials suspended in homogeneous isotropic turbulence, little focus has so far been placed on wall-bounded flows where turbulence and shear are inhomogeneous. This study presents a first investigation of a fully developed wall-bounded flow of resolved cohesive particles. Five direct numerical simulations of turbulent channel flows laden with finite-sized particles at successively increasing cohesive strength are performed. A population balance equation (PBE) framework is used to analyze aggregate dynamics. When integrated over the full domain, the PBE is closed by aggregation and breakup alone. However, this balance is found to not hold locally in the wall-normal direction, where regions of net aggregate production and depletion are identified. This imbalance is shown to be compensated by the size-dependent wall-normal transport of aggregates, revealing a mean circulation: larger aggregates are preferentially produced in the channel center and migrate toward the wall where they break, while smaller aggregates are transported away from the wall, grow, and reenter the cycle.

papers.title: DeepHartree: A Poisson-Coupled Neural Field for One-Shot Density Functional Theory
papers.summary: Density functional theory (DFT) with linear combinations of atomic orbitals (LCAO) is costly because of Coulomb-matrix construction and self-consistent-field (SCF) iterations. We introduce DeepHartree, a Poisson-coupled neural field that connects continuous real-space prediction to LCAO electronic structure. An E(3)-equivariant network predicts the Hartree potential, and the Poisson equation yields the electron density. Atom-centred Gaussian fields resolve near-nuclear structure, and a molecular correction enforces the electron count. Analytical Gaussian integrals and numerical quadrature assemble the Kohn-Sham matrix; one diagonalization yields orbital estimates and a density matrix for energy evaluation and SCF initialization. Mean molecular weighted normalized mean absolute density errors (wNMAEs) are 0.110% for QM9 and 0.199% for VQM24 on PySCF level-0 grids, rising to 1.366% and 2.218% on level-3 grids. Models trained on def2-SVP densities transfer to def2-TZVP and def2-QZVP without retraining, retaining total-energy accuracy and occupied-subspace agreement. A Hybrid method combines finite differences, first-order automatic differentiation, analytical integrals, and multilevel quadrature for near-linear density-matrix construction in alkanes and PEG chains. Excluding grid construction, the density-matrix build for a 1004-atom PEG chain is 8.75-fold faster than full automatic differentiation and 7.34-fold faster than converged GPU4PySCF SCF. Without fine-tuning, the QM9 model achieves a total-energy MAE of 9.437 meV per atom on 1,000 larger OE62 molecules. DeepHartree initialization reduces mean QM9 SCF iterations by 15.3-15.6% across the three basis sets and total SCF time by 12.9% for a 620-atom organic cage, including initialization. These results support continuous electrostatic fields as an accurate, scalable interface between machine learning and LCAO DFT.

papers.title: The rapidly advancing contact line Part-1: Navier slip and microscale inertial effects
papers.summary: Curtain coating, in which a moving plate is coated by a falling liquid sheet, sustains rapidly advancing contact lines at large capillary numbers Ca ~ 1. Steady-state solutions exist up to a critical capillary number, beyond which wetting failure occurs through the entrainment of air bubbles. In the steady regime, experiments report an acceleration of the velocity along the fluid-fluid interface as the contact line is approached, down to a few tens of micrometres, and this observation has been interpreted as evidence against the Navier slip model. Here we show that the observed acceleration is compatible with slip models. We perform two-phase Navier--Stokes Volume-of-Fluid simulations with quadtree adaptive mesh refinement use Navier slip and a fixed contact angle. Although the velocity vanishes at the contact line in the contact-line frame, the experimentally accessible microscale region lies outside the slip region. The local Reynolds number based on the distance from the contact line is order unity in this region, and therefore local inertial effects cannot be neglected. The scaled interfacial velocity is well described by an inertially corrected wedge flow solution whose wedge angle can be chosen as the interfacial angle at the inflection point, with agreement improving as the slip length is reduced. Reducing the slip length also recovers a non-monotonic dependence of the critical capillary number on the feed-flow Reynolds number, beyond which wetting failure occurs. At larger scales, a local Young--Laplace arc describes a finite sessile-drop-like region of the outer heel; this region contracts as the heel is suppressed.

papers.title: High-throughput full-f gyrokinetics of the tokamak boundary
papers.summary: Full-f gyrokinetics of the tokamak boundary have so far been limited to individual, expert-curated cases. We report hundreds of concurrent and unsupervised simulations of the edge and scrape-off layer (SOL) in a geometry based on the Tokamak \`a Configuration Variable (TCV), scanning triangularity, elongation and heating power, each evolving turbulence for more than a millisecond, i.e. about two energy confinement times. Without tuned transport coefficients or experimental inputs, the ensemble reproduces the range of SOL heat-flux decay lengths measured in TCV, as well as the reduced SOL density fluctuations and the improved confinement of negative triangularity. The effect of triangularity on confinement is power dependent. At high power, negative triangularity improves the ion energy confinement by weakening the dominant microinstability rather than by a stronger sheared flow. At low power, positive triangularity flattens the ion temperature profile across the separatrix, which we attribute to a longer distance between the trapped ions and the cold recycling source. Local linear gyrokinetic calculations and the transport coefficients extracted from the turbulent fluxes consistently indicate a trapped-electron-mode regime, in which the conductive heat flux at the separatrix is carried by the electrons and the ion energy transport is convective. This article details the simulation setup, the ensemble statistics and the verification of the results, which are also summarized in a companion Letter.

papers.title: Fast reduction of electron-beam-activated graphene oxide by an infrared laser pulse
papers.summary: Rapid and controllable reduction of graphene oxide (GO) remains a critical challenge for realizing its full technological potential. Here, we report the reduction of GO by a synergistic electron-beam-assisted single-pulse near-infrared (NIR) laser process. We find that the efficiency of 1064-nm laser photoreduction can be dramatically enhanced by prior exposure of the sample to a high-energy electron beam. Time-resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy measured with a dynamic transmission electron microscope (DTEM) is used to quantitatively track the oxygen concentration evolution after subsequent NIR laser pulse irradiation. This finds an oxygen diffusivity for the process of 1.4 +/- 0.3 x 10$^{-9}$ m$^2$/s, which suggests oxygen is released by diffusion through defects and imperfections in the film. Electron beam irradiation is found to change the optical absorptivity of GO in the NIR region, and COMSOL simulations are carried out to estimate the thermal heating cycle resulting from the laser pulse. Structural characterization via selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) find localized restoration of sp$^2$ bonding accompanied by turbostratic disorder in the reduced GO. Together, these results point to a mechanism involving the creation of defects and vacancies produced by electron beam irradiation, which increases the efficiency of NIR light absorption and oxygen diffusion normal to the layers. This study demonstrates the important role of such defects in controlling the photochemistry of GO and its photoreduction kinetics.

papers.title: Optical and magnetic penetration depths under a modified electromagnetic coupling in charged bosonic condensates
papers.summary: We establish the relation between optical condensate spectral weight and static magnetic screening in a proposed effective theory of charged bosonic condensates with an additional diamagnetic coupling. Starting from an explicit Ginzburg--Landau functional, we derive both the London equation and the transverse low-frequency conductivity. At fixed condensate parameter $q^2n_s/m^\ast$, the modified coupling doubles the inverse-square magnetic screening length and the optical condensate weight, giving $\lambda_{\rm mag}=\lambda_{\rm stiff}=\lambda_L/\sqrt{2}$, where $\lambda_L^{-2}=\mu_0q^2n_s/m^\ast$. Their ratio is therefore unity in both the standard and modified local theories: it tests consistency between measurement methods but cannot distinguish the couplings. A structured comparison of published results for Nb, Pb, YBCO, MgB$_2$, and Ba(Fe,Co)$_2$As$_2$ identifies the roles of sample matching, absolute calibration, nonlocality, and spectral-weight extraction. We formulate the requirements for a discriminating absolute-response experiment and discuss a complementary single-particle spectral prediction. The analysis separates experimentally accessible consistency checks from tests requiring independent information about condensate parameters or a different observable.

papers.title: Simulations of Particle-Laden Flows with Large Dispersed-Phase Size Disparities Using Scalable Parallel Adaptive Methods
papers.summary: The numerical simulation of multiphase flows involving dispersed components with large scale disparities, such as the collisions between millimeter-sized bubbles and micron-sized mineral particles in flotation, poses a significant computational challenge. Accurately resolving the thin boundary layers of finite-size objects while tracking massive numbers of small particles within a large turbulent domain is often prohibitively expensive on uniform grids. To address this, we present a parallel scalable computational framework that couples the lattice Boltzmann method with the immersed boundary method on a dynamically adaptive octree grid. A key algorithm is developed for the efficient parallel host-cell searching, which significantly accelerates the tracking of Lagrangian points on distributed unstructured grids. The accuracy and robustness of the code are rigorously validated against canonical benchmarks, including the flow induced by an oscillating cylinder and the sedimentation of a sphere. The framework is applied to the multiscale problem of bubble-particle collisions. In quiescent flow, the simulations accurately capture the hydrodynamic interception mechanism, reproducing the theoretical collision efficiency scaling law proportional to the square of the particle-to-bubble size ratio. Furthermore, the framework is applied to the simulation of fully resolved bubbles interacting with inertial point particles in homogeneous isotropic turbulence.

papers.title: Cathodoluminescence Wavefront Retrieval
papers.summary: Free-electron-based nanoscopy enables the study of optical excitations in materials with deep-subwavelength spatial resolution, with cathodoluminescence (CL) being one of the most useful resulting signals. When combined with an optical collection system, CL measurements can access multidimensional information of light; yet the phase of the emitted optical fields has remained largely elusive. Here, we demonstrate a reference-free phase retrieval approach for far-field CL wavefronts using the Gerchberg-Saxton algorithm implemented with real-space and angular-space CL intensity data. Applying this approach to representative nanostructures, including a planar surface, nanosphere, plasmonic crystal, and nanowire, we reconstruct distinct phase distributions that reveal their underlying radiation mechanisms. This reference-free framework offers a robust and flexible route for retrieving the phase of electron-beam-excited optical fields without relying on a reference wave, making it readily extendable to a wide range of nanostructures.

papers.title: On the Shafranov shift in stellarators
papers.summary: As first shown by Shafranov, toroidal plasmas in magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium tend to expand in major radius when the pressure is increased. Here, an average measure of the resulting Shafranov shift is introduced, and its properties are discussed for various classes of stellarator configurations. It is shown to be particularly small in quasi-helical and quasi-isodynamic stellarators with a large number of field periods, which are thus relatively robust to variations in the plasma pressure.

papers.title: pANO-F12: An atomic natural orbital-inspired route to more compact basis sets for F12 explicitly correlated methods
papers.summary: Explicitly correlated methods such as MP2-F12 and CCSD(F12*) exhibit much faster basis set convergence (asymptotically $\propto L^{-7}$, with L the highest angular momentum) than orbital-only approaches. Yet it has been pointed out that cc-pVnZ-F12 basis sets themselves are substantially larger than the corresponding cc-pVnZ, and specifically that cc-pVDZ-F12 is the size of cc-pVTZ. One way to generate compact basis sets in an orbital-only context are Atomic Natural Orbital (ANO) basis sets [J. Alml\"of and P. R. Taylor, JCP 86, 4070 (1987)]. However, obtaining the required first-order reduced density matrix while properly accounting for the F12 geminal is problematic. In this work, we show that an energy minimization-based contraction process under linear independence constraints yields `pseudo-ANO' (pANO) basis sets that are functionally equivalent in quality. Subsequently, we apply this recipe to obtain pANO-F12 basis sets from the same elements, then validate them for several thermochemical benchmarks and for the hypersensitive out-of-plane vibrations of benzene. We show that, unlike cc-pVnZ-F12, pANO-F12 exhibits the familiar shell structure seen in cc-pVnZ and ANO basis sets, and that pANO-F12 offers a route to more compact F12 basis sets more amenable to medium-sized systems, especially in conjunction with localized pair natural orbital approaches. Overall, the pANO approach is most beneficial for the smaller double-and triple-zeta basis sets, offering either superior performance to cc-pVnZ-F12 at same cost, or similar performance at lower cost.

papers.title: On the Two-Dimensional Structure and Asymmetries of Ionic Liquid Electrospray Plumes
papers.summary: Vacuum electrosprays play important roles in electrospray propulsion, a type of spacecraft electric propulsion wherein charged ions or droplets are accelerated at high velocity to provide spacecraft thrust, and they also have important implications for surface etching and mass spectrometry. Here we present the first fully two-dimensional time-of-flight (TOF) mass spectrometry survey of a vacuum electrospray plume, generated by a tungsten needle externally-wetted with the ionic liquid 1-Ethyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate (EMI-BF$_4$). We find that the plume exhibits clear two-dimensional compositional variation, structure, and asymmetry, with heavy particles and energetic neutrals being more prevalent in the center and a ring-shaped distribution for the monomers (the lightest molecular ions) peaking at 10$^\circ$ off beam-axis with a relative minima in the center. Using a new spatial baseline characterization method, we find a population of energetic neutrals firing 3.4$^\circ$ off beam-axis. In particular, we find that by comparing different parts of the plume, the estimated propulsive efficiency from any one sampled point may vary by as much as a factor of 6. We also find that high mass droplets, which are often assumed as absent in many studies of externally-wetted needles, may carry away significant propellant mass at lower effective velocity and reveal a cone-jet mode of operation at 470 nA output current. We thus find that whole-plume compositional surveys may more accurately assess plume composition and propulsive efficiency, and a significant portion of the `missing mass' in electrospray propulsion sources presumed to be operating in the pure ion regime can be potentially explained by limited sampling of the spatially non-uniform ion plume.

papers.title: Local network evolution rules driving shortest path multiplicity
papers.summary: The shortest path multiplicity, here denoted by $\mu$, is an important metric of complex networks. For real networks $\mu$ is high and it correlates with the network community structure. Since local network evolution induces network communities, it is possible that a high shortest path multiplicity is the natural expectation of local evolution rules. Here I demonstrate, by means of numerical simulations and exact results, that this is indeed the case. For random graphs with arbitrary degree distributions $p_k$, $\langle\mu\rangle\sim \langle k(k-1)\rangle / (\langle k\rangle e)$, growing with the network size when $p_k\sim k^{-\gamma}$ and $\gamma\leq3$. For networks generated by stochastic local rules, $\langle\mu\rangle$ increases with the network size and it does so faster than what is observed in their randomized versions. Furthermore, the number of communities increases with the network size and the correlation with $\langle \mu\rangle$ follows.

papers.title: Nanoscopic Multiplexing Optical Data Storage via Chip Fabrication
papers.summary: The accelerating growth of global data demands storage technologies combining high capacity, long lifetime and low energy consumption. Optical storage is attractive for archival applications, but conventional optical writing is constrained by diffraction-limited resolution and scalability, while thermal accumulation limits high-speed writing. Here we shift optical data writing from a serial optical process to a fabrication-defined process, in which lithographic masks govern where material modification occurs. Using patterned resist masks and ion implantation, we create fluorescent information voxels with nanoscale control over millimeter-scale areas. The platform supports multilevel and multidimensional encoding by independently encoding information in fluorescence intensity and wavelength. A machine-learning-assisted super-resolution reconstruction protocol is developed to recover information beyond conventional optical resolution for information readout. Overall, the framework reaches an areal storage capacity of 1.1 Tbit within the area of a standard 120-mm optical disc, approximately fivefold that of a conventional single-layer Blu-ray disc. This architecture establishes a micro/nanofabrication-compatible route to scalable optical memory and opens a pathway to wafer-scale archival storage.

papers.title: Characterizing the energy resolution of the MicroBooNE LArTPC at the MeV scale using monoenergetic features of $^{208}$Tl decays
papers.summary: A detailed understanding of the capabilities and fidelity of low-energy reconstruction is crucial for taking advantage of MeV-scale neutrino physics opportunities in liquid argon time projection chambers (LArTPCs). This study presents a measurement of the resolution of reconstructed energy in the MicroBooNE LArTPC at $\approx 1.5$ MeV. The characterization is performed using monoenergetic signals generated by $2.614$ MeV $\gamma$-rays from $^{208}$Tl decays undergoing pair production in the detector. The resolution is found to be ($7.52 \pm 0.78 \text{(stat)} \pm 0.92 \text{(syst)}$)%. This value is consistent with the MicroBooNE simulation prediction of ($9.70 \pm 0.65 \text{(stat)}$)% at the $1.6 \sigma$ level. This study represents the first ever measurement of LArTPC energy resolution at the MeV scale and provides a pathway for monoenergetic energy calibrations in future experiments using LArTPC detectors.

papers.title: Wave instabilities in anisotropic regularized Kappa plasmas: New plasma dispersion functions and numerical validation
papers.summary: Plasmas in space and astrophysical environments are frequently found in (quasi-)stationary states not in thermal equilibrium, indicated by velocity distribution functions (VDFs) featuring nonthermal characteristics, such as Lorentzian high-energy tails and kinetic (temperature and strahl/beam) anisotropies. For decades, in-situ observations of electrons and ions in the solar corona, solar wind or planetary magnetospheres have been modelled using so-called Kappa VDFs, whose standard form, however - depending on the considered VDF moment - imposes stringent constraints on the minimum value of the Kappa power-law parameter. Such limitations have posed difficulties on the derivation of a fully-consistent hydrodynamic formulation of suprathermal plasmas. To improve this situation, the recently proposed regularized Kappa VDF avoids strict constraints on the Kappa parameter by introducing an exponential, regularizing cut-off. In this work we assume that the plasma particles are described by regularized-Kappa VDFs that feature anisotropies not only in their thermal velocity spread parameters but also in their exponential cut-offs. The dielectric tensor components for waves propagating along a magnetic field are derived, in terms of new plasma dispersion functions. The resulting dispersion equations are solved with two complementary techniques, namely by using the analytical expressions derived here and by employing the ALPS code. This is done for physical parameters that give rise to electromagnetic and electrostatic instabilities. Both approaches show excellent agreement and the results demonstrate how an anisotropy in the regularizing cut-off of VDFs can serve, depending on an instability's nature, either as a stabilization factor or as an additional free energy source.

papers.title: Multi-pulse accumulation of gas molecular coherence enables gigahertz ultrafast frequency conversion
papers.summary: Frequency conversion of ultrafast lasers is fundamentally constrained by the trade-off between pulse energy and repetition rate. Here, we demonstrate a frequency conversion mechanism in which molecular coherence accumulates across ultrafast pulse trains in gas-filled hollow-core fibers. Unlike conventional nonlinear interactions initiated by individual high-energy pulses, this mechanism relies on the collective buildup of coherent molecular oscillations driven by successive pulses. Using this approach, we achieve Raman frequency conversion at repetition rates up to 3 GHz with nanojoule pulse energies. The results demonstrate that accumulated molecular coherence can govern nonlinear frequency conversion, revealing a domain of light-matter interaction whose physical limits remain largely unexplored.

papers.title: Transferable machine learning of excited-state dynamics with extremal pooling
papers.summary: Photochemical processes govern phenomena ranging from solar energy conversion and atmospheric chemistry to vision and photosynthesis. Accurate simulation of these processes requires modeling excited-state potential energy surfaces, often involving chemical reactions, tasks that remain computationally prohibitive for extended systems and long timescales using traditional \textit{ab initio} methods. Machine learning interatomic potentials have revolutionized ground-state simulations, but their extension to excited states faces fundamental challenges: standard architectures assume energy extensivity, an assumption that fails for excited states. Here, we present a size-intensive machine-learning framework for excited-state dynamics based on \textit{extremal pooling} of predicted atomic HOMO and LUMO contributions. Trained exclusively on excitations energies and forces, the architecture learns interpretable atomic-level contributions that encode physical information on the extent of electron localization. We demonstrate this framework on the photoexcited solvated electron in liquid water, a paradigmatic problem in radiation chemistry leading to competing pathways involving both hydrogen-atom dissociation and proton-coupled electron transfer. The model not only reproduces the relevant chain of reactions and product species that form during excitation, but also allows one to explicitly study the dynamics of the solvated electron in quantitative agreement with previously reported Restricted Open-Shell Kohn-Sham calculations, while enabling excited-state simulations of periodic systems at length and time scales inaccessible to the reference electronic-structure method. This work establishes a general strategy for machine learning-driven excited-state dynamics applicable to diverse photochemical systems, from molecular chromophores in solution to extended condensed-phase systems.

papers.title: Generation of continuous-wave laser light at 148.4 nm using cavity-enhanced second harmonic generation in $BaMgF_4$
papers.summary: The development of a nuclear optical clock based on \textsuperscript{229}Th is expected to influence the next generation of time and frequency standards. At its heart is the need for a continuous wave (CW) at laser at 148.4~nm to drive the clock transition between the ground and excited isomeric state. In this work we experimentally investigate the potential of BaMgF\textsubscript{4} crystals to create a CW solid state laser at the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) wavelength of 148.4~nm via cavity-enhanced second harmonic generation. For this purpose, a BaMgF\textsubscript{4} crystal was grown, optically polished and periodically poled. The crystal was inserted into a power-enhancement cavity, resonant at the fundamental wavelength of 296.8~nm and the generated laser light at 148.4~nm was characterized. Within this proof-of-concept investigation, a VUV output power of typically ($16\pm1$)~pW is obtained. This marks the first time that this type of crystal is used to generate VUV laser light. The experimental findings are compared to theoretical expectations and provide a clear path for future improvements, which could have implications not only for compact laser sources in the VUV but also solid-state as well as single-ion based \textsuperscript{229}Th nuclear clocks.

papers.title: A neural delta-$f$ particle-in-cell method: evolving the background with learned backward flows
papers.summary: We present a novel {\delta}f particle-in-cell (PIC) method for the kinetic simulation of electrostatic plasmas in which the bulk density, acting as a control variate, is evolved using symplectic neural networks (SympNets). The SympNets are used as an approximation of the backward flow and trained using the particle trajectories. We introduce a periodic variant of the SympNet architecture that encodes the spatial periodicity of the problem into the network itself. We validate the approach with numerical results in 1D1V and 3D3V for the Vlasov-Poisson system.

papers.title: Optical Amplification with Large Goos-H$\ddot{a}$nchen Shift Driven by Non-Hermitian Bilayer Meta-Grating Under Lasing State
papers.summary: The coexistence of gain and loss in parity-time symmetric bilayer meta-gratings enables the transformation of bound states in the continuum into a ring of lasing threshold modes. Under lasing state, gain saturation drives the contraction of this mode ring into a single discrete lasing point. Additionally incident weak optical field with frequency and incident angle nearly matched to the lasing mode can obtain amplification accompanied by prominent Goos-H$\ddot{a}$nchen shifts. Specifically, active meta-grating with lasing mode at the $\Gamma$ point induce sizable Goos-H$\ddot{a}$nchen shifts. In contrast, active meta-grating with lasing mode off the $\Gamma$ point induce large Goos-H$\ddot{a}$nchen shifts that are proportional to the quality factor of the effective resonant modes under lasing state. In finite meta-grating, finite-size effects exert distinct influences on the lasing state as well as the Goos-H$\ddot{a}$nchen shifts of the additionally incident optical field: the lasing characteristics and Goos-H$\ddot{a}$nchen shifts of $\Gamma$-point lasing modes remain nearly unaffected, whereas those of off-$\Gamma$ lasing modes are significantly modulated by finite-size perturbations.

papers.title: TD-Link: A Daisy-Chain Optical Architecture for Integrated Data Readout and Deterministic Timing Distribution in Large-Scale Detector Systems
papers.summary: TD-Link is an optical communication architecture that combines high-throughput data readout and sub-nanosecond timing synchronization over a single fiber for large-scale detector systems. It adopts a multidrop daisy-chain ring topology connecting a Data Concentrator to up to sixteen FERS front-end boards per link, with up to eight links per concentrator. Operating at 3.125 Gb/s, TD-Link carries data, synchronization, and control traffic in the same serial stream through a token-based streaming protocol that minimizes per-hop latency and supports on-the-fly payload fragmentation. Deterministic latency is enforced at two levels. On the concentrator, transmitter lanes are aligned by using the half-full flag of the multi-gigabit transceiver (MGT) elastic buffer as a one-bit phase detector: a firmware state machine steps the transmit phase interpolator (PI) until the buffer pointer difference crosses half-depth, locking every lane to the same phase condition. On each front-end board, where the synchronization pulse must also cross from the recovered-clock to the transmit domain, the residual three-to-five-cycle ambiguity of the synchronizer is removed by a calibration-free multiphase oversampling time-to-digital converter (TDC) with 0.8 ns bins, which time-stamps the incoming edge on the transmit time base so that a scheduler regenerates it at a fixed, programmable latency. A Digital Dual Mixer Time Difference (DDMTD) circuit measures the inter-concentrator phase. Tests with CERN PicoTDC-equipped FERS boards show a board-to-board synchronization $\sigma$ of 24 ps on the same ring, 27 ps across transceiver quads, and 28 ps across two cascaded concentrators, against an intrinsic front-end floor of 7 ps. Over more than one thousand cold boots without re-calibration, the boot-to-boot spread of the board-to-board skew stayed below 20 ps, consistent with the 18.6 ps phase-interpolator step.

papers.title: Optomechanical transducers for gigahertz frequency ultrasound imaging
papers.summary: Ultrasound is a noninvasive, real-time, and therefore widely used imaging modality; yet its application in cellular and sub-cellular biology is significantly limited by rapidly increasing acoustic losses in aqueous solutions with decreasing wavelength. Here we introduce a nano-optomechanical cavity transducer platform to generate and detect ultrasound in aqueous solutions with a sub-micron acoustic wavelength. We analyze the full signal pathway through a combination of finite element method modeling and the coupled differential equations that describe the dispersive optomechanical interaction. Our findings project a signal-to-noise ratio in the thousands at ~5 GHz, limited by diffraction losses and thermal-acoustic noise. This work establishes a viable path towards optomechanical ultrasound systems capable of label-free imaging at cellular and sub-cellular length scales while also providing a broader framework for optomechanical crystal device operation in aqueous environments relevant to biochemical sensing, medical diagnostics, underwater acoustic sensing, and nanoscale imaging.

papers.title: The fixed boundary plasma equilibrium basis for a one Gigawatt electric stellarator power plant
papers.summary: A fixed boundary stellarator equilibrium capable of producing 3 GW of fusion power (1 GW-electric) is presented as the design basis for the GIGA fusion power plant being developed by Gauss Fusion GmbH. The stellarator concept provides a steady-state, transient free, low recirculating power approach to a fusion power plant, which builds on 50 years of progress in plasma physics. A set of requirements for a fixed boundary equilibrium were determined through application of 0.5 D modeling. Optimization of a modified Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) equilibrium was performed to achieve these requirements including alpha power confinement greater than $85\%$, neoclassical effective ripple below 0.01, bootstrap current below 50 kA, and reduced turbulent heat fluxes. In order to fix the plasma volume of $1500~m^3$ during optimization, the VMEC code was modified to renormalize the boundary coefficient to the desired plasma volume. The STELLOPT stellarator optimization code was modified as well to include new bootstrap current targets, a new target for the radial electric field, and the capability to hold the magnetic field on axis at a fixed value. An intermediary conceptual design plasma and final evolved fixed boundary equilibria are compared to the original modified W7-X equilibrium. The final evolved equilibrium is shown to achieve all the necessary requirements for the GIGA fusion power plant through more detailed modeling of stability, fast ion confinement, and transport.

papers.title: Orientation Dynamics of Rigid Fibers in a Microfluidic Burgers-like Vortex
papers.summary: Fiber suspensions are common in biological and environmental flows and are widely used in industrial applications. Fiber transport and orientation dynamics are affected by interactions with the surrounding fluid and strongly depend on the nature of the flow. The complexity of realistic flows, which are often heterogeneous or time-dependent, hinders a full understanding of fiber dynamics. In this study, we combine microfluidic experiments, theory and numerical simulations to investigate the orientation dynamics of rigid neutrally buoyant fibers in a well-controlled model system, a streamwise stationary vortex at moderate Reynolds number. Despite the three-dimensional nature of the flow, the orientation dynamics are remarkably simple: the fiber orientation is accurately described by Jeffery equations coupled with the Burgers-vortex model over a large range of particle Reynolds number. We show that fibers undergo uniform precession about the vortex axis driven by fluid vorticity while simultaneously aligning with the latter due to strain in the vortex core. These two motions are decoupled, with the alignment timescale determined by the local strain rate and the fiber aspect ratio. Finite particle size and inertia induce weak deviations from the base flow streamlines while leaving the orientational dynamics largely unaffected. These results establish a simple framework for understanding the behavior of elongated particles in stretched vortex flows, which constitute key building blocks of turbulence.

papers.title: Continuous 3-D Latent Diffusion for Medical Image Generation and Reconstruction
papers.summary: High-resolution three-dimensional (3-D) medical latent diffusion remains limited by the cost of decoding full volumes, which existing latent autoencoders (AEs) handle through overlapping sub-volume decoding. We propose a continuous 3-D latent diffusion model framework for computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) generation and measurement-guided reconstruction, built on a coordinate-rendering autoencoder (CoRe-AE). Its decoder applies its convolutional stage once on the compact latent grid and renders voxel intensities from spatial coordinates through a lightweight implicit head, evaluated in memory-bounded chunks. This design avoids overlapping sub-volumes and remains differentiable with respect to the latent, so that the decoder can be used inside measurement-guided reconstruction. The framework was evaluated on CT volumes of 512\textsuperscript{3} voxels and MRI volumes of 256\textsuperscript{3} voxels. At 512\textsuperscript{3}, the decoder was 4--18 times faster than the MAISI and 3D MedDiffusion AEs and required the lowest peak graphics processing unit (GPU) memory, including when its gradient was computed. CoRe-AE also achieved the highest peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) among the evaluated AEs on both modalities. The resulting frozen 3-D latent prior generated full volumes without patch seams and, without retraining, reconstructed sparse-view CT and accelerated MRI through hard data consistency, within 2.4--4.9 dB PSNR of the pixel-domain decomposed diffusion sampler (DDS). A single volumetric latent prior thus supports both generation and reconstruction of high-resolution medical volumes on one GPU. Our code will be made available at https://github.com/Mellak/continuous-3d-latent-diffusion/.

papers.title: Ambient Pressure-Driven Actuators and Shape-Morphing Metamaterials
papers.summary: Actuators which change shape in response to ambient pressure have great potential for use in extreme environments, from space to the deep ocean. Bi-layer actuators have so far not been explored to this end, despite their lightness and mechanical simplicity (there is no requirement for a separate power source or pump, for example) making them ideal for applications where transport and maintenance are difficult. In this paper, foam-based bilayer actuators powered by ambient pressure change have been constructed, modelled mathematically, characterised in terms of their actuating force, and built into deployable devices and metamaterial structures to showcase properties such as negative pressure expansivity. Actuators such as these are ideally suited for a range of applications, from deploying solar panels and sensors in space and extra-terrestrial atmospheres, to under-sea expandable structures and sensing.

papers.title: From risk to flourishing: Seeds for responding to a complex world
papers.summary: Complex risk arises when interacting hazards, infrastructures, ecological systems, institutions, and human behaviors produce nonlinear impacts that cannot be inferred from any component in isolation. We call the study of these dynamics complex risk science. Flourishing is the actualization of all beings toward their good--individually and collectively--answering the question of `how do we live well with and for each other?'. In science as in society, the tendency to reduce, segregate, specialize, and settle has precluded embracing the concept of flourishing as a guiding principle. We describe how complex risk science reframes risk science research so that it can promote the flourishing of socio-ecological-technological systems, and explore how its practice may point society toward a more flourishing future. Our exploration mirrors the unsettled and searching nature of flourishing: examine ideologies traditionally believed to be rigidly in opposition and consider what emerges in the space(s) and conversation between them. We call this a dialectical approach: not a means of resolving contradiction, but a practice of sustaining it, so that systems, and our understanding of them, remain capable of reframing as conditions change. Within this dialectical paradigm, we revisit longstanding tensions in risk science: physical|social, determinism|uncertainty, and contextuality|generality. Examining the conversation among these tensions reveals five seeds that are dispositions for practicing complex risk science: interdependence, responsivity, participation, pluralism, and ongoingness. They can support any scientific endeavor to embrace complexity and promote flourishing. Practicing these seeds at scale will depend on institutional reform: creating collectives toward complex risk science, supporting them with skillfully governed commons, and centering care in our research and evaluation.

papers.title: Breathing chimera states from purely triadic interactions
papers.summary: Chimera states, characterized by the coexistence of synchronized and desynchronized dynamics in identical oscillators, are typically studied in systems with pairwise interactions. Recent studies have shown that purely higher-order interactions can support chimera states. Here, we show that breathing chimera states arise in a model governed solely by a triadic phase interaction, whose intrinsic $\pi$-symmetry permits bimodal phase distributions. We construct a bimodal Ott-Antonsen reduction that incorporates an asymmetry parameter via prescribed asymmetric initial conditions, thereby achieving an exact low-dimensional description of the macroscopic dynamics. This allows us to derive an analytic condition for the emergence of chimera states and identify a bifurcation to a breathing chimera regime characterized by persistent oscillations. Furthermore, the reduced dynamics can be expressed as a Riccati-type equation, providing a geometric interpretation of the chimera state as a closed periodic orbit in the complex plane. Our results establish purely triadic coupling as a minimal higher-order mechanism for chimera formation and provide a tractable framework for studying symmetry-broken collective dynamics in systems dominated by many-body interactions.

papers.title: An Adaptive Approach for Modeling Collisionless Plasma Shocks and Ion Heating in the Shock Frame
papers.summary: We present a novel computational method for hybrid (kinetic ions, quasi-neutral fluid electrons) simulations of non-relativistic magnetized collisionless plasma shocks, observed near the Sun, in the solar system, and beyond. This Adaptive Frame-Of-Reference Approach (AFORA) enables simulations of shocks in their co-moving frames of reference, where shock evolution remains quasi-steady for quasi-stationary upstream conditions, in contrast to moving shocks. We demonstrate our method in two spatial dimensions for a range of angles between the background magnetic field and the shock normal (obliquities). Shock-frame simulations, conducted with a time-adaptive hybrid code, HYPERS, are shown to self-consistently capture upstream and downstream magnetic fluctuations commonly observed by spacecraft at interplanetary shocks and Earth's bow shock. These fluctuations, which may be crucial for estimating the efficiency of ion acceleration at heliospheric and astrophysical shocks, are notably missing from many hybrid simulations of shocks, unless upstream external turbulence is imposed. The quasi-stationary behavior of numerical shocks in the shock frame is confirmed in a series of animations and by demonstrating converged ion energy spectra in the downstream region. Our approach underscores computationally efficient and physically more accurate modeling of shock-driven turbulence, downstream plasma relaxation, and concomitant ion heating in the shock frame. The new method can be used for exploring ion relaxation at interplanetary (IP) shocks, more efficient studies of cosmic rays (CRs) and plasma turbulence, and more accurate predictions of seed populations of Solar Energetic Particles (SEPs) at heliospheric shocks driven by coronal mass ejections (CMEs).
