In the magnetic case, there are no loop contributions to the Green functions of the elementary fields --i.e., Green functions not involving composite operators-- and the only connected parts of such Green functions with a dependence on the coupling constant are the tree level contributions to the three and four point functions of the field $\xi_i$. We also show that in the magnetic case the Green functions involving only Wilson loops are trivial and not so in the electric case.

papers.title: Imaginary HTEE: Probing Criticality and Coherence
papers.summary: We study the imaginary part of the holographic timelike entanglement entropy (HTEE) in a charged asymptotically AdS$_5$ black-hole background whose dual field theory exhibits a critical point in the presence of a chemical potential $\mu$ and temperature $T$. Identifying the imaginary part of the HTEE with the imaginary part of the pseudoentropy, we derive an analytical expression for this quantity and investigate its behavior on the stable and unstable thermodynamic branches. We find that the imaginary HTEE vanishes in the uncharged limit and is induced entirely by a nonzero chemical potential, signaling the emergence of quantum coherence between the initial and final states. As the dimensionless ratio $\mu/T$ approaches its critical value, we obtain an inverse-square-root divergence in the derivative of the imaginary HTEE and extract the critical exponent $\theta_I = 1/2$ analytically. We further show that the same exponent governs the temperature response at fixed chemical potential. Our results establish the imaginary part of the HTEE as a non-local quantum-information probe of criticality in strongly coupled systems, and they imply that the initial and final states become maximally coherent at the critical point.

papers.title: Late-time electric screening in dS from EAdS loops
papers.summary: We compute the one-loop gauge-field two-point functions analytically in scalar QED on dS$_{d+1}$ for general dimension and scalar mass, using the EAdS reformulation of the in-in formalism arXiv:2007.09993. The Dirichlet EAdS gauge field acquires a Schwinger-type mass, with its longitudinal mode supplied by a composite of charged scalars obeying opposite boundary conditions, while the Neumann mode remains protected by gauge invariance. In dS, the Dirichlet correction induces an anomalous dimension $\gamma_J$ for the boundary current and modifies the late-time falloff of the electric field. This bulk calculation reproduces the boundary multiplet-recombination result of arXiv:2509.18888. Summing over the in-in contour branches gives the retarded dS bubble kernel, making direct contact with the Bros-Moschella framework. We establish a spectral Cutkosky rule that expresses the discontinuity of this kernel across the principal-series cut in the Casimir plane in terms of a two-particle cut, with both internal scalar lines placed on shell. Although the full bubble coefficient involves a ${}_7F_6$ hypergeometric function, the cut collapses to a closed product of Gamma functions and determines the complete non-local part of the kernel through a dispersion relation. Analytic continuation of the same cut reproduces the complete one-loop result for $\gamma_J$. In the complex Casimir plane, the loop-corrected Dirichlet photon appears as a pole on the second sheet and is therefore naturally interpreted as a dS resonance, or quasinormal mode, whose frequency is shifted at one loop.

papers.title: Ultralight scalars and invisible gravitons

papers.title: Categorifying Quantum Spin Systems
papers.summary: We develop a homotopical framework for understanding the space of quantum spin systems based on topological $n$-nets, which assign associative unital algebras to local regions in an $n$-dimensional space in a manner that captures the locality structure of the underlying lattice theories. Moreover, the nets of greatest physical interest form a Karoubi-complete subcategory that shares many of the characteristic structural features of the category of finite TQFTs. papers.title: A Witten effect for global monopoles

The same group theory condition that allows the operator also guarantees the existence of monopoles. We also give a fermionic UV completion and determine the coefficient by matching the Goldstone-Wilczek current.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Interpretation of the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event: A Minimal $U(1)_B$ Dark Sector and Its Experimental Tests
papers.summary: The $248$ keV nuclear-recoil candidate reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation, in which scattering converts the DM particle into a slightly heavier state. We provide a comprehensive study of this interpretation in an anomaly-free model of gauged baryon number, where a new vector boson, $Z_B$, mediates interactions between DM and quarks. Breaking the baryonic gauge symmetry generates the new particle masses and a small splitting between two DM states, while a residual symmetry keeps the lighter state stable. We identify regions compatible with the LZ candidate, the observed DM abundance, and current ATLAS and CMS dijet constraints. Within the scanned domain, these regions span DM masses $m_\chi\simeq0.19$-$4.5$ TeV, mediator masses $M_{Z_B}\simeq0.05$-$5.0$ TeV, and gauge couplings $g_B\simeq0.004$-$0.74$, with correlated values of these parameters. A representative thermal solution has $m_\chi=1$ TeV, $M_{Z_B}=1.44$ TeV, $g_B\simeq0.228$, and a mass splitting of $300$ keV. A small electroweak mixing allows the heavier DM state to decay rapidly, suppressing unwanted signals from its surviving population. This interpretation can be tested through complementary measurements: additional LZ and XENONnT data can establish whether the high-energy recoil signal persists, ATLAS and CMS Run-3 dijet searches can probe the mediator mass and coupling, and a dedicated IceCube analysis of four-quark final states can test DM capture and annihilation in the Sun. Together, these measurements can test complementary parts of the surviving region and assess whether the LZ candidate is consistent with this interpretation.

papers.title: Non-Stationary Wormholes and Matter Source Reconstruction in General Relativity
papers.summary: We investigate non-stationary wormhole geometries in General Relativity embedded in evolving cosmological backgrounds. We employ a Simpson-Visser-like regularization of the temporal coordinate of the $(n+1)$-dimensional FLRW metric, together with a homogeneous Cuscuton field, to construct cosmological backgrounds in which the scale factor remains finite and non-zero at the would-be initial singularity. We then consider two specific dynamical wormhole geometries: the four-dimensional defect wormhole and the topologically charged Perry-Mann type wormhole. We show that the former can be supported by a canonical scalar field with vanishing potential, while the latter requires a mimetic matter sector to support its spatial structure, with the Cuscuton governing the cosmological evolution in both cases. We subsequently generalize the analysis to a separable non-stationary spacetime and derive a scaling condition that strongly constrains the admissible matter sources. In particular, for minimally coupled scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics fields, this condition removes the functional freedom available in static reconstruction schemes. We show that, within this framework, regular, asymptotically flat wormhole geometries cannot be obtained while simultaneously satisfying the required smoothness and reflection symmetry conditions. Our results illustrate both the possibility of constructing specific non-stationary wormholes in regular cosmological backgrounds and the restrictions that arise when attempting to generalize such constructions to arbitrary spatial geometries.

Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. papers.title: Quantum Energy Inequalities with a twist: rotating frames along stationary worldlines
papers.summary: The energy densities of the quantised scalar and electromagnetic fields need not be positive, but their averages along timelike worldlines are constrained by Quantum Energy Inequalities (QEIs) that hold in flat and curved spacetimes for arbitrary Hadamard quantum field states. However the general QEI bound is not easy to compute in closed form. Here, we compute closed form expressions for the massless scalar and electromagnetic fields along stationary worldlines in Minkowski spacetime. These worldlines are solutions to the four-dimensional Frenet-Serret equations with constant curvature invariants and include inertial, uniformly linearly accelerated, and uniformly rotating worldlines as special cases. The QEI bound depends on a choice of tetrad along the worldline, and we compute it for any tetrad with constant angular velocity relative to the Frenet-Serret tetrad. Optimising over the angular velocity, we show that the tightest electromagnetic QEI bound occurs when the tetrad is invariant under Fermi-Walker tetrads. Surprisingly, the Fermi-Walker tetrad does not produce the tightest QEI bound for massless scalar fields, and we investigate the optimal bound both analytically and numerically. Our results and methodology significantly improve on those in [CJ Fewster & J Thompson, Class. Quantum Grav. 40 (2023) 175008], in which only Frenet-Serret tetrads were considered for massless scalar fields.

papers.title: Cosmology & Astrophysics of the Dark Dimension with Bulk Majorana Neutrinos
papers.summary: Recently, the possibility of having sterile Majorana neutrinos charged under $B-L$ gauge symmetry in the bulk of the dark dimension has been explored. If the mass of the bulk neutrino is at the lower end of this bound, it can potentially also explain the recently observed Fermi halo excess on gamma rays through the evaporation of long-lived 5d (i.e. dark) black holes through Hawking radiation to bulk neutrinos, which promptly decay into standard model particles.

papers.title: Primordial Graviton Entanglement in Quasicrystalline Inflation
papers.summary: We study the entanglement structure of gravitons in quasicrystalline inflation. Both parity-even and parity-odd interactions generate graviton pairs with nonzero total momentum. For opposite-helicity pairs with identical momenta, the parity-even contribution can be nonzero, whereas the parity-odd contribution vanishes. The transition from inflation to radiation domination produces additional conventional two-mode squeezing. We derive the resulting normal and anomalous covariances. The initially nonzero reciprocal blocks of the full field-momentum covariance remain nonzero under homogeneous evolution, although individual components can vanish. We show that this homogeneous, helicity-preserving evolution acts unitarily within each helicity sector and therefore preserves the entanglement between the complete right- and left-helicity sectors. Nevertheless, it can eliminate entanglement in the reduced state of a co-propagating pair. We illustrate this distinction using a solvable four-mode model.

papers.title: Modular $S_4$ Inverse Seesaw at the LZ High-Recoil Frontier
papers.summary: The extension of the LUX--ZEPLIN nuclear-recoil analysis to approximately $270\,\mathrm{keV}$ probes a qualitatively new dark-matter regime in which endothermic scattering can suppress conventional low-energy recoils and concentrate the surviving spectrum near the Galactic high-velocity tail. We construct a modular-$S_4$ realization in which a minimal $2N_R+2S$ inverse seesaw accounts for lepton flavor, while a separate pair of Standard-Model-singlet fermions forms the pseudo-Dirac state relevant for high-recoil xenon scattering. The sectors share a common complex modulus $\tau$, so the modular forms selected by charged-lepton and neutrino data also enter the operators generating the dark Dirac mass and Majorana splitting. Our scan yields $181447$ lepton-sector solutions satisfying $\chi^2_{\ell+\nu}<30$, distributed among several disconnected modular regions, and predicts one effectively massless light neutrino at leading order. Restoring the physical scales allows TeV-scale heavy quasi-Dirac neutral fermions with small non-unitarity. We subsequently scan $2\times10^6$ dark-sector points only over flavor-accepted values of $\tau$ and identify common-modulus solutions in the LZ-oriented region $300\,\mathrm{GeV}\le m_\chi\le2\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and $300\,\mathrm{keV}\le\delta\le400\,\mathrm{keV}$. An exploratory two-bin Poisson likelihood, including endothermic xenon kinematics, the Helm form factor, Standard-Halo-Model velocities, Gaussian energy smearing, and profiling over the signal normalization, gives a best grid point at $(m_\chi,\delta)\simeq(1.847\,\mathrm{TeV},371.5\,\mathrm{keV})$, close to the terrestrial inelastic kinematic ceiling. The construction provides a direct link between modular lepton flavor, TeV-scale inverse-seesaw dynamics, and high-recoil inelastic dark matter.

papers.title: Dynamical chiral symmetry breaking in rotating QED$_3$: critical flavor number and the occupation-reweighting channel
papers.summary: We study dynamical chiral symmetry breaking in $(2{+}1)$-dimensional QED on a rigidly rotating disc, $\Omega R<1$, within the rainbow Schwinger--Dyson framework. At zero temperature the rotation response of the condensate vanishes identically, so $N_c^{\rm SD}(\Omega,T{=}0)=N_c^{\rm SD}(0)=2.60\pm0.01$ (using three operational definitions). At finite temperature, rotation suppresses the condensate through a dominant occupation-reweighting channel, $\hat{\kappa}_{\rm occ}=-1.55$, accounting for $\ge 99.995\%$ of the linearized total response at the reference parameters, with self-consistent feedback amplifying it by $26.5$. The screening channel is reported at fixed regularization, $\hat{\kappa}_{\rm scr}(\varepsilon = 0.01)=-0.97$; its $\varepsilon \to 0$ behavior is logarithmically divergent. The crossover flavor $N^{*}(\Omega)$ falls monotonically at fixed temperature (a corollary). The critical flavor number is unchanged by rotation at $T=0$ (theorem). Together these results set the finite-temperature reference for the model.

papers.title: Axionic Casimir Torque
papers.summary: In the canonical Casimir effect, the quantum vacuum is isotropic, and the minimization of vacuum energy drives only a linear attractive force between the plates. However, the introduction of an axion gradient breaks this rotational symmetry. It can be demonstrated that these asymmetric zero-point fluctuations exert a macroscopic mechanical twist on the plates proportional to $\vec{b}^2 \sin (2\vartheta)$ where $\vec{b}$ is the spatial axion gradient and $\vartheta$ is the angle between the axion gradient and the normal to the plates.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium framework for first-order phase transitions
papers.summary: The first-order phase transition is central to electroweak baryogenesis and gravitational wave generation, yet thermal equilibrium effective potential analyses cannot describe the real-time non-equilibrium dynamics of the phase transition process. We use the Schwinger-Keldysh closed-time-path formalism of real-time finite-temperature field theory to study these effects. For the $\phi^6$ model, we derive the effective action and the corresponding Langevin equation. We further extend the formalism to the two scalar fields case, obtaining the coupled Langevin equations. These results provide a theoretical framework for the bubble nucleation simulation of the non-equilibrium phase transition process, laying the foundation for reliable predictions of baryogenesis and gravitational wave signals.

papers.title: Entanglement and parametric resonance in coupled oscillator systems
papers.summary: We study a system of two quadratically-coupled harmonic oscillators, prepared respectively in the ground state and in a coherent state. This toy model can describe for instance the dynamics of one mode of a quantum field evolving in a harmonically-oscillating classical background. In such situations, it is well-known that, depending on the background oscillation amplitude and coupling strength, the system may exhibit parametric resonance. Using the Feynman-Vernon influence functional, we analyze the interplay between parametric resonance and quantum entanglement by perturbatively computing the purity of the mixed state resulting from tracing over one of the oscillators. We find a runaway behavior of the quantum entanglement between the two oscillators, as well as a rapid breakdown of the validity of perturbation theory, in regions of parametric instability. This provides a quantitative confirmation of various statements in the literature and is highly relevant to questions pertaining to the validity of the semiclassical approximation in coupled quantum-classical systems.

papers.title: Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO--supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt
papers.summary: Recent measurements from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) have reported a moderate preference for dynamical dark energy, challenging the standard $\Lambda$CDM paradigm. Nonetheless, such a trend could reflect a tension between the shape and the offset of the Hubble diagrams predicted by current BAO and Type Ia supernovae (SN) data, which may underpin a possible breakdown of the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR) linking luminosity distances $D_{\rm L}$ and angular-diameter distances $D_{\rm A}$. We explore this possibility by parametrizing deviations from this relation as $\eta(z) \equiv D_{\rm L} / [{(1+z)}^2 D_{\rm A}] = \alpha{(1+z)}^\varepsilon$, and investigate how the preference for a Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) dynamical dark energy is modified once $\varepsilon \!\neq\! 0$ is allowed. Using DESI DR2 and uncalibrated SN data (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, Union3, and Union3.1), we find that allowing $\varepsilon$ to vary freely in both $\Lambda$CDM and CPL reduces the CPL preference with respect to $\Lambda$CDM by a larger amount than the addition of spatial curvature $\Omega_k$; only Union3.1 exhibits comparable reductions. We also find that the preference reduction is robust to alternative $\eta(z)$ parametrizations, and that the $\eta(z)$ constraints remain stable under the removal of BAO tracers or low-redshift cutoffs for Pantheon$+$, whereas the DES-Dovekie preference largely disappears once $z < 0.1$ SN are removed. In a separate calibrated analysis, illustrative Planck sound-horizon and SH0ES absolute-magnitude priors give $\alpha \simeq 0.942 \pm 0.014$, quantifying the normalization mismatch under those assumptions. We also map the CDDR violation onto photon-loss and varying-$G$ scenarios, concluding that the cosmological constraints are much weaker than existing constraints on these physical mechanisms.

papers.title: Conserved-charge diffusion in hot and dense QCD matter
papers.summary: We study the coupled diffusion of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness in hot and dense quark matter using a three-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model with self-consistently generated constituent quark masses. The complete diffusion matrix is evaluated within a relaxation-time kinetic approach, including its diagonal and off-diagonal components. We find that the off-diagonal transport coefficients exhibit distinct temperature and baryon-chemical-potential dependence associated with the flavor-dependent composition of the charge carriers. We further investigate generalized charge diffusivities and mobilities obtained from the corresponding susceptibilities. At finite baryon chemical potential, the baryon and strangeness mobility scales cross, reflecting the different density dependence of their transport coefficients and susceptibilities. The results provide model benchmarks for coupled conserved-charge transport in baryon-rich QCD matter.

papers.title: Where is the conformal coupling in Palatini gravity?
papers.summary: We study the conformal coupling in the torsion-free Palatini formulation with an ordinary scalar kinetic term. Tuning the curvature coupling cannot restore Weyl invariance in a Palatini theory with an ordinary scalar kinetic term because, for an independent and inert connection, the scalar-curvature term is separately Weyl-invariant, and no finite curvature coupling cancels the Weyl variation of the kinetic term. This can be demonstrated by evaluating the energy-momentum trace on the scalar equation of motion and noting that it is explicitly independent of the Palatini coupling. Eliminating the connection, we construct a map between the curvature coupling and the effective coupling for the equivalent metric theory, and demonstrate that the scalar continues to propagate even if the reduced kinetic coefficient vanishes. We also show that it becomes a Weyl compensator with a scale-invariant potential only in the rescaled infinite-coupling limit, which in four dimensions is directly related to Palatini ${\cal R}^2$ gravity. We calculate the running of the couplings at one loop, and we find that the conformal shift in the metric-curvature coupling's beta function generates a metric-curvature coupling on a fixed metric-affine background, whereas the independent-curvature coupling runs homogeneously. Furthermore, we follow an alternate prescription in which the connection is allowed to respond to the scalar fluctuations, which results in a different scalar Hessian and therefore different beta functions. Nonetheless, we find that both prescriptions admit the formal infrared limit $(\xi_{eff},\lambda_{eff})\to(1/6,0)$ through different limits of the original couplings in the case of positive perturbative quartics. Finally, we note that trajectories starting on the positive gravitational branch encounter a vanishing gravitational coefficient at a finite scale before this endpoint.

papers.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
papers.summary: We develop a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), connecting microscopic dark-sector physics to nonlinear structure formation. We systematize particle-physics ingredients of representative SIDM models and map microscopic parameters and interactions onto structure-formation simulation inputs. These include internal-state populations and reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, inelastic and dissipative energy exchange, decay rates and recoil kinematics, and modifications to cosmological initial conditions. The numerical framework builds on the efficient, scalable SIDM infrastructure introduced in our companion work for the moving-mesh code AREPO-2, providing substantial performance gains over AREPO-1. We implement isotropic and anisotropic self-scattering with constant or velocity-dependent cross sections, multi-state and inelastic reactions, and dissipative scattering, complemented by a dedicated dark-matter decay module. For strongly forward-peaked interactions, the anisotropic hybrid SIDM scheme combines frequent small-angle drag-diffusion with explicit rare large-angle scattering, achieving speed-ups of up to $\sim100\times$ relative to fully anisotropic Monte Carlo in the tested configurations. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection experiments, thermalization and uniform-box decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. These tests recover analytical predictions, establish consistency between equivalent numerical treatments, and reproduce published inelastic and dissipative SIDM benchmarks. The resulting modular framework connects dark-sector models to nonlinear astrophysical predictions, enabling exploration of microscopic interactions beyond standard isotropic, elastic SIDM.

papers.title: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
papers.summary: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that bound sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band, beam-beam hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming such limitation. Driven by modest jet misalignments ($\theta_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 6^\circ$), co-streaming proton beams collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ - six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in a strictly optically thin regime ($\tau_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary PeV-EeV neutrinos and sub-TeV $\gamma$-rays fall directly within reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.

papers.title: Vanishing Love Numbers of Kerr-Newman Black Holes
papers.summary: Tidal Love numbers characterize the conservative response of compact objects to external perturbations and provide a powerful probe of their nature. While the static Love numbers of Schwarzschild, Kerr, and Reissner--Nordstr\"om black holes remarkably vanish, the tidal response of a generic Kerr--Newman black hole has remained unexplored due to the intrinsic coupling between gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations. Exploiting a recent breakthrough in the separability of these perturbations, we analytically determine the static tidal response of the most general stationary black hole in four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory. For arbitrary multipole order, charge, and spin, we show that the entire matrix of conservative Love numbers vanishes, including the mixed gravito-electromagnetic couplings. We also compute the nonvanishing static dissipative response induced by frame dragging.

papers.title: Revisiting Critical Higgs Inflation: Electroweak Couplings, CMB Observables, and Perturbative Unitarity
papers.summary: We revisit the scenario of critical Higgs inflation, in which inflation is driven by the Standard Model Higgs boson with parameters chosen close to a critical point, giving rise to an inflection point in its potential. After reviewing this model, we perform a systematic study of its viability centered around three criteria: (1) consistency with electroweak-scale measurements, (2) ability to reproduce the cosmic microwave background (CMB) observables, and (3) sensitivity of the model predictions to unknown UV physics, based on a breakdown of perturbative unitarity. We first show that compliance with electroweak-scale measurements is controlled by the parameters in the Higgs potential at inflationary scales, also updating the literature values. We then demonstrate how for any choice of potential parameters, agreement with the CMB observables can be achieved through the choice of the nonminimal coupling, in both metric and Palatini formulations of gravity. However, we also find that there exist no regions of parameter space, in either the metric or Palatini formulations, in which compliance with all three physical criteria is possible. While this does not exclude the possibility of the Higgs field driving inflation, it means that predictions for any observable are in principle sensitive to the details of the model's UV completion.

papers.title: What Do Event Generators Compute? Flux Functionals from Detector Operators
papers.summary: Every physical prediction of an event generator is a statement about the hadronic fluxes that can be recorded by particle detectors. By contrast, the formal backbone of modern event-generator precision is provided by the unobservable partonic final states of the parton shower, with hadronisation included as a model. We construct the probability distribution of the hadronic fluxes non-perturbatively, directly from detector operators acting on asymptotic hadronic states, and encode it in an event generator source functional. This distribution contains every measurement a detector can make, and is therefore what a generator must compute with precision, including the effects of hadronisation. Restricting the functional to the energy flow yields the parton shower source functional, which is infrared and collinear safe and contains every calorimetric observable, making it a natural object against which to assess parton-shower accuracy. We compute its logarithmic structure at one loop in $e^+e^-$ annihilation, finding it directly sensitive to kinematic recoil and hence to the recoil scheme of a parton shower. The parton shower functional depends on a continuum of low scales, one for each resolved direction, and in a toy model its logarithms cannot be entirely resummed within a factorisation whose evolution derives only from the high-scale physics. Our operator-based formulation opens the door to the study of event-generator-like systems in theories beyond QCD, including conformal theories such as $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory, and thereby offers a new route to non-perturbative insight into event generation.

papers.title: Internal Nucleon Properties and the Equation of State of Ultra-Dense Matter
papers.summary: The question of the link between the nucleon properties and the equation of state of ultra-dense matter, both being composed of quarks and gluons, is investigated by adopting a soliton model to describe internal nucleon properties and a direct mapping between nucleon and quark matter to obtain the equation of state of ultra-dense matter. We compare $\pi+\omega$ and $\pi+\omega+\rho$ soliton models and analyze the presence of a pressure singularity at the nucleon center due to the $\rho$ field. This singularity impacts the equation of state in ultra-dense matter. Only the pressure derived from the canonical energy-momentum tensor has a singularity, while the Belinfante pseudo-gauge transformation of the energy-momentum tensor generates an internal pressure without a singularity. We then investigate predictions for the equation of state of ultra-dense matter based on different prescriptions for the nucleon pressure. It is shown that none of the prescriptions agree with the thermodynamical pressure defined in uniform matter. The mismatch between any equation of state and the thermodynamical one questions the simplicity of the direct mapping between finite-size nucleon properties and uniform matter as well as the role of the nucleon surface in the internal energy density and the pressure.

papers.title: Signature of GW from the Hidden Sector in light of the Recent LZ Event
papers.summary: The LZ collaboration has recently reported a single nuclear-recoil event at $E_R=248\pm23_\text{stat}\pm23_\text{sys}$ keV, observed in a 2.84 tonne-year exposure with a local significance of $3.4\sigma$, pointing towards an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation. The symmetry-breaking scale thus provides a multi-messenger probe connecting terrestrial direct-detection kinematics at the LZ and early-universe FOPT thermodynamics while obtaining thermal DM relic abundance. We delineate the viable parameter space compatible with the LZ event, correct relic density, and detectable GW signals in the low frequency regimes at future interferometers like $\mu {\rm ARES}$ and THEIA while satisfying existing cosmological, astrophysical, and terrestrial bounds.

papers.title: Linear Response to Black Hole Deformations
papers.summary: Modifications of gravity beyond (vacuum) General Relativity have a subtle impact on the physics around black holes. Describing these effects across different observables is, however, a priori strongly model dependent. While effective descriptions of the geometry allow to efficiently capture deviations from benchmark predictions, they sometimes lack a clear passage towards (effective) new physics. Inspired by linear response theory, in this work I therefore propose a formalism that allows to calculate leading corrections of observables relative to the Schwarzschild black hole anywhere in space-time (outside of the horizon): the order of corrections is fixed through an eigenvalue $\mathcal{E}$ of the Einstein tensor, which is identified with an external energy momentum tensor that generates the deformation of the geometry. In this ways, $\mathcal{E}$ can be linked to effective physics models. Focusing on spherically symmetric and static black holes, I illustrate the approach at the hand of a number of observables in the vicinity of the horizon, such as characteristic quantities of particles moving around the black hole (e.g. the black hole shadow or the radius of the innermost stable circular orbit) or the spectrum of scalar quasi-normal modes. Reversing the logic, I argue that the knowledge of such observables provides non-trivial constraints on $\mathcal{E}$, which in turn grant insights into the effective physics in the vicinity of the black hole.

papers.title: Plasmon modes in triple-point semimetal, its quadratic cousin, and Hopf semimetal
papers.summary: We study collective charge excitations in pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals within the random-phase approximation, considering both the linearised model with a flat-band and its quadratic-corrected counterpart. The quadratic correction renders the flat-band dispersive and endows it with a Fermi surface, thereby affecting the overall response. Comparisons with Weyl and Hopf semimetals reveal how bandstructure and quantum geometry jointly govern collective charge dynamics. While the Drude weights are determined by the Fermi surface and band-velocities, interband screening, plasmon dispersion, and Friedel oscillations reflect the quantum geometry of the eigenstates.

papers.title: Okubo algebras and Exceptional Periodicity: tetracode gradings, root-lattice obstructions and Clifford cones
papers.summary: The Okubo algebra brings together ternary gradings, integral root frames and rank-three geometry. We examine how these structures extend to the complex Exceptional Periodicity algebras. With $N=4(n+1)$, a tetracode character gives eight nonzero homogeneous components of dimension $t_n=8n+3+2^{4n}$. On a tip, a compatible grading has zero component of dimension $8n-5$ and eight nonzero components of dimension $1+2^{4n-3}$. The arithmetic behaves differently: for $n\geq2$, the lattice $D_N^+$ has no full-rank orthogonal frame of unscaled $A_2$ lattices. We exhibit failures of the Jacobi and Jordan identities and determine the derivations and full automorphism group of the ambient algebra above level one. We also give a Clifford-module proof, with the normalization fixed by root products, of the published realization of EP tips as special Vinberg $H$-algebras. This identifies a positive real form and yields explicit formulas for its cone, cubic, Cholesky coordinates and rational dual invariant. The cone is symmetric exactly at $n=1$. Its determinant-one hypersurface belongs to the known $L(8n,1,0)$ series, whose $r$- and $c$-maps give homogeneous scalar manifolds for supergravity theories with eight real supercharges.

papers.title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
papers.summary: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $\beta$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.

papers.title: Exact two-loop gravitational tail integrals and their ultraviolet-infrared structure
papers.summary: Gravitational tail-of-tail corrections arise when radiation scatters twice from the mass-monopole field of its source. In the multipolar effective field theory, one of the two-loop topologies contributing to this process involves genuinely coupled loop momenta, preventing its evaluation through nested one-loop integrations. After tensor reduction, this nonfactorizing structure leads to a particularly challenging family of scalar integrals with unbounded numerator powers as the multipole rank increases. We derive exact closed-form expressions for the entire relevant integer numerator domain, valid in generic dimension and accommodating Feynman, retarded, and advanced prescriptions through consistent analytic continuation. Near $d=3+\epsilon$, we also obtain explicit Laurent expansions through $O(\epsilon)$, retaining the subleading information needed in higher-order radiative calculations. While these expansions determine the dimensional poles, identifying their ultraviolet (UV) or infrared (IR) origin requires a separate analysis of momentum regions. We carry out this analysis throughout the integral domain and apply it directly to the coupled tail-of-tail emission diagram for arbitrary electric and magnetic multipoles. In this way, we independently determine the UV and IR residues, and explicitly verify that the complete infrared pole structure, including both double and simple poles, agrees with the exponentiation of the one-loop gravitational tail. The UV residues, calculated directly from hard-momentum regions, reproduce the established multipole anomalous dimensions when combined with the known contributions of the remaining diagrams.

papers.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
papers.summary: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product K\"ahler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $\psi=Bz$ and $\phi=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.

papers.title: Scale-separated AdS$_3$ vacua from $G_2$-orientifolds using bispinors
papers.summary: In this paper, minimal supersymmetric AdS$_3$ solutions on $G_2$-orientifolds of type IIA and IIB supergravity are studied. These are obtained by techniques of the bispinor formalism. A straightforward argument is derived against AdS$_3$ solutions in massless type IIA string theory on such $G_2$-backgrounds. Furthermore, it is shown that some of the AdS$_3$ solutions in massive type IIA do admit a separation of scales, whereas the same cannot be said for the type IIB vacua. Finally, a formula for the 3d superpotential in the bispinor language is given that is valid for both type IIA and type IIB configurations. It is shown that the supersymmetry conditions of this superpotential lead back to the bispinor equations.

papers.title: Rational Q-systems at Root of Unity I. Closed Chains
papers.summary: The solution of Bethe ansatz equations for XXZ spin chain with the parameter $q$ being a root of unity is infamously subtle. In this work, we develop the rational $Q$-system for this case, which offers a systematic way to find all physical solutions of the Bethe ansatz equations at root of unity. The construction contains two parts. In the first part, we impose additional constraints to the rational $Q$-system. These constraints eliminate the so-called Fabricius-McCoy (FM) string solutions, yielding all primitive solutions. In the second part, we give a simple procedure to construct the descendant tower of any given primitive state. The primitive solutions together with their descendant towers constitute the complete Hilbert space. We test our proposal by extensive numerical checks and apply it to compute the torus partition function of the 6-vertex model at root of unity.

papers.summary: We investigate the twist-3 generalized parton distributions (GPDs) for the valence quarks of the proton within the basis light-front quantization (BLFQ) framework. Using the LFWFs we then calculate the twist-3 GPDs via the overlap representation. By taking the forward limit, we also get the twist-3 parton distribution functions (PDFs), and discuss their properties. Our prediction for the twist-3 scalar PDF agrees well with the CLAS experimental extractions.

papers.title: Fusion rules and structure constants of E-series minimal models
papers.summary: In the ADE classification of Virasoro minimal models, the E-series is the sparsest: their central charges $c=1-6\frac{(p-q)^2}{pq}$ are not dense in the half-line $c\in (-\infty,1)$, due to $q=12,18,30$ taking only 3 values -- the Coxeter numbers of $E_6, E_7, E_8$. The E-series is also the least well understood, with few known results beyond the spectrum. Here, we use a semi-analytic bootstrap approach for numerically computing 4-point correlation functions. We deduce non-chiral fusion rules, i.e. which 3-point structure constants vanish. These vanishings can be explained by constraints from null vectors, interchiral symmetry, simple currents, extended symmetries, permutations, and parity, except in one case for $q=30$. We conjecture that structure constants are given by a universal expression built from the double Gamma function, times polynomial functions of $\cos(\pi\frac{p}{q})$ with values in $\mathbb{Q}\big(\cos(\frac{\pi}{q})\big)$, which we work out explicitly for $q=12$. We speculate on generalizing E-series minimal models to generic integer values of $q$, and recovering loop CFTs as $p,q\to \infty$.

papers.title: New Crosscap States
papers.summary: We investigate crosscap states in two-dimensional rational conformal field theories (RCFTs), with an emphasis on the role of non-invertible symmetries. In particular, we argue for the existence of crosscap states labelled by each Verlinde line in the RCFT, extending previous constructions involving simple currents. Evidence for the existence of these new states is obtained by deriving a generalized Cardy condition incorporating both crosscaps and topological defects, which we check in some concrete examples. Finally, we briefly discuss how these crosscap states transform under the action of Verlinde lines, as well as the connection to mixed anomalies between parity and internal symmetries.

papers.title: SymTFT Entanglement and Holographic (Non)-Factorization
papers.summary: Given two otherwise decoupled $D$-dimensional CFTs which possess a common (finite) symmetry subcategory, one can consider entangled boundary states of their $(D+1)$-dimensional SymTFTs. This roughly corresponds to performing a gauging of the tensor product of two CFTs, and we call this phenomena ``SymTFT entanglement" (or ``S-entanglement" for short). In the case when these CFTs have semiclassical holographic duals, the S-entanglement relates the bulk gauge charges between two otherwise disconnected AdS spacetimes as we highlight in several top-down examples. We show that taking partial traces of such S-entangled states leads to a streamlined approach to preparing ensemble-averaged CFTs in string theory. This ensemble averaging coincides with that generated by $\alpha$-states in the baby universe Hilbert space, and we propose a symmetry-enriched generalization of this Hilbert space via generalized global symmetries. We quantify how this symmetry-governed averaging violates holographic factorization and leads to the emergence of bulk global symmetries. We also consider the eternal (two-sided) AdS black hole geometries, where our SymTFT entanglement considerations imply that there exist refinements of the usual theromofield double state preparation of the system. We show that one may prepare the system in such a way that the total CFT data does not factorize into left and right copies. As anticipated by Marolf and Wall \cite{Marolf:2012xe}, we highlight that such considerations are necessary to define the gauge charges of eternal black holes, and in certain cases, can imply that there exist extended bulk objects stretching across the wormhole which cannot be expressed in terms of a product of left and right CFT operators.

papers.title: Groupoid Representation of Lorentz Transformations Including Superluminal Observers
papers.summary: We construct a Minkowski-pointed Poincare groupoid that extends the geometric description of Lorentz transformations to frames superluminal relative to a distinguished rest frame. Real four-dimensional superluminal boost matrices factorize into ordinary Lorentz boosts and finite infinite-speed limits. For each spatial direction, the two oriented limits define arrows between the Minkowski metric object and a directional metric object; their composition yields an involutive isotropy loop generating a direction-dependent extension of the Poincare group. These arrows induce *-isomorphisms of Poincare observable algebras, transporting generators and their tensor products. Since all metric objects share a common affine spacetime and dual momentum space, transported spectral data can be classified relative to the distinguished Minkowski metric. This Minkowski-pointed classification recovers ordinary massive and massless Wigner sectors and assigns spacelike orbits, with SO(2,1) little groups, to massive momentum representatives transported to directional objects. It thus provides a geometric interpretation of tachyonic Wigner wavefunction classes without postulating intrinsically tachyonic states. As a kinematic application, we examine polarized cobalt-60 beta decay. Under an explicit source-arrow correspondence, reversal of nuclear polarization exchanges oriented arrows and reverses the preferred momentum direction, consistently with the observed reversal of the Wu counting asymmetry. The measured angular law is compatible with this correspondence; a derivation of decay amplitudes and asymmetry coefficients remains open.

papers.title: Timelike Holographic Complexity
papers.summary: Motivated by the pseudo-entropy program, we study timelike subregion complexity within the holographic Complexity=Volume framework, extending previous spatial constructions to Lorentzian boundary intervals. For hyperbolic timelike regions in pure AdS, we compute the enclosed bulk volume and show that, despite the Lorentzian embedding, the resulting complexity is purely real under the stated volume prescription. We generalize the analysis to AdS black brane geometries, where the extremal-surface configurations considered may either remain outside the horizon or penetrate it, with the horizon-to-turning-point segment being timelike in the exterior case and spacelike in the interior case. In both configurations, the complexity exhibits the same leading UV-divergence structure as the spacelike case and receives no imaginary contribution when the horizon terms are combined with a common regulator. This reality contrasts with the potentially complex-valued pseudo-entropy and reflects the chosen Lorentzian volume prescription, while a precise boundary interpretation of the proposed complexity remains conjectural.

papers.title: A Master Superspace Action for 3D S-Duality
papers.summary: We formulate a `master' partition function in three-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ superspace that realises, upon integrating out complementary superfields, both the electric Maxwell--Chern--Simons (MCS) theory and its magnetic $S$-dual: a non-gauge Deser--Jackiw self-dual massive vector times a decoupled level-$k$ Chern--Simons term. The two descriptions share the topological mass $M=\frac{g^{2}k}{2\pi}$ and obey an exact partition-function identity $\mathcal Z_{\rm mag}(g_m^2,k)=\mathcal Z_{\rm ele}(g_e^2,k)$ with $g_e g_m=2\pi$, mapping a weakly coupled MCS theory to a strongly coupled Deser--Jackiw CS theory. Special limits reproduce pure Chern--Simons/Gaiotto--Witten ($g^{2}=0$) and Maxwell/compact-scalar duality ($k=0$). We extend the construction to a non-Abelian U$(N)$ gauge group obtaining $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills--Chern--Simons on the electric side and a massive non-gauge vector coupled to level-$k$ Chern--Simons on the magnetic side; the interaction terms between the massive vector and the Chern-Simons term vanish in the Abelian case. Decomposing the $\mathcal N=2$ vector into an $\mathcal N=1$ vector and a real-linear multiplet factorises the master action and yields the $\mathcal N=1$ counterparts. This uplifts the bosonic duality formulated recently to $\mathcal N=2$ and clarifies its non-Abelian and $\mathcal N=1$ reductions.

papers.title: Holographic Codes from Enriched Link Entanglement in Spin Networks
papers.summary: We introduce an enriched entanglement structure for spin networks, inspired by tensor-network constructions, in which internal links can carry a controlled and discrete amount of entanglement. In the spin-network picture, vertices are dual to simplices (more generally, to polyhedra) and links are dual to their faces. Standard spin-network gluing corresponds to fully identifying two simplices along a face, implemented by a maximally entangled, gauge-invariant singlet state on the corresponding link, while unglued faces correspond to links carrying no entanglement. Working on a complete graph, we promote this binary choice to a controlled and tunable structure by allowing each link to carry a variable amount of entanglement, interpolating between product states and the fully entangled singlet. The additional link variables therefore control not only the amount of entanglement but also the extent to which gauge invariance at internal links is preserved or broken, admitting an interpretation in terms of emergent edge-mode-like degrees of freedom. Within this framework, spin-network contraction defines a bulk-to-boundary map from link-entanglement data to boundary states. Adapting techniques developed in random tensor networks, we show that in a suitable large-spin regime the map is a co-isometry in expectation value, meaning that its adjoint preserves boundary inner products on average, up to the overall scale. Restricting to a code subspace defined by configurations in which links are either effectively glued or open, with small fluctuations around this pattern, the map becomes an isometry up to corrections that vanish in the large-spin limit. This yields a discrete and geometrically meaningful realization of holographic and error-correcting features within the spin-network Hilbert space.

papers.title: Axion Wormholes and the AdS/CFT Factorization Problem
papers.summary: This work investigates the relevance of Euclidean and complex axion wormholes to the AdS/CFT factorization problem. We use a framework that defines bulk gravitational path integrals by integrating over a real Lorentz-signature contour and then, as needed, perhaps further analytically continuing the resulting functions of boundary conditions. For technical reasons we focus on the case of 2+1 bulk dimensions. The AdS boundary conditions (in any dimension) require us to impose Dirichlet boundary conditions on the standard Euclidean axion $\chi_E$. Fixing its asymptotic values on two boundary spheres to $\pm \chi_{E,\infty}$, we find such wormholes to be subdominant to a UV-sensitive endpoint contribution for $\chi_{E, \infty}$ near the real axis, and that (with our conventions) they become dominant only for $\chi_{E, \infty}$ near the negative imgainary axis. Furthermore, such wormholes are irrelevant to our computation for ${\rm Im} \chi_{E, \infty} >0$ (in the sense that the associated ascent contour fails to intersect the contour of integration). The relevance of the wormhole saddle for real positive $\chi_{E, \infty}$ is in fact a matter of choice, as the saddle then lies on a Stokes' line at which the relevant intersection number changes from zero to one.

papers.title: Symmetric Gapped States and Symmetry-Enforced Gaplessness in 3-dimensions
papers.summary: We establish a comprehensive framework for characterizing the infrared (IR) phases of a fermionic quantum theory in three spatial dimensions, based on its quantum anomalies associated with a finite symmetry. We uncover a fundamental dichotomy among these anomalies: the first class of anomalies can always be realized by symmetric gapped states, while the second class can never be realized by gapped states without breaking the given symmetry, establishing the phenomenon of symmetry-enforced gaplessness in these settings. Moreover, using the construction of symmetry extension, we construct the candidate gapped states that theories with the first class of anomalies can flow to in the IR. As an application, we provide concrete predictions of the candidate IR phases of (3+1)-dimensional gauge theories based on our results. Our results also suggest that systems with discrete chiral anomalies cannot be gapped out by adding arbitrary bosonic degrees of freedom.

papers.title: The Generalized Dirac Oscillator in Doubly Special Relativity: A Complexified Morse Interaction
papers.summary: We study the one-dimensional Generalized Dirac Oscillator (GDO) under Doubly Special Relativity (DSR) kinematics. The GDO extends the Dirac oscillator by replacing the linear non-minimal coupling with a general interaction function $f(x)$, thereby generating broad families of exactly solvable relativistic models and, for suitable complex choices of $f(x)$, entering the domain of $\eta$-pseudo-Hermitian and $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric dynamics with real spectra. We present a review of the factorization (supersymmetric) structure that decouples the GDO into partner Schr\"odinger-like Hamiltonians, and we clarify how pseudo-Hermiticity and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry provide consistent inner products and reality conditions for the spatial spectrum. We then embed these results into two representative DSR prescriptions: the Magueijo--Smolin (MS) and the Amelino--Camelia (AC) frameworks. In this approach, the spatial problem yields a real set $\{\epsilon_n\}$, while DSR deforms the algebraic reconstruction map between $\epsilon_n$ and the relativistic energies $E_n$. The MS model induces a branch-asymmetric deformation through an energy-dependent effective mass, whereas the AC model introduces a characteristic criticality through a momentum-sector deformation, resulting in an admissibility requirement of the form $\epsilon_n<4k^2$ in the leading-order realization adopted here. As an explicit illustration, we treat a pseudo-Hermitian complexified Morse interaction, discuss the interplay between the intrinsic Morse finiteness of bound states and DSR-induced truncations, and analyze the massless limit ($m=0$), where MS collapses to the undeformed energy map while AC remains deformed.

papers.title: One-loop mass corrections and decay widths of Type II heavy string states
papers.summary: We approach a systematic investigation of the one-loop mass corrections to (super-)string massive higher-spin states. While the imaginary part of the relevant amplitudes is finite, being related to the width of the decay of the states into two lower-mass states at tree level, the real part is generally IR-divergent and needs regularization and renormalization. We mostly focus on states of the first Regge trajectory in the NS-NS sector of Type-II string theories. We explicitly derive a closed-form expression for the integral over the insertion point, relying on properties of elliptic functions and lattice sums. We then regularize the IR divergent integral over the modular parameter of the torus, applying the $i\varepsilon$-prescription in string theory. As a result we compute the desired mass corrections up to level $N = 10$ and analyze their behavior at increasing $N$. Finally, we speculate on the existence of mixing among lower-spin states and conjecture that the one-loop mass matrix be governed by some random matrix theory.

papers.title: Kinematic Flow for Banana Loops and Unparticles
papers.summary: We extend kinematic flow to a class of momentum-integrated loop-level cosmological correlators: banana loops of conformally coupled scalars in power-law cosmologies and, in de Sitter, banana loops containing arbitrary mixtures of massless and conformally coupled scalars. The corresponding basis is constructed from tubings of marked graphs and is distinguished by the appearance of nested tubes and an arborescence ordering of the vertices. We derive the connection matrices from four combinatorial rules---activation, merger, swap, and copy. The last two are unique to unparticle exchanges: they induce richer mixing among basis functions and introduce new kinematic letters. Our framework extends systematically to arbitrarily complicated configurations, including necklace diagrams, and establishes unparticle exchange as a distinct class of kinematic flow.

papers.title: Couch-Torrence conformal inversion, supersymmetry and conserved charges for D3-branes
papers.summary: An asymptotically flat spacetime in $D=4$ can be mapped via Couch-Torrence conformal inversion to the geometry around an extremal non-expanding and non-rotating horizon. At the linearized level, an infinite tower of conserved Newman-Penrose charges can be found at null-infinity, while infinitely many Aretakis charges are conserved in the near-horizon. Couch-Torrence inversion allows one to establish a matching between the two sets of asymptotic charges. In this work we construct the Newman-Penrose and Aretakis scalar charges in higher-dimensional geometries of D3-branes in $D=10$ and D3-brane bound states in $D=4$ and $D=5$ and establish a precise matching between them through the inversion. By exploiting the residual unbroken supersymmetry of Type IIB supergravity, we demonstrate that it is possible to relate scalar (complex dilaton) charges to higher spin charges. In particular, we determine infinite towers of conserved asymptotic spinorial charges associated with the dilatino fluctuations, and determine the map through inversion.

papers.title: The Hagedorn Temperature as a Nonequilibrium Dynamical Bottleneck in String Thermodynamics
papers.summary: We revisit the Hagedorn regime of string theory from a nonequilibrium perspective using Steepest-Entropy-Ascent Quantum Thermodynamics (SEAQT), which formulates thermodynamic evolution directly on the state manifold without requiring a globally well-defined canonical ensemble. Treating the inverse temperature as an instantaneous, state-dependent quantity, we derive its exact scalar evolution equation, governed in the commuting limit by higher-order fluctuation moments. In an open-system extension we prove that the inverse-temperature mobility equals unity identically on the quasi-canonical family: a divergent Hagedorn variance is necessary but not sufficient for slowing-down, and a reservoir coupled democratically to the whole spectrum drives the system across the Hagedorn scale unimpeded. Slowing-down requires instead a hierarchy of injection rates, in which direct production of highly excited strings by the reservoir is slow compared with a cascade through light quasi-particle modes. The mobility then collapses to a floor set by the ratio of the two rates, the intensive variable is pinned near the Hagedorn scale, and energy condenses into the long-string sector at a finite rate; the pinning is a long-lived transient of computable duration. Promoting the Hagedorn scale to a moduli-dependent quantity along emergent-string limits yields a finite critical distance $\Delta_*$ at which the thermodynamic inertia diverges as $(\Delta_*-\Delta)^{a-3}$ for $1<a<3$, and beyond which pinning can activate. Since Kaluza--Klein towers admit no such divergence, this provides a thermodynamic discriminant between emergent-string and decompactification limits.

papers.title: A general proof of integer R\'enyi QNEC
papers.summary: We prove the R\'{e}nyi quantum null energy condition for every integer R\'{e}nyi order $n\geq2$. In local Poincar\'e-invariant quantum field theory, this states that the sandwiched R\'{e}nyi divergence (SRD) of an excited state relative to the vacuum is convex along a future-directed null deformation. We assume that the deformation is realized by the canonical translations of a half-sided modular inclusion and that the divergence is finite for the initial, undeformed algebra. The proof establishes convexity of the SRD along the induced positive contraction semigroup on Haagerup $L^n(M)$, for every non-zero positive initial element. We also establish a R\'enyi ant formula at every even integer order and, under an additional regularity assumption, at odd integer orders. The R\'enyi ant formula identifies the negative first null derivative of SRD with a multiple of the infimum of the canonical null-translation energy over vector purifications of an escort state constructed from the excited state and the vacuum.

papers.title: A fluid dual to the charged large $D$ membrane paradigm
papers.summary: According to the formulation of the charged large $D$ membrane paradigm, an arbitrary dynamic black hole solution to a theory of gravity with a $U(1)$ gauge field is dual to the dynamics of a membrane in a non-gravitational background. This membrane is endowed with a stress-energy tensor and a charge current, whose conservation equations govern its dynamics. In this work, we demonstrate that the dynamics of these membrane configurations (at the leading nontrivial order in $1/D$) can be mapped to a relativistic charged fluid, establishing a correspondence for asymptotically flat black holes with a particular class of fluid systems. Unlike the standard AdS/Hydrodynamics correspondence, this dual fluid does not reside on an asymptotic boundary, but is localised strictly on the non-gravitational membrane worldvolume. By evaluating the system in both the Eckart and Landau frames, we systematically extract the out-of-equilibrium transport coefficients. We find that the fluid is governed by a negative effective thermal conductivity and a negative heat capacity. This mechanism provides a hydrodynamic interpretation of thermodynamic stability, effectively translating the previously established quasinormal mode damping of the large-$D$ Reissner-Nordstr\"om geometry into the language of fluid dynamics.

papers.title: Exact Holographic Kinematics in AdS/CFT
papers.summary: We propose that holography contains an exact kinematic sector distinct from holographic dynamics. The appropriate setting for this sector is a CFT on an open solid torus in the Weyl frame. The open solid torus introduces an intrinsic scale, and the Weyl frame makes this scale manifest as an extra bulk direction. The resulting bulk-boundary pairs are exact and finite: no cutoff, large-$N$ limit, strong-coupling assumption, or heavy-operator approximation is required. The AdS geometry appearing in this sector should be understood as a kinematic geometry; only in special CFTs and appropriate limits is it promoted to a dynamical semiclassical bulk. The standard boundary-anchored dictionary entries are recovered only as singular limits. As a striking demonstration, we show that Weyl-frame two-point functions provide a replica-free definition of entanglement entropy.

papers.title: From Trees to All Loops: The Combinatorial Geometry of Two-Site Cosmological Wavefunctions
papers.summary: We prove, at arbitrary loop order and including arbitrary tadpole decorations, the shifted-tree decomposition of two-site cosmological wavefunction coefficients proposed in our previous work, and uncover the combinatorial and geometric structure underlying it. For conformally coupled scalars with polynomial interactions, this decomposition expresses each loop coefficient as a finite signed sum of tree coefficients evaluated at shifted energies. For bubble-like graphs, the alternating sum over a Boolean lattice can be written in terms of finite differences or maximal chains. We prove the maximal-chain identity algebraically by induction on loop order and geometrically by decomposing a cubical Laplace integral into simplices. The maximal chains correspond to permutohedron vertices, whose incident facets encode the chain-dependent divisors. For tadpole-decorated graphs, the finite-difference Leibniz rule gives an explicit expansion indexed by ordered partitions and local maximal chains, which glue into global maximal chains and organize the coefficient as a combinatorial "path integral". A natural ordering of the divisors yields a term-by-term match with graph tubings and completes the all-loop proof, while other orderings give alternative tubing representations of the same coefficient. These identities hold before spatial loop-momentum integration and extend to power-law FRW backgrounds by linearity of the twisted integral. Two-site loop coefficients can therefore be obtained directly from known tree coefficients without solving new loop-level differential systems.

papers.title: Black holes with quantum corrections in $3d$: The case of Page curve in Lindblad, greybody factor, and Lyapunov exponent
papers.summary: In this work, first we discuss black holes with quantum corrections as an open quantum system and apply Lindblad formalism to explain the ``zig-zag" behavior in the Hawking- Page curve and radiation process, specially by considering the effects of exceptional points. Then, we calculate quantum corrections for various parameters of $3d$ Cotler-Jensen theory which is $\text{AdS}_3$ with reparametrized modes. At each step of the calculations, we compare the results with the case of JT. We then calculate quantum-corrected greybody factor for various black hole solutions, and specially for the case of Cotler-Jensen theory. Finally, we study the effects of quantum corrections on Lyapunov exponent, potential, and quantum information structure of black holes.

papers.title: A class of half-BPS boundary conditions for $A_{K-1}$ circular quivers
papers.summary: We study a string-motivated class of $\tfrac12$-BPS boundary conditions for 4d $\mathcal N=2$ $A_{K-1}$ circular quiver gauge theories with gauge group $SU(N)^K$, engineered by D4-branes suspended between NS5-branes on a circle. For D4-branes ending on a boundary D6-brane sent to infinity, a single-pole ansatz reduces the BPS equations to a constrained algebraic problem. We characterize the structure of its solutions, which exhibit a winding phenomenon with no analogue for linear quivers, and solve several cases explicitly in closed form. A brane-duality argument suggests looking for the S-dual of the pure Neumann boundary condition within this class. We show that the residual gauge symmetry can be discrete only under a condition fixed by tracelessness, in which case it is the centre $\mathbb Z_N$, and that solutions with this property exist for every $N$ and $K$.

papers.title: Non-linear evolution of five-dimensional black strings in effective field theory
papers.summary: We use numerical relativity to study the non-linear instability of five-dimensional black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity. Black strings evolve into a series of black holes joined by thinner string-like segments, but key features of the dynamics depend on the sign of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. For positive coupling, favored by UV considerations, the growth of curvature invariants is limited within the validity of effective field theory (EFT), suggesting a mechanism for restoring weak cosmic censorship. For negative coupling this cap is absent and curvatures may grow until the EFT breaks down.

papers.title: Holographic heavy quark potential, free energy, and running coupling in backgrounds with broken translational symmetry: Separating finite density from momentum relaxation
papers.summary: We study heavy quark observables, namely the static interquark potential, the thermal free energy, and the running coupling, in a five dimensional asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime with broken translational symmetry. The Einstein-Maxwell-axion (EMa) geometry contains two independent scales: the chemical potential $\mu$, which controls finite baryon density, and the translational symmetry breaking parameter $\beta$, which controls momentum relaxation. Using high precision numerical calculations at finite temperature and at zero temperature, we show that both scales weaken color interactions and promote quarkonium dissociation in a strongly coupled quark gluon plasma, although the underlying mechanisms differ. The chemical potential dominates color screening and strongly modifies the heavy quark potential and running coupling, whereas $\beta$ mainly changes the plasma entropy and therefore gives the leading correction to the thermal free energy. At zero temperature, thermal contributions vanish and the renormalized free energy reduces to a static potential modified by the medium, with an approximately Coulombic form. At all temperatures, a finite baryon density suppresses the binding of quark antiquark ($Q\bar{Q}$) pairs much more strongly than momentum relaxation. We extract the color screening length and dissociation scale, and discuss implications for quarkonium production in heavy ion collisions. These results show that static color interactions and thermodynamic observables are controlled by different medium scales, which offers a unified picture of heavy quark probes in dense dissipative plasmas.

papers.title: When does a state-dependent proto-area define a bulk geometry?
papers.summary: A holographic code assigns a state-dependent entropy remainder to every boundary region, but such remainders need not be the extremal lengths of any one bulk metric. We study this common-source question for the proto-area of a calibrated recovery, the entropy of a boundary region minus that of the matter recovered from it. At zeroth order the reference values must match the lengths of one reference geometry in a fixed renormalization scheme, and this matching also determines the entropy-to-length factor. On a graph with a fixed minimum-cut chamber the data derivatives must lie in the image of the cut-incidence matrix, whose left null vectors are witnesses. On the hyperbolic disk the first variation of renormalized length is the rank-two geodesic X-ray transform, with closed range in an adapted data space, and the geodesic displacement, fixed by a forced Jacobi equation, enters at second order. The resulting normal Hessian gives a gauge-invariant criterion, necessary and sufficient, for a regular pair of response coefficients to come from one metric two-jet. For the constant-curvature family generated by a boundary reparametrization the Hessian has a nonzero rank-four mode, so the image of the length map is curved. For a fixed recovery the proto-area Hessian is minus the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori information lost in recovery, which the Petz map decomposes orthogonally at a product reference, and which, on a finite-dimensional space of logical directions with positive minimum retained fraction, is at most a sharp multiple of the retained information. Geometric realization requires this loss to reproduce the normal length Hessian on every interval. Two codes show that exact regional area operators can fail to sew into one graph geometry, and that a matched reference with vanishing first response can fail at second order. All criteria refer to one recovery branch and one extremal-surface branch.

papers.title: Exact and Finite de Sitter QFT from CFT
papers.summary: Parallel to the AdS Scale-Space construction in \cite{Yang:2026AdS}, we construct a $(d+1)$-dimensional de Sitter QFT directly from $d$-dimensional CFT data. The dS geometry is the moduli space of oriented balls, and the lifted operators are obtained by conformal-family Casimir completion. The Euclidean parent CFT gives a finite wavefunction representation, while the Minkowski parent CFT gives a double-time representation that is unitary in the parent-time polarization. This provides a CFT-based framework for reexamining puzzles of dS and double-time QFT.

papers.title: Gravitational wave scattering at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$: Murua construction and elliptics
papers.summary: We compute the amplitude for the scattering of a gravitational wave off of a spinless point particle at fourth order in Newton's constant, using the worldline quantum field theory formalism. A decomposition of our master integrals incorporating Murua coefficients allows us to entirely bypass the cut subtraction needed to convert the scattering amplitude into the Magnusian, the latter mapping directly onto the scattering phase shift in partial wave space. Elliptic functions appear in momentum space for the first time for this process at this order. To compare to the phase shift from black hole perturbation theory, we present an analytical method for performing the partial wave projection of the new elliptic sector to any partial wave order $\ell$, and verify the equivalence of the Magnusian and the phase shift. This demonstrates that point-particle worldline quantum field theory accurately describes Schwarzschild black holes up to $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$.

papers.title: Conformal Renormalisation of 8D Einstein Gravity
papers.summary: We show that Holographic Renormalisation (HR) in eight dimensions is encoded in the unique conformal gravity theory that admits an Einstein sector with constant negative curvature. We explicitly relate HR to Topological Regularisation (TR), where the latter prescribes to add the Euler term to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian density, with a precise coefficient so as to ensure that the resulting density is polynomial in the anti de Sitter (AdS) curvature. The polynomial is still asymptotically divergent. We find that the aforementioned, unique conformal gravity action in 8D, reproduces the polynomial, together with extra boundary terms that cancel the divergent terms in the action. We conjecture that, in arbitrary even dimension, HR is equivalent to conformally completing the Einstein-Hilbert action with negative cosmological constant, plus the Euler term with fixed coupling prescribed by TR.

papers.title: A Horizon-to-Boundary Dictionary Linking Smooth Horizon Continuation, Pole-Skipping, and $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ Lowest-Weight Structure
papers.summary: We study pole-skipping for a scalar field in the JT/AdS$_2$ black-hole background. Previous work established the local mechanism: at a pole-skipping point, a near-horizon recurrence relation becomes degenerate and an additional regular expansion coefficient is left undetermined. We take this local degeneracy as the starting point and track two independent solutions normalized at the AdS boundary, denoted by $R_1$ and $R_2$ for the source and response branches, respectively. Let $\widehat A$ and $\widehat B$ denote the source and response coefficients after their common singular factor is removed, and let $\chi_\mu$ denote the universal ingoing horizon factor. We find \[ \widehat A=0 \Longleftrightarrow \frac{R_2}{\chi_\mu}\in C^\infty, \qquad \widehat B=0 \Longleftrightarrow \frac{R_1}{\chi_\mu}\in C^\infty . \] Thus the source and response zeros correspond separately to horizon smoothness of the two boundary-normalized solutions after the ingoing factor is removed. At integer resonance the local regular solution contains an additional coefficient $a_N$. In the JT/AdS$_2$ model, continuation of the nonresonant ingoing solution fixes $a_N=0$ and thereby selects a unique retarded value at resonance, although unrestricted approaches in parameter space remain path dependent. At the endpoint of the pole-skipping lattice, the response branch is a lowest-weight state of the background $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry. A static holographic-superconductor example further shows that simultaneous horizon smoothness is insufficient if the two boundary branches are linearly dependent. A two-branch pole-zero intersection therefore requires \[ W[R_1,R_2]\neq0. \] These results distinguish the known local horizon degeneracy from the global relation between boundary branches and the resonant horizon solution space.

papers.title: No off-diagonal quantum focusing for R\'enyi divergences
papers.summary: The quantum focusing conjecture (QFC) is a mathematical expression of the idea that semiclassical gravity remains universally attractive. In its non-gravitational limit, the diagonal inequality is the quantum null energy condition (QNEC), which requires convexity of relative entropy with respect to the vacuum under null deformations. R\'enyi divergences generalize relative entropy, and positive results for the diagonal R\'enyi QNEC raise the question of whether they also satisfy the off-diagonal inequalities required by a full focusing principle. We show that classical correlations between distinct null generators obstruct this extension for any non-affine R\'enyi-type divergence satisfying data processing, tensor additivity, and matched classical-quantum conditioning.

Regular endpoint conditions give an algebraic quantization condition. Eigenvalues obtained from the truncated instanton prepotential are tested against independent angular spectra near extremality and at larger acceleration. The axisymmetric sector recovers the known exact spectrum.
