papers.title: Branching fraction measurement of the $B^0\to K^+\pi^-\mu^+\mu^-$ decay at high dihadron mass
papers.summary: This Letter presents the first measurement of the $B^{0} \to K^{+}\pi^{-}\mu^{+}\mu^{-}$ differential branching fraction in the region of the dihadron $K^+\pi^-$ mass, $m_{K\pi}$, $1000< m_{K\pi} < 1835\,\text{MeV}/c^{2}$. This decay mode is mediated by the quark-level transition $b \to s\ell^{+}\ell^{-}$, for which the measured effective couplings show tensions with Standard Model predictions. The analysis is performed using proton-proton collision data collected with the LHCb detector between 2011 and 2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $8.4\,\text{fb}^{-1}$. The differential branching fraction is determined across different regions of dimuon mass squared, $q^2$, in the interval $0.1 < q^2 < 18.0\,\text{GeV}^2/c^{4}$, as well as in different regions of $ m_{K\pi}$ in the interval $1.1 < q^2 < 6.0\,\text{GeV}^2/c^{4}$. The results represent the first differential measurement of the branching fraction across $m_{K\pi}$ within the selected dihadron-mass region, and the first observation of the decay within this region above the $J/\psi$ resonance.

papers.title: Energy-energy correlators within $Z$-tagged jets in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: Energy-energy correlators probe perturbative and nonperturbative QCD regimes of jet formation through momentum-weighted angular correlations between hadrons. First measurements in light-quark-enriched jets are presented for inclusive, like-sign, and opposite-sign charged-hadron pairs, using proton-proton collisions at LHCb. The results support universality of the confinement scale for light-quark-initiated jets across collision systems and the reported transverse momentum scale of the jet. In the charge-dependent measurements, opposite-sign correlations are enhanced as angular separation decreases down to the confinement-scale region, a behavior that is well described by simulations.

papers.title: Forward decay chain reconstruction with displaced vertices in intense magnetic fields
papers.summary: Precise reconstruction of particle decay chains is essential for a broad range of analyses in particle physics experiments, particularly those targeting flavour physics and spectroscopy. We present a standalone, modular and extensible decay tree reconstruction framework designed to handle complicated topologies, accounting for tightly constrained particle decays and long-distance trajectory extrapolations through regions of intense and inhomogeneous magnetic field, as well as limited momentum resolution. Implemented in C++, the framework is optimised for configurability and performance. Developed primarily within CERN's LHCb experiment, its focus is on decay chains with vertices located several metres from the LHC proton-proton interaction point, where the dipole magnetic field is maximal and non-uniform. Even so, it remains flexible: it can accommodate these special cases as well as the approximations commonly used in standard decay tree fitting tools, and the geometries of general-purpose collider detectors. Benchmark studies using simulated data demonstrate significant improvements in reconstruction efficiency, invariant mass resolution, and vertex position resolution with respect to existing tools, opening new opportunities for precision measurements and searches involving highly displaced decays.

papers.title: Exploring Collective Effects in Small Collision Systems via Light-Flavour Particle Production in High-Multiplicity pp Collisions at $\sqrt{s}=$ 13 TeV in ALICE
papers.summary: High-multiplicity pp and p-Pb collisions show signatures of radial and anisotropic flow, as well as the enhanced production of strange hadrons. These observations resemble phenomena seen in heavy-ion collisions, where a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is formed, although their origin in small systems remains under discussion. This contribution presents ALICE Run 2 results on light-flavour hadron ($\pi$, K, p) production in high-multiplicity (HM) pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, where the charged-particle multiplicity reaches values comparable to peripheral or semi-peripheral Pb-Pb collisions. The multiplicity dependence of $\pi$, K, and p transverse momentum spectra, $p_{\rm T}$-differential and $p_{\rm T}$-integrated particle ratios, and mean transverse momenta ($\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$) is presented and compared with published results from other collision systems and energies, as well as with PYTHIA 8 and EPOS4 model calculations.

papers.title: Detecting photons in radiative Bhabha interaction with Si-strip and LYSO crystals at future e+e- colliders
papers.summary: Next-generation e+e-colliders have been proposed for the Super Tau Charm Facility covering center-of-mass energies sqrt(s) = 2-7 GeV, and for the Higgs Factories optimized for Z-pole physics and for HZ production. Luminosity can be determined by measuring forward Bhabha scattering. The QED cross-section calculation has reached a precision of better than 10^-3. Detecting radiative photons in Bhabha events provides a tool for validating higher-order corrections in theory. We propose the Forward Detector for detecting Bhabha scattering events at the STCF. The design uses high-resolution silicon detectors and finely segmented LYSO crystals to discriminate radiative photons from closely associated electrons. Bhabha scattering events are simulated with the BHLUMI and BHWIDE programs, and the detector is modeled using GEANT. Systematic uncertainties due to multiple scattering and bremsstrahlung in the beam pipe were evaluated. The potential for achieving precise measurements of radiative processes in Bhabha events is investigated.

papers.title: Measurements of the branching fractions of \boldmath $\chi_{cJ}\to\Sigma^0\bar{\Sigma}^0\eta$
papers.summary: Using $(2712.4\pm14.3)\times10^{6}$ $\psi(3686)$ events collected with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider, we report the first observations of the decay $\chi_{cJ}(J=0,1,2) \to \Sigma^0\bar{\Sigma}^0\eta$. The signal significances, after considering systematic uncertainties, are determined to be 7.2$\sigma$, 5.7$\sigma$, and 6.7$\sigma$ for $\chi_0$, $\chi_{c1}$, and $\chi_{c2}$, respectively. The branching fractions are measured to be $\mathcal B(\chi_{c0}\to\Sigma^0\bar{\Sigma}^0\eta)=({9.7 \pm 1.7 \pm 0.8}) \times 10^{-5}$, $\mathcal B(\chi_{c1}\to\Sigma^0\bar{\Sigma}^0\eta)=({4.9 \pm 1.1 \pm 0.4}) \times 10^{-5}$, and $\mathcal B(\chi_{c2}\to\Sigma^0\bar{\Sigma}^0\eta)=({6.1 \pm 1.2 \pm 0.3}) \times 10^{-5}$, where the first uncertainties are statistical and the second systematic. No significant structure in the $\Sigma^0\bar{\Sigma}^0,\Sigma^0\eta,\bar{\Sigma}^0\eta$ mass distributions is observed under the current statistics.

papers.title: Measurement of the cross sections for $e^{+}e^{-}\to p\bar{n}\pi^{-}$ at center of mass energies from 3.510 to 4.946 GeV
papers.summary: Using a data sample corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 43.8~fb$^{-1}$ collected with the \mbox{BESIII} detector at 44 center-of-mass energy points between 3.510 and 4.946~GeV, the Born cross sections for the process $e^+e^- \to p \bar{n} \pi^-$ and its charge-conjugated process are measured. The energy dependence of the dressed cross sections is investigated to search for possible contributions from vector charmonium and charmonium-like states. No evidence for contributions from the $\psi(3770)$, $Y(4230)$, $Y(4360)$, $\psi(4415)$, $Y(4500)$, or $Y(4710)$ resonances is observed. The upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are determined for the products of the electronic partial widths and the branching fractions for the decays of these resonances into the $p \bar{n} \pi^- + \mathrm{c.c.}$ final state.

papers.title: Real-time Track Reconstruction with FPGAs: an example from MUonE
papers.summary: The feasibility of real-time track fitting of straight tracks for online event selection is shown in the context of the MUonE experiment. In order to reach the high throughput and low latency required for real-time track fitting, the tracking algorithm is implemented using High-Level Synthesis for an FPGA, which provides provides a balance between flexibility and performance. Hardware tracking results from a test with high-rate muons at the CERN M2 beam are presented. This test, a joint effort by the MUonE and Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiments, operated with Two-Strip (2S) modules provided by the CMS tracker group. The prototype version of the fitter used in this test achieves 3.75 $\mu$s latency and 7.75 % resource use. A comparison of the results with those obtained from a pure software implementation shows agreement well below relevant uncertainty scales. Developments since the test are also presented, with the hardware algorithm now reaching 1.35 $\mu$s latency and producing pipelined fitting results above 50 MHz while requiring less resources than the initial version. Doing so required including certain assumptions in the algorithm, but these assumptions hold for linear track fitting in general and algorithm remains useful in contexts other than MUonE.

papers.title: A new AI-based Full Event Interpretation model for flavour physics
papers.summary: The increasing event complexity and data rates foreseen for future LHC coinditions motivate a transition from selecting proton-proton ($pp$) collision events by reconstructing predefined signal candidates to constructing a reduced data stream by interpreting the relevant event features in a signal-agnostic way. We explore the capabilities of deep-learning-based architectures on heavy-flavour physics using LHCb as a case study. Graph-based full-event interpretation techniques address the problem by representing visible products of $pp$ collisions as nodes of a graph, and reconstructing heavy-hadron decay chains hierarchically. A new neutral-particle-aware architecture extends the input data from charged tracks to calorimeter clusters, and uses metric learning to clusterize particles from the same decay chain in a common latent space. Tests on inclusive simulated $pp\to b\bar b$ events show that this approach retains its ability to reconstruct decay chains across a broad range of topologies and multiplicities. We discuss the resulting physics opportunities, with a focus on inclusive $b\to s\ell\ell$ measurements and on searches for exotic hadrons.

papers.title: Measurements of lepton-flavour universality in semileptonic $B$ decays at Belle and Belle II
papers.summary:
Tests of lepton-flavour universality in semileptonic \(B\)-meson decays provide sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. The Belle and Belle II experiments, respectively operating on the KEKB and SuperKEKB colliders in Japan, have collected \(e^+e^-	o B ar{B}\) collisions at a center-of-mass energy corresponding to the \(\Upsilon(4S)\) resonance in samples with a combined integrated luminosity exceeding \(1\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}\). These data, with low particle multiplicity, constrained initial-state kinematics, and excellent lepton identification, provide an ideal environment to study lepton-flavour universality in semileptonic decays of \(B\) mesons. New results on the ratios of semitauonic \(B\)-decay rates compared to analogous light-lepton rates are presented. These include new Belle II measurements of branching-fraction ratios \(R(D^{(*)})\) involving exclusive \(B	o D^{(*)}	au
u\) and \(B	o D^{(*)}\ell
u\) decays using semileptonic or hadronic reconstruction of the accompanying \(B\)-meson tag. Belle II and Belle measurements of angular observables in \(B	o D^*\ell
u\) modes that test light-lepton universality and the Lorentz structure of the decay are also presented. The measurements are statistically limited and individually consistent with Standard Model expectations. The new \(R(D^{(*)})\) results are also compatible with experimental world averages, which continue to exhibit tension with Standard Model predictions. Belle II has now accumulated an \(\Upsilon(4S)\) data sample exceeding that of Belle, offering substantial opportunities for new analysis approaches and heightened precision.

papers.title: Real-time monitoring of LHCb beam spot properties based on FPGA hit reconstruction
papers.summary: We present a real-time trackless method to monitor the centre of the LHCb luminous region and the relative alignment of the two halves of the LHCb Vertex Locator, using cluster counts accumulated in selected regions of the detector and processed in firmware. A Principal Component Analysis performed on simulated data yields a set of weight vectors that reduce the position estimators to scalar products of the counter rates, executable with negligible computational overhead. With pp collision data from 2024, the transverse position of the luminous region is reconstructed with a statistical precision of approximately 4 micrometre per coordinate in a 90 millisecond accumulation window. A measurement of the longitudinal centre is demonstrated with a statistical precision of a few millimetres in simulated studies. The introduction of run-time configurable firmware counters has been studied in simulation to improve the transverse and longitudinal resolutions by a factor of three with respect to the fixed-geometry baseline.

papers.title: Amplitude analysis of $\psi(3686)$ radiative decays into $\pi^{0} \pi^{0}$ system
papers.summary: A model-independent amplitude analysis of the $\pi^{0} \pi^{0}$ system produced in radiative $\psi(3686)$ decays is presented. The analysis is based on the unique dataset of $(2712.4\pm14.3)\times10^6$ $\psi(3686)$ decays collected by the BESIII detector. Scalar and tensor partial-wave contributions are obtained as piecewise functions of $M_{\text{inv}}(\pi^{0} \pi^{0})$ with minimal model assumptions. The observed contribution of the scalar partial wave exhibits similar behavior to the one reported in the study of radiative $J/\psi$ decays, while the tensor contributions provide no evidence for resonance-like structures except for the clearly visible $f_2(1270)$. The results are presented in the form of log-likelihood scans in $M_{\text{inv}}(\pi^{0} \pi^{0})$ bins, which preserve all the statistical information and account for relevant systematic uncertainties. The model-independent description provided in this paper allows to combine the presented results with other related data in the development of phenomenological models.

papers.title: An end-to-end experimental pipeline for automated track identification for paleo-detectors
papers.summary: Paleo-detectors aim to exploit the damage tracks left in natural minerals by cosmic messengers over geological times to reconstruct past fluxes of energetic particles. For cosmic rays, the expected signal is abundant, and the tracks are micron-scale, so they can be revealed by etching and read out with conventional optical microscopy; what remains challenging is turning a bulk sample into a calibrated track-length spectrum that can be quantitatively confronted with theoretical predictions. In this work we present the experimental pipeline we developed for this purpose within the INFN PRImuS experiment, from sample preparation and automated multi-focus microscopy to track recognition with OptimusPrimus, a two-stage machine-learning algorithm, and to a forward-folding model that propagates geometric sectioning, etching and the measured detection response into simulated spectra. The pipeline was built and validated on chemically etched obsidian where the recovered track-length distribution is statistically compatible with expert annotation. In parallel, we developed and characterized a dry argon-plasma etching protocol for halite, an evaporite mineral of particular interest as a low-background cosmic-ray paleo-detector. Since every stage of the pipeline is mineral-agnostic, with only the trained networks and the detection response to be re-derived from annotated data, we are now applying it to plasma-etched halite with the aim of identifying cosmic-ray-induced tracks.

papers.title: Search for charged Higgs bosons decaying into top and bottom quarks in lepton+jets final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: A search is presented for charged Higgs bosons (H$^\pm$) in proton-proton (pp) collision events via the pp $\to$ (b)H$^\pm$ processes, with H$^\pm$ decaying into top (t) and bottom (b) quarks. The search targets final states with one lepton, missing transverse momentum, and two or more b jets. The analysis is based on data collected at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV with the CMS detector at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. We search for charged Higgs bosons in the 200 GeV to 1 TeV mass range. The results are interpreted within the generalized two-Higgs-doublet model (g2HDM). This model predicts additional Yukawa couplings of the Higgs bosons to the top quark $\rho_\mathrm{tt}$, the top and charm quark $\rho_\mathrm{tc}$, and the top and up quark $\rho_\mathrm{tu}$. This search focuses on the real components of $\rho_\mathrm{tt}$ and $\rho_\mathrm{tc}$, which are probed up to values of unity. An excess is observed with respect to the standard model expectation with a local significance of 2.4 standard deviations for a signal with an H$^\pm$ boson mass ($m_{\mathrm{H}^\pm}$) of 600 GeV. Limits are derived on the product of the cross section $\sigma$(pp $\to$ (b)H$^\pm$) and branching fraction $\mathcal{B}$(H$^\pm$ $\to$ tb, t $\to$ b$\ell\nu$), where $\ell$ = e, $\mu$. The values of $\rho_\mathrm{tc} \gtrsim$ 0.11$-$0.38 are excluded at 95% confidence level, depending on the $m_{\mathrm{H}^\pm}$ and $\rho_\mathrm{tt}$ assumptions. The results represent the first search for charged Higgs bosons within the g2HDM framework and complement the existing results on additional neutral Higgs bosons performed on the same-sign top quark pair, three top quark, or four top quark pair final states, constraining extra Yukawa couplings for the neutral Higgs boson below the TeV scale.

papers.title: Observation of $\Upsilon$(1S) + Z associated production and measurement of the effective double-parton scattering cross section in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: The observation of associated production of an $\Upsilon$(1S) meson with a Z boson and a measurement of the ratio of its fiducial cross section to the fiducial cross section of the Z boson are presented. Both the $\Upsilon$(1S) meson and the Z boson are identified via decays into a pair of opposite-sign muons. The analysis is based on proton-proton (pp) collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, collected with the CMS detector in 2016$-$2018 and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. Using the production of the Z boson decaying into four muons as a normalization channel, the ratio of the fiducial cross sections $\sigma$(pp $\to$ Z $+$ $\Upsilon$(1S))$\mathcal{B}$(Z $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-$)$\mathcal{B}$($\Upsilon$(1S) $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-$ ) to $\sigma$(pp $\to$ Z)$\mathcal{B}$(Z $\to$ 4$\mu$) is measured to be $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Z+\Upsilon}\mathrm{(1S)}}$ = (21.1 $\pm$ 55 (stat) $\pm$ 0.6 (syst) $\times$ 10$^{-3}$), where stat and syst denote the statistical and systematic uncertainties, respectively. The result is used to extract the effective double-parton scattering cross section $\sigma_\text{eff}$ = 13.0 $^{+7.7}_{-3.4}$ mb. In addition, for the first time, $\sigma_\text{eff}$ is measured in bins of the transverse momentum of the $\Upsilon$(1S) meson or of the Z boson.

papers.title: Measurement of event shape variables using charged particles inside jets in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: Event shape variables, constructed from the four-momenta of the final-state objects in an event, are sensitive to the predictions of quantum chromodynamics in multijet production. A measurement of five event shape variables is presented, using proton-proton collision data collected at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV with the CMS detector during 2016$-$2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. The variables are evaluated using the charged particles inside jets. After correcting for detector effects, their distributions are compared with the predictions from several models for multijet production. Overall, there is general agreement between several theoretical predictions and the data with scope for improvement of our understanding of QCD at different energy scales.

papers.title: Measurement of the local and nonlocal amplitudes in $B^{+}\to K^{+}\mu^{+}\mu^{-}$ decays
papers.summary: This paper presents a thorough study of the local and nonlocal amplitudes in $B^+ \to K^+\mu^+\mu^-$ transitions through an amplitude analysis of the dimuon mass spectrum of the decay. The analysis is based on $pp$ collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 8.4fb$^{-1}$ collected by the LHCb experiment. This measurement employs a model that describes both one-particle and two-particle nonlocal amplitudes across the entirety of the dimuon mass spectrum, enabling the determination of both short- and long-distance contributions to the decay. The compatibility of the Wilson coefficient combinations $C_9+C_9'$ and $C_{10}+C_{10}'$ with the Standard Model prediction is found to vary between $1.6\,\sigma$ and $4\,\sigma$, depending on the choice of local form factors.

papers.title: Measurement of dijet angular distributions and search for beyond the standard model physics in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: A measurement is presented of dijet angular distributions in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, using data collected with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. For the first time, the dijet angular distributions, corrected for detector effects, are compared with the predictions of perturbative quantum chromodynamics at next-to-next-to-leading order, including next-to-leading-order electroweak corrections. While data are generally found to be in agreement with predictions, a small difference in shape of the normalized distributions is seen for dijet masses ranging from 2.4 to 4.8 TeV and above 6 TeV. The distributions are used to search for proposed signatures of quark compositeness, extra spatial dimensions, quantum black holes, dark-matter mediators, axion-like particles, and anomalous gluon couplings. The most stringent limits to date are set for most of these scenarios. Quark contact interactions are excluded at 95% confidence level (CL) up to a scale of 17 (37) TeV for destructive (constructive) interference in a benchmark scenario, valid to next-to-leading order in quantum chromodynamics, and in which only left-handed quarks participate. The coupling of axion-like particles to the gluon, $c_{\text{g}}/f_{\text{a}}$, is constrained to be lower than 0.42 TeV$^{-1}$ at 95% CL. The anomalous triple-gluon coupling, $C_{\text{G}}/\Lambda^2$, in a standard model effective field theory is constrained to be lower than 0.0076 TeV$^{-2}$ at 95% CL.

papers.title: Evidence for the decay $B^0_s\to\phi\eta'$
papers.summary: Using a dataset corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $9 \,\textrm{fb}^{-1}$ collected in proton-proton collisions between 2011 and 2018 by the LHCb experiment, evidence is found for the decay $B^0_s\to\phi\eta'$ with $3.5 \sigma$ significance. The branching ratio relative to the $B^0_s\to\phi\phi$ decay is determined to be $R=(3.56 \pm 0.79\pm 0.18\pm 0.06)\times10^{-2}$. This corresponds to a branching fraction, $B(B^0_s\to\phi\eta')=(0.66 \pm 0.15 \pm 0.03 \pm 0.02) \times 10^{-6}$ where, in both cases, the first uncertainty is statistical, the second systematic, and the third due to external branching fractions.

papers.title: Search for single vector-like quark production in opposite-sign dilepton final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: A search is presented for single production of a vector-like top quark T, decaying into the standard model top quark and Higgs boson, in a final state including two opposite-sign leptons (electrons or muons), jets, and missing transverse momentum. The data were recorded by the CMS experiment in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV at the CERN LHC in the years 2016$-$2018, and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of up to 138 fb$^{-1}$. No excess in data over the background expectations is observed. Upper limits at 95% confidence level on the product of the T production cross section and its decay branching fraction to tH are set. The observed limits are 2.0 pb at a T mass 600 GeV and 0.3 pb at $M_\mathrm{T}$ = 1200 GeV, with a minimum of 0.1 pb at $M_\mathrm{T}$ = 1000 GeV. This is the first search for single vector-like T quark production, followed by a decay to a top quark and the Higgs boson, in opposite-sign dilepton final states.

papers.title: Search for single production of a vector-like B' quark decaying to a top quark and a W boson in the single-lepton final state in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: A search is presented for the single production of a narrow-width vector-like B' quark that decays to a t quark and a W boson. This search targets a single-lepton final state, where a muon or electron originates either from the semileptonic decay of the t quark or from the leptonic decay of the W boson, with the other particle decaying hadronically. The (semi-)leptonic portion of the event is reconstructed from an electron or muon, missing transverse momentum, and a small-radius jet identified as a b quark jet if the muon or electron originates from the t quark. The hadronic portion of the event is reconstructed as a single large-radius jet. The originating particle of the large-radius jet is identified using a neural-network-based tagger, and the dominant background contributions are modeled from data using a neural autoregressive flow network. The data were collected from 2016 to 2018 by the CMS experiment at the LHC in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. This search is the most sensitive to date to the production of single narrow-width B' quarks. It excludes electroweak-singlet B' quarks with $\Gamma/m_\mathrm{B'}$ = 5% for masses between 0.8 and 1.23 TeV. Limits are also placed on the production cross section of single B' quarks produced in association with t quarks, and on the coupling factor of the B' quark to electroweak bosons.

papers.title: Separating charm and bottom decay electrons with point-cloud deep learning on the charged-hadron environment
papers.summary: Electrons from semi-leptonic decays of charm ($D$) and bottom ($B$) hadrons are important probes in high-energy collisions, while their separation remains challenging due to the similarity of the underlying decay topologies. In this work, the charged-hadron environment associated with each electron is represented as an unordered point cloud and combined with the electron kinematics and charge. Several set-based machine learning architectures, including DeepSets, Transformer, and graph neural networks, are used to distinguish electrons from prompt $D$ and direct $B$ decays without explicit vertex observables. The three architectures achieve comparable performance. Moreover, the Transformer is found to perform better than a boosted decision tree trained on physics-motivated high-level observables. At an efficiency of about 40\%, the classifier reaches a purity level close to 80\% on the test sample. The classifier response is strongly related to the geometric and topological properties of the charged-hadron environment. The information learned by the classifier is further studied using non-prompt $D$ electrons and charged hadrons from different angular regions. Our results indicate that the learned separation is driven mainly by the later stages of the decay chain rather than by initial production effects. The angular-region study further shows that useful discriminating information extends beyond the near- and away-side cones. This method is also evaluated for mid-rapidity proton--proton collisions at both RHIC and LHC energies.

papers.title: Search for the $\boldsymbol{B^0 \to K^0_{\rm S} \tau^+ \tau^-}$ decay
papers.summary: We present the first search for $B^0 \to K^0_{\rm S} \tau^+\tau^-$ decays. We look for signal decays in $B^0\bar B^0$ events produced in asymmetric-energy electron-positron collisions. This work uses samples from the Belle and Belle~II detectors, comprising 1.16 billion $\Upsilon(4S)$ events. In $\Upsilon(4S)\to B^0\bar{B}^0$ decays, the non-signal $\bar{B}^0$ meson is fully reconstructed in a hadronic channel. For the signal $B^0$ meson, $\tau$-lepton decays into final states with a single charged particle are selected. We observe no evidence for the signal and set an upper limit on the branching fraction $\mathcal{B}(B^0\to K^0_{\rm S} \tau^+\tau^-) < 8.3 \times 10^{-4}$ at the 90\% confidence level. Combining this with the recent measurement of the isospin-partner decay $B^+\to K^+\tau^+\tau^-$, we determine an upper limit $\mathcal{B}(B\to K\tau^+\tau^-) < 5.4\times10^{-4}$ at the 90\% confidence level.

papers.title: Silent coverage failures in rare-event searches and a degeneracy index that predicts them
papers.summary: Searches for new physics in low-background experiments infer a non-negative signal strength from few events and often report an upper limit. Nominal frequentist coverage requires both a valid interval construction and an adequate data model. We study how controlled model departures affect lower- and upper-endpoint coverage for six interval procedures in an exact Poisson counting experiment, dark-matter recoil spectra, and a neutrinoless-double-beta-decay peak search. We introduce the Poisson--Fisher degeneracy index $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PF}}(\delta\nu;\vartheta_0)=(\beta,\gamma)$, which maps a specified expected-count deformation, after projection onto the complete fitted tangent space, to $\beta$, the signed fitted signal shift in profiled standard-error units, and $\gamma$, the Poisson--Fisher norm of the unabsorbed residual. Locally, the sign of $\beta$ identifies the threatened endpoint, while larger $\gamma$ implies greater detectability by the saturated-Poisson goodness-of-fit test used here at a fixed $5\%$ type-I error rate. Across the studied deformations, positive signal-like bias degrades discovery-side coverage while making upper limits conservative; negative signal bias from overestimated signal efficiency can make the upper endpoint undercover. Calibration under the nominal simulator does not protect against misspecification of that simulator relative to the data-generating process. A plausible deformation with large $|\beta|$ and small $\gamma$ may therefore evade diagnosis and should be represented by a nuisance constrained with auxiliary information or included in a defensible envelope. In the exactly collinear constrained-nuisance benchmark, modelling the deformation restores coverage at the evaluated grid points, at a quantifiable cost in interval sensitivity.

papers.title: Measurement of $e^{+} e^{-}\to p\bar{p}$ around $\psi(2S)$ with scan method
papers.summary: This paper uses the data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $495$~pb$^{-1}$ in the center-of-mass energy region from 3.58~GeV to 3.71~GeV to study the relative phase between strong and electromagnetic amplitudes in the $\psi(2S)\to p\bar{p}$ decay. The cross sections and the effective form factors around $\psi(2S)$ of proton-antiproton pairs are presented thereby filling the gap in the experimental results around the $\psi(2S)$ resonance for the first time, and the results are consistent with the previous BESIII and BaBar results. The relative phase is extracted from the cross-section line shape as $\Phi_{g,\gamma}=(105.9\pm9.4)^\circ$ or $\Phi_{g,\gamma}=(-105.3\pm9.1)^\circ$. Correspondingly, two solutions for the $\psi(2S)\to p\bar{p}$ branching fractions are obtained as $\mathcal{B}=(3.21\pm0.13)\times10^{-4}$ and $\mathcal{B}=(3.47\pm0.19)\times10^{-4}$. These results support the universality of the phase and provide new insights into its underlying mechanism.

papers.title: Overview of the HL-LHC CMS outer tracker upgrade and lessons learned from 2S module production
papers.summary: For operation at the High-Luminosity LHC, the CMS collaboration is developing a significantly enhanced silicon detector system with improved radiation hardness, higher granularity, and extended coverage up to a pseudorapidity of $|\eta|\approx$ 4. The Outer Tracker will be equipped with two types of modules (2S and PS) that will provide tracking information to the L1 trigger of the HL-LHC CMS detector, by rejecting signals from particles below a certain transverse momentum threshold. Hence, these modules must be assembled with high precision and have to pass strict requirements. In this note, an overview of 2S module production is presented, as well as representative examples of problems and experience acquired during module assembly and performance tests.

papers.title: Gravitational-Wave Propagation in Quadratic Einstein--Cartan--Dirac Gravity: A Conditional Tensor-Sector Analysis
papers.summary: We study leading tensor propagation in a specified first-order Einstein--Cartan--Dirac theory with the parity-even quadratic torsion invariant $\zeta T_{\lambda\mu\nu}T^{\lambda\mu\nu}$. Eliminating the nondynamical Lorentz connection on the regular algebraic branch gives a metric description containing the Einstein--Hilbert term, the Dirac action, and a $\zeta$-dependent axial--axial fermion contact interaction. We evaluate the transverse-traceless (TT) Hessian under an explicit factorized mean-field closure, with vanishing connected-current TT response, vanishing first- and second-order TT response of the factorized current scalar, and zero intrinsic TT anisotropic stress. Under these imposed conditions, the leading two-derivative tensor action has $Q_T=M_{\rm Pl}^{2}$ and $c_T=1$, with no leading dispersion or propagation-induced polarization splitting. These conditions do not follow from isotropy of the one-point axial current, and the present calculation does not derive them from a microscopic fermionic state. The result is therefore conditional and does not establish a general Einstein--Cartan--Dirac no-go theorem. We identify the connected-current TT response that must be calculated to extend the result beyond this closure. Published NANOGrav summaries are used only to check consistency with the GR-like prediction; no new timing-data likelihood or constraint on $\zeta$ is obtained.

papers.title: Perturbative Renormalization of Noether Currents in SYM with Improved Discretizations
papers.summary: We investigate the perturbative renormalization of Noether currents associated with chiral symmetry and supersymmetry transformations in $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, regularized on the lattice using improved discretizations. In particular, we study the chiral current and the supercurrent operator for a broad class of lattice actions: Wilson fermions with one-step stout-smeared links and a clover term, together with a family of Symanzik-improved gluon actions. Since the supercurrent mixes with both gauge-invariant and gauge-noninvariant operators, we compute the corresponding renormalization factors and mixing coefficients at one-loop order. We analyze the impact of improved gluon and gluino actions on this mixing pattern and investigate whether suitable choices of lattice parameters, such as the clover and stout coefficients, can reduce unwanted lattice artifacts at one loop. Our results provide perturbative input for the implementation of Ward identities and for matching lattice observables to their continuum counterparts, while also offering guidance for simulations aimed at restoring supersymmetry in the continuum limit.

papers.title: Time-Domain Observables for Resonant Scattering in Quantum Simulations of Lattice Gauge Theory
papers.summary: Quantum computing may allow unprecedented access to nonequilibrium quantum dynamics, including problems of interest in particle physics, like the real-time development of scattering processes. Although fault-tolerant simulations at scale are still in the future, recent advancements toward early fault-tolerant simulations motivate building increasingly elaborate benchmark problems in order to assess state-of-the-art capabilities and test new algorithms and observables. In this work, we study glueball scattering on a line-of-plaquettes lattice in pure $SU(3)$ lattice gauge theory. We characterize scattering of the lowest-energy glueball states using classical exact diagonalization methods, identifying the continuum resonance structure using real-time simulations and approximate analytic methods, and we propose time-domain observables for extracting properties of the resonance from quantum simulations. We furthermore construct a toy model that shares the spectral features of the lattice gauge theory and demonstrate extraction of the observables. Feasibility on near-term hardware is demonstrated through simulation of a resonant collision of this toy model on Quantinuum System Model $\texttt{H2-2}$, with a 14-plaquette chain encoded in 28 qubits. The Trotterized circuit after optimization and compression requires $\sim 25n$ entangling gates for $n$ Trotter steps.

papers.title: Signal-to-noise problems in fault-tolerant quantum computation
papers.summary: Quantum computation offers a promising alternative to classical Monte Carlo methods by naturally avoiding sign problems through unitary evolution. A common misconception follows from this: because quantum simulation sidesteps the sign problem, it is often assumed to be an essentially perfect substitute for classical sampling. This is false---quantum measurements are intrinsically stochastic, and estimating observables often requires a number of samples that grows exponentially with system size, time separation, or inverse temperature, exactly as in the classical signal-to-noise problem. In this work, we analyze the origin and structure of signal-to-noise problems in quantum computation, drawing parallels with classical Monte Carlo, and demonstrate that such noise persists even in sign-problem-free regimes. We discuss strategies to mitigate it, in particular a quantum generalization of Stein control variates construction, in which unbiased estimators are built from operator commutators $[X,A]$ and their discrete diagonal counterparts, and validate the approach with exactly solvable numerical examples that quantify the achievable variance reduction. Our results underscore that variance reduction, not merely sign-problem avoidance, is required to make quantum algorithms practically viable for many-body physics.

papers.title: A Spectroscopic Census of Cluster White Dwarfs from DESI, LAMOST, and SDSS
papers.summary: Gaia has substantially expanded the sample of candidate white dwarfs (WDs) in open clusters, but many remain without spectroscopic characterization. We leverage the increasingly extensive archives of large public spectroscopic surveys to identify 62 candidate cluster WDs with available spectra from DESI, LAMOST, and SDSS. After discarding sources with very low S/N and unreliable host clusters, 44 candidates remain, including 37 non-magnetic DA WDs, of which 15 had not previously been characterized in the literature for cluster studies. We find that nine are consistent with single-star origins in their proposed host clusters, increasing the combined cluster DA initial--final mass relation (IFMR) sample to 132 WDs. All lie within $2\sigma$ of the best-fit IFMR from the most comprehensive recent cluster WD sample, suggesting these additions do not require recalibrating the empirical IFMR. One is a likely Hyades tidal-tail WD, providing further evidence that dynamical dispersal helps explain the long-standing WD deficit in the nearest cluster. We further compare WDs with spectra from multiple surveys. Among seven Praesepe WDs observed by both DESI and SDSS, DESI gives higher WD masses in six cases, with a mean difference of $0.067\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, while the inferred progenitor masses differ by as much as $0.459\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. More broadly, nine of ten single-star cluster DAs with DESI spectra lie above the empirical IFMR, with a mean final-mass residual of $0.06\pm0.04\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. These results show that survey-dependent differences can strongly affect cluster WD parameters, and should be considered when combining heterogeneous spectroscopy in empirical IFMR studies.

papers.title: Where Cluster Galaxies Reside and How Strongly They Lens
papers.summary: The efficiency of galaxy-galaxy strong lensing (GGSL) in clusters depends jointly on the inner mass distributions of member galaxies and their locations within the cluster potential. Observed GGSL probabilities exceed $\Lambda$CDM predictions by nearly an order of magnitude, but the relative roles of internal structure and environment remain unclear. We disentangle these effects by comparing HST strong-lensing clusters with TNG-Cluster analogs at similar lens redshifts, matched by their primary Einstein radius. For each member, we measure its lensing strength in isolation and when embedded in the cluster field. Members in cluster-critical regions are classified as Major or Minor Perturbers depending on whether they strongly lens in isolation; those in subcritical regions are classified as Intrinsic Lenses, Boosted Lenses, or Inert Members according to whether they lens independently, only with environmental assistance, or not at all. Observed clusters contain 33.7% of selected members in cluster-critical regions, compared with 21.6% in TNG-Cluster, while their Major-to-Minor ratios are similar. Outside these regions, observations contain substantially more Intrinsic and Boosted Lenses and fewer Inert Members, with Boosted Lens fractions of 25.8% and 13.5%, respectively. The discrepancy persists at fixed subhalo mass and after including line-of-sight structure. A mass-conserving contraction mimicking core-collapsed self-interacting dark matter largely recovers the conditional lensing fractions but not cluster-critical occupancy. The GGSL discrepancy therefore reflects both insufficient central concentration in simulated members and differences in their locations within the cluster lensing field.

papers.title: Cluster Ages to Reconstruct the Milky Way Assembly (CARMA). VI. The age-metallicity relation of in-situ clusters and the age of the Universe
papers.summary: Within the homogeneous framework for the derivation of GC ages defined by the CARMA collaboration, we focus on the clusters born in-situ in the MW. As they are the oldest among the old GCs, their absolute age provides constraints about the age of the Universe. Moreover, the shape of their AMR is expected to show the imprints of past merger events, in case these were able to trigger GC formation in the Galaxy. We derive new homogeneous ages for 18 GCs dynamically and/or chemically classified as in-situ, and build the MW AMR from a total sample of 34 GCs. We find that all the selected GCs follow a well defined AMR, with the exception of NGC6642 and Pal1. While the former is likely a member of the LKH merger event, thus putting chronological evidence for the existence of this progenitor on even more robust ground, for the latter we propose an alternative scenario according to which it formed in-situ, but in a metal-depleted region of the Galaxy, possibly due to the interaction with an unspecified merger event. To find evidence of merger-driven GC formation, we use a GMM for the observed age distribution. This is statistically best-fit by 4 components, which we associate with significant events of the MW merger history. Cluster ages were finally calibrated to a more accurate absolute age scale based on asteroseismic measurements of the mass of red giant stars in NGC6791, and the resulting AMR was fit to compute the look-back time for the beginning of cluster formation in the MW. The fit yields t_GC,i=13.59+0.33-0.32 Gyr for initial cluster formation, and tU=13.79+/-0.34 Gyr for the age of the Universe. This value translates to H0=68.72+3.95-3.49(stat.)+2.65-2.32(sys.) km s-1 Mpc-1, where the systematic error comes from a realistic estimate of the zero point uncertainty on the GC absolute ages derived from stellar models.

papers.title: A first view of interstellar Fe-bearing dust grains with XRISM
papers.summary: Understanding the reservoirs of iron (Fe) in our Galaxy is crucial for probing the mechanisms that drive dust grain growth in the interstellar medium (ISM). High-resolution X-ray absorption spectroscopy offers a powerful tool to investigate the chemistry of dust grains, particularly those containing Fe, through spectroscopic features near photoabsorption edges known as X-ray Absorption Fine Structures (XAFS). With the Resolve spectrometer aboard XRISM, we can now examine the Fe K-edge (7.1 keV) owing to its improved spectral resolution in this energy range. This enabled us to probe the dust grain chemistry in high Galactic column densities. In this work, we present a pilot study on dust grain chemistry through the Fe K-edge of the XRISM Performance Verification target GX 340+0. This source is a persistently bright low-mass X-ray binary with a hydrogen column density of 6.6x10^22 cm^-2 along the line of sight, providing sufficient optical depth at the Fe K-edge. By fitting combined dust and gas models, we find that Fe is depleted by 95% into dust along the line of sight towards the source. Moreover, we find evidence that 38% of the solid-phase Fe is in metallic iron, 47% in iron sulfides, and the remainder in silicates. The large contribution from metallic iron and iron sulfides differs from what is typically inferred from X-ray studies of diffuse ISM and may suggest that that these compounds become more significant reservoirs of Fe in higher column density Galactic sightlines.

papers.title: Searching for Nearby Supermassive Black Hole Binaries with GRAVITY
papers.summary: We present a systematic interferometric search for close supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries in 20 nearby type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGN) observed with VLTI/\grav. We investigate parsec-scale asymmetric emission by modeling the squared visibilities and closure phases with a single circular Gaussian component plus a background point source for the central AGN, and searching for additional compact companions through grid-based binary models. The robustness of the search is validated using injection-recovery simulations and point-spread-function diagnostics. Several features are identified in the initial significance maps, but only one candidate out of 20 shows a persistent compact asymmetry, corresponding to an observed incidence of $5\%$. If NGC~3783 is interpreted as a binary AGN, we derive a Poissonian one-sided $1\sigma$ upper limit of $f_{\rm bin}<16.5\%$ for GRAVITY-detectable binaries among bright nearby AGN (K<12.5) at separations of $\sim1$-$100$~pc. Conversely, if the observed asymmetry in NGC~3783 is associated with asymmetric circumnuclear dust emission, the corresponding upper limit on the binary fraction is $f_{\rm bin}<9.2\%$. We compare these results with predictions from the Horizon-AGN simulation, finding comparable binary fractions. We also noted that the expected fraction strongly depends on the assumed distribution of individual SMBH accretion rates within binaries, which is currently unresolved in cosmological models. Our results demonstrate the potential of infrared interferometry to identify parsec-scale binary AGN candidates and motivate future GRAVITY+ observations to expand the sample and follow up known candidates, helping to confirm their nature and distinguish genuine binaries from asymmetric nuclear structures.

papers.title: Stellar discs and intermediate-mass black holes in galactic nuclei II. Fragmenting the disc and forming the S-stars in a live nuclear star cluster
papers.summary: We present direct $N$-body simulations of a stellar disc around the supermassive black hole Sgr~A*, perturbed by an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) and embedded in a live nuclear star cluster. A retrograde IMBH with $m_\bullet=2000\,M_\odot$, relative inclination $\theta_\bullet=150^\circ$, and initial semi-major axis $a_\bullet=0.15$~pc breaks the disc into three disc-like components and an angular momentum filament. The stochastic torques of the cluster, together with the IMBH's inward migration, increase the angular separation between these substructures. By ${\sim}5$~Myr, their separations become comparable to those among the observed Galactic-centre young star structures. The innermost ($a\le0.04$~pc) disc stars evolve into an S-star-like population. Relaxation driven by the cluster disperses their orbital planes, excites their eccentricities and depletes the `zone of avoidance' within ${\sim}10$~Myr even without an IMBH. The IMBH further accelerates their orbital-plane reorientation. However, the most eccentric S-stars may require an additional formation channel, such as the Hills mechanism. The distinctive signatures of the IMBH are the well-separated disc components and the eccentricity excitation confined to the radial range swept by its orbit. Dynamical friction from the cluster reduces the orbital size of a $2000\,M_\odot$ IMBH initially at $0.15$~pc by more than a factor of two within $10$~Myr. Prograde IMBHs tend to align with the stellar disc, whereas a $2000\,M_\odot$ retrograde IMBH can anti-align with the radially overlapping disc stars. We also quantify how the IMBH affects the supply of stars to the loss cone and the rates of stellar tidal disruptions and binary separations.

papers.title: Globular cluster Observations for Luminosity-dispersion Distances (GOLD): Project description and velocity catalogue
papers.summary: We introduce and describe the Globular cluster Observations for Luminosity-Dispersion distances (GOLD) project, which has the principal aim of determining independent distances based on the globular cluster (GC) absolute magnitude-velocity dispersion ($M_V - \sigma$) relation calibrated with Milky Way GCs with Gaia distances. The project comprises observations of GCs in 19 early- and late-type galaxies taken with FLAMES/GIRAFFE on ESO's Very Large Telescope. So far, 17 galaxies have been observed. The spectra cover the wavelength range 8483-9000 AA, including the calcium triplet region at a spectral resolution of $R\sim18,000$. The spectra provide line-of-sight velocities with typical uncertainties of $\Delta v = 1-2$ km s$^{-1}$. Using primarily velocities to separate extragalactic sources from foreground stars, we present here our initial sample of 1062 GCs and 101 ultra-compact dwarf galaxies (UCDs). For more than 650 of these objects we present the first velocity measurement. We discuss the available photometry and size measurements, and show that our velocities are in good agreement with previous studies. Our velocity catalogues are made publicly available. Beyond the principal aim of obtaining precision distances, additional science to be explored with these data includes host galaxy halo dynamics and clustering analysis, mass-to light ratios of GCs and UCDs in the sample, the stellar initial mass function and black hole occupation fraction of the GCs, and chemical abundances from high-dispersion spectra.

papers.title: What does self-supervision add to engineered features for stellar light curves?
papers.summary: TESS light curves encode a star's pulsation, rotation, binarity and oscillations, among other physical properties, but the survey produces far more light curves than can be labelled by hand. Astronomers have engineered a few dozen physically motivated features from them, which together remain a strong baseline. Previous work has trained encoders on light curves and judged them by their own downstream scores, but has not asked what they add to the engineered features. We pre-train a convolutional encoder on unlabelled TESS light curves to predict each window's latent representation from those of its neighbours. We then freeze it, add its features to the 25 engineered features, and read the combination out with one fixed linear probe on ten tasks: five variability classes, four asteroseismic targets and rotation period. Adding the learned features improves the readout on 7 of 10 tasks over the engineered features alone, where an untrained encoder does not. The combination also outperforms two networks trained end-to-end on the same labelled stars on most tasks. An encoder trained without labels therefore gives astronomers new features that complement the ones they already use rather than replace them.

papers.title: Harmonic and intermodulation emission from direct-to-device satellites - Harmonics of the Starlink 2.6 GHz downlink and the products around them
papers.summary: Direct-to-device (DTD) satellites carry mobile base stations transmitting in terrestrial mobile bands. Their non-linear emission products can fall into radio astronomy bands, including passive bands. We measure the harmonics of the Starlink DTD downlink at 2620-2630 MHz and the intermodulation products around them, search for products next to the carriers, and compare them with the ITU-R unwanted-emission limits and radio astronomy protection criteria. We use autocorrelations of single Australia Telescope Compact Array antennas on tracked passes of DTD and other satellites with the 16 cm and 4 cm receivers. Harmonic ratios and receiver tests show that the harmonics are satellite-generated. We simulate the aggregate equivalent power flux density of a constellation at Effelsberg and the ATCA. The harmonics H2 to H4 at 5240, 7860 and 10480 MHz fall by about 16 dB per order, show no trend with elevation, and originate on the satellite. H2 is also detected in 32% of integrations more than 10 degrees from any DTD satellite. Inside the harmonic zones the spectra follow the n-fold convolution of the carriers; outside them, intermodulation products of order n+2 and higher lie on average 19 dB below the zone and switch between -23 and -15 dB within seconds. Next to the carriers no satellite emission is detected to 33 dB below the carriers. H2, >=-38.9 dBW in 4 kHz isotropic-equivalent, is at or above the SM.329 space-station limit; H3 and H4 meet it. For 8640 satellites the aggregate exceeds the protection criteria by 65 and 25 dB at the second and fifth harmonics, and by >100 dB for out-of-band emission at the mask level in 2690-2700 MHz. Harmonics are received far outside the serving beams. Their radiated level must be limited directly, not through the power at the antenna port. Compliance with per-satellite ITU-R limits does not protect radio astronomy from the aggregate of a constellation.

papers.title: Mapping Wolf-Rayet winds with spectro-interferometry I. Detection of multiple co-rotating interaction regions in WR 6
papers.summary: WR 6 is the prototype for periodic variability due to large-scale wind structures in Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars, showing a consistent periodicity of 3.76 d in photometry, spectroscopy, and polarimetry. However, the origin of this variability is debated, attributed either to corotating interaction regions (CIRs) or a low-mass companion. We use time-resolved interferometry to investigate the origin of periodic variability in WR 6. We aim to detect and characterize structures in the stellar winds of WR 6 and discriminate between the CIR and low-mass companion scenarios. Using the extended configuration of the Auxiliary Telescopes at VLTI, we obtained six GRAVITY epochs over six months to search for the presence and variability of wind-structures in WR 6. We also obtained complementary spectroscopic observations during one of the epochs to monitor contemporaneous spectral line variability. For all six epochs of GRAVITY observations: (i) WR 6 is consistent with a single star and has no spatially resolved companion detected above $M\gtrsim6\,M_\odot$; (ii) The He I line-emitting region is spatially resolved, while the He II lines remain unresolved, consistent with atmosphere models; (iii) Around 2.19 $\mu$m, discrete line-emitting features offset from the center of the star are detected. The number, positions, and wavelengths of these features vary across epochs. Spectroscopic monitoring reveals spectral line residuals that broadly correspond to the two features seen in the GRAVITY data of the fifth epoch. Finally, the first three epochs, observed on three consecutive nights, show significant variability in these features but cannot be directly linked across epochs. We thus report the detection of multiple large-scale structures in the wind of WR 6 with VLTI/GRAVITY. We favor CIRs as their likely origin owing to temporal and spatial variability that cannot be reconciled with a low-mass companion.

papers.title: The effect of triples on the Chemically Homogeneous Evolution Channel for producing Gravitational Wave Sources
papers.summary: Despite the growing number of gravitational-wave (GW) detections, the formation of merging binary black holes (BBHs) is still debated. One of the proposed formation channels is Chemically Homogeneous Evolution (CHE), which makes distinct predictions for the properties of the resulting black holes (BHs): high masses ($\gtrsim35\, M_\odot$) and large, orbitally-aligned spins. These predictions are based on studies that consider this channel only in isolated binaries. However, most massive stars reside in triples. We investigate how a tertiary affects the CHE channel. We use detailed binary models computed with MESA for the inner CHE systems coupled with analytical prescriptions for the hierarchical triple dynamics. Specifically, we study the von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai mechanism that can accelerate the merger of the inner BBHs through high-eccentricity excitations. We show that a tertiary companion enables mergers at higher metallicities, where the classical binary CHE channel does not operate. At $Z_\odot/3$, triples produce BHs with lower masses (around $15\,M_\odot$) and lower spins (around 0.25) compared to the low-metallicity classical scenario. We further expect triple dynamics to lead to spin-orbit misalignment and potential residual eccentricities at merger. In triples at $Z_\odot/3$, half of the mergers occur within 1 Gyr. Moreover, 10% of the population leads to prompt mergers within 1 Myr (1% within 1 kyr) that are of potential interest for electromagnetic counterparts. We conclude that the triple CHE channel is promising as (i) it may contribute more substantially to the local merger rate than had been expected for the classical CHE channel due to the shorter delay times and effectiveness at higher metallicities and (ii) produces mergers with properties that more closely resemble the lower masses and lower spins inferred for most of the observed GW merger population.

papers.title: TESS Pulsation Timing Reveals the JWST Calibration Star HD 158485 as a Double-pulsator Binary
papers.summary: HD~158485 is an A-type $\delta$~Scuti star in the CALSPEC network and the JWST absolute-flux calibration program. Gaia DR3 assigns it a binary classification probability close to unity but provides no orbital solution. Using TESS observations from Sectors 14--26, 40--41, 47--60, and 73--86, we measure the pulsation phases of six $\delta$~Scuti modes. The frequencies form two groups with opposite light-travel-time delays, revealing two pulsating components. A direct light-curve forward model yields an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb}=382.80^{+0.80}_{-0.76}$~d, eccentricity $e=0.242^{+0.045}_{-0.046}$, projected light-time amplitudes of $195.8^{+9.2}_{-8.9}$ and $239.7^{+6.8}_{-6.8}$~s, and a dynamical mass ratio of $q=M_B/M_A=0.818^{+0.046}_{-0.045}$. A blind prediction based only on the first two long TESS campaigns reproduces the third campaign without updating the orbital parameters, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of $r=0.983$. Its held-out rms is 83.8~s, compared with 289.9~s when the period is fixed at 365.25~d. A 5.15-$\sigma$ Hipparcos--Gaia EDR3 proper-motion anomaly independently indicates unresolved astrometric motion. The unresolved companion can also affect spectrophotometric predictions: a conditional PB2-constrained two-atmosphere model differs from the corresponding single-star atmosphere prediction by 1.6\% over 1--5~$\mu$m and 2.5\% over 5--28~$\mu$m. HD~158485 therefore shows that a calibration-relevant binary can lack a catalogued orbital solution while two independent pulsation clocks reveal and measure its orbit.

papers.title: Reawakening of GS 1843+00: A Multiwavelength Study of its 2026 Giant X-ray Outburst
papers.summary: GS 1843+00 (Ginga 1843+009) is a poorly studied Be/X-ray binary system that underwent a major X-ray outburst in 2026 February-May after nearly sixteen years of quiescence. We present an X-ray, optical, and radio study of GS 1843+00 during this outburst, focusing on the evolution of the neutron star emission geometry, Be-disk connection, and possible outflow activity. We analyse three NuSTAR observations obtained at different stages of the outburst, complemented by archival RXTE and Chandra data, optical spectroscopy and imaging with the Nordic Optical Telescope, and a MeerKAT radio observation. NuSTAR observations reveal coherent X-ray pulsations around 29.7 s with a spin-up rate of $(-5.1\pm0.1)\times10^{-8}$ s s$^{-1}$ during the outburst. The pulse profiles show strong evolution with energy and outburst phase, with distinct morphologies even at comparable luminosities. The pulsed fraction varies between 1 and 16% and exhibits a complex reversal in energy dependence above 7 keV, increasing with energy during the first two observations and decreasing during the third. The 3-79 keV broadband spectra are described by thermal Comptonization with a blackbody and an Fe K$\alpha$ emission line, with no evidence for a cyclotron absorption feature. Phase-resolved spectroscopy reveals variations in the Comptonization and blackbody parameters, indicating changes in the accretion-column structure. Optical spectroscopy confirms the presence of a Be-circumstellar disk through H$\alpha$ and Paschen-series emission lines. No radio counterpart is detected, with a $3\sigma$ upper limit of 36 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ at 1.28 GHz. Weaker H$\alpha$ emission compared with previous epochs indicates that the Be-circumstellar disk was in a different state during the current episode, while the radio non-detection suggests that any associated outflow activity was faint or below the detection limit.

papers.title: Impact of Decay-Chain Feeding by Long-Lived Heavy Nuclei on Nuclear Cosmochronology
papers.summary: Nuclear cosmochronology provides an independent method for determining the ages of astrophysical objects without relying on Galactic chemical evolution models. Long-lived radioactive actinides synthesized via the rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) particularly thorium and uranium serve as ideal chronometric nuclei. However, predicting the initial abundances of these nuclei and their subsequent long-term evolution remains a major source of uncertainty in nuclear cosmochronology. In this work, we investigate the impact of decay-chain feeding from long-lived progenitor nuclei on nuclear cosmochronology and estimate the corresponding age corrections. We develop a self-consistent radioactive decay network that includes all relevant decay pathways and couple it to $r$-process nucleosynthesis calculations. By tracking the long-term evolution of $r$-process nucleosynthesis based on neutron star merger trajectories, the dominant long-lived nuclei shaping the evolution of the chronometric elements Th and U are identified as $^{232}$Th, $^{235}$U, $^{236}$U, $^{238}$U, and $^{244}$Pu. It is found that delayed feeding substantially modifies the long-term evolution of actinides particularly for $^{232}$Th, which receives significant late-time contributions from heavier progenitor nuclei such as $^{244}$Pu and $^{236}$U. As a consequence, the U/Th and Th/X chronometers exhibit significant sensitivity to delayed feeding from the progenitor nuclei $^{244}$Pu and $^{236}$U, with age corrections reaching $\sim5$~Gyr. These results suggest that decay-chain feeding from long-lived progenitor nuclei plays a crucial role in nuclear cosmochronology and should be properly accounted for in age determinations based on actinide chronometers.

papers.title: Magnetar X-ray flares as elementary reconnection events in a self-organized critical magnetosphere
papers.summary: Magnetar bursts are commonly attributed to magnetic energy release, yet the physically relevant dissipation unit has remained uncertain. Here we argue that this unit is not the burst as conventionally defined, but the short substructures within bursts, namely magnetar X-ray flares (MXFs). Using 789 MXFs from SGR~J1935+2154, we show that their waiting times separate into two components, interpreted as reflecting clustered intra-episode events and longer inter-episode intervals, that their proxy emission measure and temperature exhibit distinct rising and declining trends, and that their energy release scale (ERS) proxy distribution has a high-end slope in the same statistical regime as solar and stellar flares. Combined with the previously measured MXF duration slope, these results identify MXFs as a three-dimensional fractal-diffusive self-organized critical (FD-SOC) system with $\beta_{\rm diff}\simeq2$, implying reconnection avalanches that expand linearly through an active magnetosphere. We infer that magnetar active episodes are global unloading states assembled from many elementary flares. Magnetar X-ray flares are therefore the physically relevant units for magnetar outburst statistics and for connecting magnetar high-energy activity to other impulsive phenomena.

papers.title: ELISA: A Bayesian X/$\gamma$-ray Spectral Analysis Toolkit
papers.summary: Forward-folded X/$\gamma$-ray spectral fitting increasingly benefits from Bayesian workflows to better capture counting statistics, background uncertainties, and complex parameter degeneracies, while fully reproducible end-to-end implementations are still not always straightforward to deploy in routine analyses. We present ELISA (Efficient Library for Spectral Analysis), an open-source Python toolkit that streamlines the full spectral analysis loop for X/$\gamma$-ray astronomy: data loading, model construction, inference, and model validation and comparison. ELISA couples a JAX-accelerated forward model with a unified fitting interface, supporting both rapid optimization and modern Bayesian sampling. Built-in diagnostics make convergence checks and predictive assessment a standard part of the workflow, motivating principled model refinement when needed. Using a spectral fitting example of the Insight-HXMT Crab observation, we find substantial improvements in sampling efficiency compared with XSPEC's default MCMC implementation. ELISA is available at https://github.com/wcxve/elisa and on PyPI at https://pypi.org/project/astro-elisa.

papers.title: Beyond the Damped Random Walk: Multiband AGN Variability from SDSS to Rubin LSST
papers.summary: The flux variability of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs) is commonly modeled using the damped random walk (DRW), but increasingly rich multiband time-domain surveys motivate more flexible stochastic models that characterize variability beyond a single timescale and exploit dependence across bands. Multivariate continuous-time autoregressive moving average (MCARMA) processes extend the multivariate DRW to higher-order stochastic dynamics and provide a matrix-valued power spectral density for characterizing marginal variability and cross-band dependence. In a carefully selected Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Stripe~82 sample, higher-order models are selected for 109 of 134 AGNs (81.3\%), with substantial rather than marginal support in most objects; convergence diagnostics indicate that this fraction is conservative. The fitted models also reveal strong cross-band dependence that generally decreases with wavelength separation. Motivated by this richer structure, we investigate its recoverability under Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) observing conditions. Model-order recovery depends strongly on the underlying stochastic behavior as well as source brightness and observing cadence. Recovery is high across many of the simulated settings, but deteriorates when the characteristic features of higher-order variability become difficult to distinguish from the multivariate DRW. Additional simulations show that this loss of distinguishability can persist over a range of underlying variability behaviors. These results show that stochastic structure beyond the multivariate DRW is prevalent in our selected SDSS sample, while its recoverability with LSST depends on both observational conditions and the form of the underlying stochastic variability. The methodology is implemented in the Python package mcarma.

papers.title: Multiphase Analysis of (U)LIRG Nuclear Activity (MAUNA). I. Spatially Resolved Optical Emission-Line Diagnostics
papers.summary: We present resolved optical integral-field spectroscopy of the 32 luminous and ultraluminous infrared galaxy systems of the Multiphase Analysis of (U)LIRG Nuclear Activity (MAUNA) sample, drawn from the GOALS survey and selected to have JWST/MIRI medium-resolution spectrometer (MRS) observations. The data set combines new Keck/KCWI observations of 10 systems with archival VLT/MUSE cubes for 22 systems, covering H$\beta$ to [S II] at ~1 arcsecond spatial resolution (~0.9 kpc at the sample median distance). Using the optical [N II]/H$\alpha$ BPT diagram, we find that composite and LINER-like excitation together account for most of the classified area (median fractions 0.44 and 0.26), while Seyfert-like gas covers a median fraction of 0.02 but carries a far larger proportion of the line luminosity where it is present. Both the projected size of the Seyfert-classified region, $R_{\rm Sy}=0.08$-$7.5$ kpc, and its [O III] luminosity increase with the bolometric AGN luminosity, with $R_{\rm Sy}\propto L_{\rm AGN,bol}^{0.54\pm0.18}$, as expected for gas photoionized at a constant ionization parameter. The scatter about the luminosity relation depends on dust opacity: the [O III] luminosity per unit AGN luminosity falls by $1.09\pm0.25$ dex per unit depth of the 9.7 $\mu$m silicate absorption feature (Spearman $\rho=-0.60$, $p=0.001$). Optical excitation diagnostics therefore locate AGN-excited gas reliably but systematically underestimate the luminosity the AGN supplies to the host in the most obscured (U)LIRGs.

papers.title: TDCOSMO 2026: A 3% measurement of the Hubble constant from strong lensing and stellar kinematics
papers.summary: We present cosmological constraints from 11 strongly lensed quasars with measured time delays (hereafter, the TDCOSMO-2026 sample). In addition to expanding the sample, we improve many aspects of our blind analysis with respect to our 2025 analysis. Among other improvements, spatially resolved kinematics are available for nine systems, including six with JWST-NIRSpec, compared to one in 2025; for three lens models, JWST-NIRCam images now replace HST; axisymmetric dynamical modeling is applied directly to the spatially resolved data, instead of an axisymmetric correction factor applied to spherical models; and the line-of-sight convergence is now based on the Euclid Flagship simulations instead of the Millennium Simulation. Our baseline and primary result is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with a prior on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ from the DES-Dovekie supernova sample. In the flat $\Lambda$ cold dark matter ($\Lambda$CDM) cosmology, we find $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$, a 3.3% uncertainty that accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. The SLACS and SL2S samples are in excellent agreement with the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, improving the precision on $H_0$ in flat $\Lambda$CDM to 3.0%. Using the DESI-DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) likelihood instead of DES-Dovekie yields fully consistent results. We also present constraints in the open $\Lambda$CDM, $w$CDM, $w_0w_a$CDM, and $w_{\phi}$CDM cosmologies; the TDCOSMO $H_0$ inference is robust and consistent across all of them. The combination of the TDCOSMO+SLACS+SL2S likelihood with those from DESI-DR2 and DES-Dovekie disfavors $w=-1$ at the $2.3$-$2.5\sigma$ level in all three dark energy extensions that we tested. We find, e.g., $w_0=-0.88^{+0.04}_{-0.05}$ in $w_{\phi}$CDM and $w_0 = -0.85^{+0.07}_{-0.06}$ in $w_0w_a$CDM, while $w_a = -0.48^{+0.46}_{-0.44}$ remains consistent with zero.

papers.title: Hera Orbit Determination Covariance Analysis of Didymos Binary Asteroid with the Full Two-Body Problem
papers.summary: Standard planetary radio science analyses may be inadequate for accurately interpreting data from the Hera mission at the Didymos system due to the anticipated challenge posed by the coupling between the translational and rotational motions of the asteroids. A more precise dynamical model, the full two-body problem model, which includes a mutual gravitational potential, may be required to fit the Hera data properly. This work presents a covariance analysis of the Hera radio science experiment using this advanced model. The tested dynamical scenarios are based on recent lightcurve observations indicating that Dimorphos is in an excited non-principal axis spin state that is, on average, tidally locked. Three non-principal axis scenarios are analyzed using a multi-arc local estimation approach instead of the global one adopted in previous investigations involving non-chaotic states. The results show that tumbling or chaotic cases significantly improve the recovery of the bodies' moments of inertia due to the enhanced observability of the system's dynamics from the excited spin state. However, the local estimation approach slightly degrades the accuracy of the mass estimation by a factor of 1.3-3 and Dimorphos' relative orbit by about one order of magnitude. Developing a dedicated constrained multi-arc filter is thus required to improve the estimation accuracy of the Didymos system's dynamical state further. Nevertheless, these results still meet the Hera radio science requirements.

papers.title: Milani and Juventas Optical Navigation Images in Support of the Hera Radio Science Experiment
papers.summary: The European Space Agency's Hera mission aims to advance planetary defense by investigating the Didymos binary asteroid system following NASA's DART impact on Dimorphos. Incorporating simulated CubeSat images into Hera's orbit determination framework significantly improves positional accuracy, reducing uncertainties by up to three orders of magnitude for Milani and one for Juventas. This data enable more precise estimation of key parameters such as asteroid masses, rotational states, and moments of inertia, with up to 90% uncertainty reduction in Dimorphos' dynamical state under chaotic scenarios. Sensitivity analysis reveals the influence of pointing accuracy, image noise, and imaging frequency. Additionally, dedicated scientific investigations using Dimorphos-focused CubeSat images further advance understanding of the system. These findings underscore the critical role of CubeSat images in refining navigation and advancing science, offering valuable insights for future small-body missions.

papers.title: Mid-IR Water-Vapor Seeing: Implications for ELT/METIS High-Contrast Imaging from VLTI Data
papers.summary: Direct imaging and characterization of rocky exoplanets remains one of the central challenges in exoplanetary science. The mid-infrared (mid-IR) offers a favorable high-contrast imaging (HCI) regime, as the planet-star contrast is more moderate than at shorter wavelengths. However, mid-IR observations with extremely large ground-based telescopes (ELTs) are strongly affected by spatio-temporal fluctuations in atmospheric water vapor (WV), which introduce chromatic wavefront errors that are largely invisible to adaptive optics systems operating at shorter wavelengths. This poses a significant challenge for mid-IR HCI instruments such as METIS, which aims to detect thermal emission from rocky exoplanets in the $N$-band (8--13 $\mu$ m). To quantify WV-induced wavefront errors, we analyze $K$-band fringe-tracker data from the GRAVITY instrument at the VLTI and derive the optical path difference between group-delay and phase-delay measurements. This difference provides a direct measure of the differential WV column density ($\Sigma$) above the telescopes. We examine the dependence of the RMS differential WV column density ($\sigma_{\Sigma}$) on precipitable water vapor (PWV), airmass, seeing, and wind speed across multiple VLTI configurations. Among these parameters, PWV shows the strongest correlation with $\sigma_{\Sigma}$. We further explore the influence of the vertical PWV distribution on this relationship. Next, we use power-spectral-density analysis to quantify how increasing PWV modulates $\Sigma$ variability. The wavefront error associated with this phenomenon on ELT scale is approximately 15~nm RMS in the $L$-band and 175~nm RMS in the $N$-band, relative to the $K$-band. These results provide a quantitative framework for assessing and mitigating atmospheric WV effects in next-generation mid-IR HCI instruments.

papers.title: Modelling the Point Spread Function of ILMT images
papers.summary: We have devised an approach to model the empirical Point Spread Function (PSF) of the images taken with the 4-meter International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT). The characteristics of the ILMT PSF are influenced by the nature of the Liquid Mirror, as well as by instrument specific and atmospheric factors. As the telescope uses Time Delay Integration (TDI) mode for tracking the passing objects, the PSF varies along the declination axis due to differential motion and star-trail curvature. The 5-element optical corrector homogenizes the PSF to some degree, but does not completely eliminate the disturbing effects mentioned above. The PSF in the RA direction is changing due to the sky conditions. We show that we can successfully model the PSF of 4k$\times$4k chunks using PSFEx, accounting for second-order X-Y variability. Our software robustly reproduces the PSF and its variation across the field.

papers.title: From Sky to Science: Time Domain Astronomy with the ILMT Survey
papers.summary: The PyLMT transient detection pipeline has been operational since November 2023 and has detected $\sim$10,000 transients and variable objects in ILMT images in near real time.
