papers.title: Electromagnetic Singularity-Aware MIMO Channels: Scattering-Based Channel Modeling and Physics-Aware Power Allocation
papers.summary: Electromagnetic information theory (EIT) brings electromagnetic physics into wireless channel analysis and offers a physical view of channel structures hidden by conventional models. This paper studies channel instability near electromag- netic singular states, where small environmental perturbations can cause large variations in the end-to-end channel. Using resolvent-based spectral analysis, we develop an electromag- netic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel model that decomposes the end-to-end channel into a smooth regular component and singularity-associated components. The analysis shows that the singularity-associated components become more sensitive to environmental perturbations near singular states. The proposed model also reveals a limitation of conventional water filling (WF): power allocation based only on instan- taneous channel gains does not account for such instability. We therefore estimate singularity information from broadband MIMO channel state information (CSI) and develop a singularity- aware transmit covariance optimization method. Simulations demonstrate numerical stability of the estimated pole frequencies and illustrate the environmental sensitivity of pole-associated channel components. The proposed allocation reduces weighted singular-channel exposure by 90.32% while retaining 95% of the nominal WF rate.

papers.title: Analysis of Integrated Communication and Sensing in Cylindrical Aerial Corridors
papers.summary: In unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks, integrated communication and sensing (ISAC) is emerging as a key enabler to support extended and continuous communication and sensing capabilities for sixth-generation (6G) services among UAVs operating in swarms. In this paper, a comprehensive framework is presented to investigate the ISAC coverage probability of a reference UAV-base station (BS) in a UAV network. A fixed number of UAV user equipment (UAVUEs) and UAV-BSs are deployed in an aerial corridor modeled as a finite cylinder. The three-dimensional (3D) binomial point process (BPP) is used to model both the 3D spatial locations of the UAV-UEs and the UAV-BSs. By adopting realistic 3D third generation partnership project (3GPP) antenna patterns for both the UAV-UEs and UAV-BSs, the UAVs' boresight direction of the maximum antenna gain is modeled as a random unit vector. All UAV-BSs have sensing capabilities, so an arbitrary yet fixed reference UAV-BS acts as a monostatic radar to acquire sensing measurements associated with a target UAV-UE at a given time snapshot while the target UAVUE communicates with the reference UAV-BS. Consequently, considering both clutter and communication interference, exact analytical expressions for ISAC coverage probability are derived. Low complexity baseline analytical expressions are also derived by ignoring clutter interference and directional characteristics of the UAV-UEs. Finally, motivated by the vision for intelligent UAV networks, a DeepSets-based model is developed and trained to estimate the optimal location of the reference UAV-BS that maximizes ISAC performance given a spatial deployment of the UAVs. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to rigorously investigate ISAC performance in UAV networks while incorporating the directionality characteristics of the UAV antennas.

papers.title: Equilibria and consensus in discrete-time opinion dynamics with mixed weighted-averaging and weighted-median mechanisms
papers.summary: Opinion dynamics models relate interpersonal influence to consensus or persistent disagreement. We study a discrete-time model combining weighted-average and weighted-median updates on a fixed directed network. Individuals update synchronously with possibly different adjustment coefficients. We characterize equilibria through local balance conditions and opinion level sets, and establish convergence to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium using nonexpansiveness and Krasnosel'skii--Mann theory. We define type-dependent cohesive sets: each weighted-average member assigns all its weight to the set, whereas each weighted-median member assigns at least one half. Consensus is reached from every initial condition if and only if no two such sets are disjoint. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent disagreement. Replacing weighted-median individuals by weighted-average individuals preserves consensus whenever it is already guaranteed for all initial conditions. Four numerical studies examine the number and locations of weighted-average individuals. The frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with their fraction in the sampled ensembles, but individual realizations need not follow this trend.

papers.title: Spiking Neural Beamforming for Multichannel Speech Enhancement on the Edge
papers.summary: Speech enhancement with wearable and edge devices requires architectures that balance enhancement quality against power and memory resources. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a promising path towards this goal through sparse, event-driven computation, but existing SNN-based speech enhancement methods are largely restricted to single-channel processing and therefore cannot exploit the spatial diversity available from microphone arrays. In this work, we propose a fully SNN framework for multichannel speech enhancement based on a fully connected architecture (FC-SNN) with sequential spike encoding, derived from a compact artificial neural network (ANN) baseline via leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. We characterize how enhancement performance scales with model size and spike-train length relative to ANN and classical beamforming baselines, and report the resulting parameter counts and computational complexity. We further compare direct and rate spike encoding, revealing a clear trade-off between event-driven computation and enhancement performance, and use these results to identify favorable configurations for edge devices.

papers.title: A Reduced Greedy Minimum Distance Phase Shift Design for Quantized RIS-Assisted Spatial Modulation
papers.summary: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have emerged as a key enabler for next-generation wireless networks, offering control over the propagation environment through nearly passive reflecting elements. When combined with spatial modulation (SM), an RIS shapes a finite set of noise-free signal points at the receiver, and the error rate performance under maximum-likelihood (ML) detection is governed by the smallest pairwise Euclidean distance among these points. In this paper, we propose a low-complexity RIS phase shift design algorithm for RIS-assisted SM under practical discrete phase shift control. The proposed method targets the minimum Euclidean distance directly through a reduced greedy search over the discrete set of RIS phase shifts, in contrast to existing approaches that align RIS phase shifts to maximize the effective channel gain and therefore do not directly address the dominant error events. The search effort is controlled by a small set of integer parameters, providing a tunable trade-off between bit error rate (BER) performance and computational cost. We evaluate the proposed method against continuous and quantized phase-alignment baselines, including a complexity-matched comparison against the most directly comparable benchmark. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves a significant SNR gain over quantized phase alignment under the same discrete hardware model, and this advantage persists under imperfect channel state information.

papers.title: Aerodynamic Promptness of Tilting-Propeller Multirotors
papers.summary: This work develops a geometric theory of aerodynamic promptness for multirotor platforms whose propeller directions depend on a smooth orientation-mechanism configuration. The actuator state consists of the actual signed propeller speeds and the mechanism configuration, and the nonlinear actuator map retains both the signed-quadratic propeller law and the configuration-dependent thrust directions. Constant direction maps represent fixed propellers, while shared dependence on mechanism coordinates represents mechanically coupled tilts. A Riemannian metric on the product actuator manifold compares propeller accelerations and orientation-mechanism rates through physically interpretable scales. Composing the actuator-map differential, the musical isomorphism induced by this metric, and the dual differential defines a task-rate authority map from wrench covectors to wrench-rate vectors. In fixed task coordinates, the square root of the determinant of its matrix defines aerodynamic promptness. Positive promptness is equivalent to local wrench-rate surjectivity, while the associated spectrum resolves directional authority and conditioning. The same construction yields the metric horizontal inverse, the orthogonal projector onto wrench-fiber directions, and task-preserving internal motions that regulate promptness without changing the instantaneous wrench. The construction is related intrinsically to dynamic feedback linearization and specialized to the independently tilting, radially arranged Holocopter and Voliro architectures, clarifying how their established allocation and rank constructions fit within the same actuator-manifold geometry.

papers.title: Design of Privacy-Preserving Estimators Under Prior Information Exposure
papers.summary: State estimation is widely used in networked dynamical systems, but released estimates may inadvertently reveal sensitive information about private state variables. Existing privacy-preserving estimation frameworks often do not explicitly account for adversarial prior knowledge. Motivated by this gap, we study privacy-preserving state estimation for discrete-time linear stochastic systems under prior information exposure using pointwise maximal leakage (PML). We first reveal a privacy anti-optimality property of the Kalman filter: in the absence of additive release noise, the steady-state Kalman filter maximizes PML privacy leakage among the considered class of stable linear estimators. We further establish a nontrivial lower bound on the steady-state estimation error enforced by $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PML privacy. We then derive sufficient release-noise conditions that guarantee $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PML privacy, first for the Kalman filter and then for stable linear estimators. Finally, a convex semidefinite program is formulated for a joint design of the estimator gain and release noise covariance, providing a tractable privacy-preserving estimator with an explicit upper bound on the steady-state estimation error. Simulations on a source--load power system demonstrate the proposed privacy--utility tradeoff.

papers.title: NANO: A Unified Optimization Framework for Nonlinear Gaussian Filtering
papers.summary: Conventional Gaussian filtering typically approximates nonlinear models or their statistical moments and retains the Kalman update structure. The resulting approximation errors can affect both state estimates and their uncertainty. This paper presents the Natural Gradient Gaussian Approximation (NANO) framework for nonlinear filtering. Both prediction and measurement update are formulated as optimization problems over Gaussian distributions, with the entire Gaussian distribution serving as the optimization variable. The framework integrates observation losses, distributional discrepancies, natural-gradient optimization, and finite-step update rules, providing a unified formulation for constructing different filters. Natural-gradient iterations account for the geometry of the Gaussian family and jointly update the distribution parameters. The framework incorporates the existing NANO-P method using the Kullback-Leibler divergence and introduces NANO-W using the Wasserstein distance. NANO-P maintains covariance positive definiteness through a positive-semidefinite curvature approximation, while NANO-W uses a covariance transport update that accommodates indefinite curvature. Their update rules and sufficient conditions for covariance positive definiteness are established within the common framework. Through these two realizations, the proposed framework achieves the best estimation accuracy among the evaluated methods on each of six benchmarks. Runtime evaluations further assess its computational feasibility for practical applications.

papers.title: Differentiable Co-Design of Ultrasound Probe Geometry and Acquisition for Plane-Wave Imaging
papers.summary: Ultrasound image quality depends on both the probe geometry and the transmit and receive processing, but engineers usually design the two separately. Physics-based simulators (Field II, k-Wave, MUST/SIMUS) compute the radio-frequency channel data but give no gradients, so design studies must use grid or black-box searches that become slow as the number of parameters increases. We present a fully differentiable end-to-end pipeline for plane-wave ultrasound imaging, with synthetic speckle phantoms, an analytical frequency-domain RF simulator, delay-and-sum beamforming and an extensible image-quality objective. The element pitch, the transmit and receive apodization and the global speed of sound are differentiable parameters of one computation graph, so one reverse-mode pass gives their exact joint gradients. Studies of each parameter rank the design parameters: the optimized pitch decreases the grating lobes, and the speed-of-sound autofocus gives clear contrast and resolution gains. Over 15 test phantoms, the optimized pitch increases the cyst gCNR from 0.55 to 0.66 (about 20%), and the speed-of-sound correction adds a further 0.05. The lateral point-spread function agrees with Field II within about 10%, and on 49 real CUBDL plane-wave acquisitions from five institutions, the framework finds the global speed of sound with a mean absolute difference of 16.6 m/s from the published corrections and phantom speed of sound.

papers.title: 2D Block OMP for Near-Field Channel Estimation with Extremely Large-Scale UPA
papers.summary: Channel estimation for extremely large-scale uniform planar arrays (UPAs) requires exploiting near-field channel structure to reduce pilot overhead. With a specifically devised channel representation matrix, the near-field channel exhibits a 2D sparse structure, which a conventional 1D block partition might divide into multiple groups. This work develops a 2D block orthogonal matching pursuit (2D-BOMP) estimator that exploits this structure through rectangular coefficient grouping. We establish sufficient recovery conditions for noiseless and noisy measurements and compare the sufficient pilot-length requirements of 1D and 2D partitions. Numerical simulations demonstrate the estimation benefits of 2D-BOMP in estimating the near-field channels of large-scale UPAs, compared with the conventional 1D-BOMP as well as the polar-domain based OMP method.

papers.title: Investigation of RIS Integration in Satellite Systems Guided by ITU-R VSAT Radiation Diagram
papers.summary: The introduction of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) technology marks a transformative era in modern communication systems, enhancing coverage and facilitating higher data transmission rates. While recent research has delved into the integration of RIS into satellite networks, a critical and practical gap persists concerning its implementation in the satellite-Very Small Aperture Terminal (VSAT) downlink, specifically amplifying contributions from the VSAT side. This paper addresses this gap by proposing a simple and engineering methodology to optimize RIS position and orientation, incorporating considerations for the antennas' radiation patterns and the system's topology to streamline optimization variables. The primary objective of this paper is to alleviate the double fading constraint in the reflect link without the need for active elements, achieved by leveraging the Fresnel zone of the RIS. The improvement power ratio depends on the frequency and the VSAT 's diameter. The results show that for a VSAT with diameter 1m the gain is up to 9dB at 2 GHz (S band) and up to 14dB at 4 GHz (C band). Additionally, the RIS channel equation is refined, encompassing the tropospheric attenuation and accounting for electromagnetic wave polarization.

papers.title: Safeguarding Intelligent Power Dispatch:A Performance-Equivalent-Model-Based Safety-Critical Control Method for DC Microgrids
papers.summary: Intelligent power dispatch is enabling fast and self-adaptive decision-making in microgrids, yet its deployment in real-world industry remains limited due to unresolved safety concerns. Existing safety-preserving approaches typically rely on an accurate characterization of the feasible operating region, which is impossible to obtain under uncertain and heterogeneous system dynamics. Moreover, even a dispatch command verified as feasible at a discrete setpoint may become unsafe during its continuous physical execution. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a safety-aware dispatch adjustment framework that uses performance-equivalent modeling of closed-loop systems (PEM-CLS) and embeds high-order control barrier functions and control Lyapunov functions within a quadratic programming formulation (HOCBF-CLF-QP). PEM-CLS captures EMS-required power-regulation dynamics solely from port-level responses, without requiring internal subsystem models, parameters, or controller information. Its modeling error is analytically characterized and explicitly bounded, enabling requirement-oriented dynamic abstraction for safety-critical control. Based on these PEMs, the HOCBF-CLF-QP safety controller coordinates heterogeneous transient power responses and corrects unsafe EMS commands to maintain dynamic safety during command execution. Four deliberately constructed extreme stress-test scenarios are used to expose conflicts between nominal EMS commands and physical safety. Without intervention, the DC-bus voltage violates its safety limit in all four cases, whereas the proposed framework maintains QP feasibility and limits the voltage deviation. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an algorithm-agnostic safety execution layer for intelligent power dispatch without requiring an exact feasible-region model or detailed internal information of lower-level devices.

papers.title: DCCB-Capability-Aware Optimal Info-Power Flow for Transmission Switching in AC/MTDC Grids
papers.summary: Transmission switching is an effective approach for restoring operational flexibility and improving the economic performance of AC/multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids following DC-side faults. Its practical implementation requires that the faulted branch be safely isolated and that the associated switching commands be successfully delivered through the communication network. However, conventional transmission switching models generally represent switching actions using binary variables, without considering the availability of communication resources or whether the corresponding DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) can interrupt the fault current affected by time delay. To address these issues, this paper develops an explicit optimal info--power flow (OIPF) formulation that incorporates information transmission into the post-fault transmission-switching optimization for AC/MTDC grids. The switching status of each DC branch is determined by the availability of its communication path and associated communication resources. In addition, binary switching decisions are supplemented by a DCCB feasibility constraint that limits the estimated delayed-interruption current to the DCCB breaking capability. The resulting problem is formulated as a mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) model that can be efficiently solved using off-the-shelf optimization solvers. Numerical results reveal that limited communication capacity and additional routing costs may render electrically beneficial switching actions infeasible or uneconomical, while delay-aware DCCB interruption constraints may favor lower-delay communication routes despite their higher costs.

papers.title: Calibrating Generative Flows through Regional Probability Matching
papers.summary: Generative models offer a powerful route to scientific simulation and discovery by enabling the study of complex populations and rare phenomena. Flow matching can generate realistic samples, yet inaccurate occurrence frequencies can distort population statistics and compromise inferences about rare events. Here we developed generalized mass-preserving coupled flow matching (G-MPCF), which matches the probability masses of Gaussian source regions to those of weighted data regions. This construction encodes the desired regional frequencies in the correspondence between noise and observations, shaping the learned dynamics while preserving the prescribed target distribution. On a rare-mode benchmark, G-MPCF reduces relative score error by 95.0% and numerical integration error by 89.9% compared with independent flow matching. On CIFAR-10 with a 100:1 class-probability ratio, it reduces corrected class-mass error by 44.6% compared with minibatch optimal transport, while improving mean image fidelity with matched computational budgets. We envision that incorporating regional probability calibration into generative modelling will support more reliable scientific simulation and inference, enabling the study of systems in which rare events and their occurrence frequencies are central to understanding the underlying mechanisms.

papers.title: Generative Deep Learning for CSI Feedback in Massive MIMO via Channel Distribution Prediction
papers.summary: Existing deep-learning-based channel state information (CSI) feedback methods reduce feedback overhead by compressing high-dimensional CSI into low-dimensional representations and/or exploiting historical CSI to predict future CSI. However, these methods may become unreliable when user equipment (UE) suddenly changes its motion. To address this issue, we propose a prediction-aided coding (PAC) framework for generative CSI feedback, which adaptively encodes CSI based on predicted channel/CSI distributions and the observed CSI in real time. Each CSI frame is represented by multiple CSI tokens obtained without using historical CSI, making token generation robust to abrupt UE motion. In the first stage, the conditional distribution, instead of a deterministic value, of the next-frame CSI tokens is predicted based on historical tokens. In the second stage, once the next frame arrives, the predicted distribution is used for variable-length entropy coding of its CSI tokens. To further reduce feedback overhead and inference latency, we propose efficient designs for both stages. For the first stage, a customized causal Transformer with a new positional embedding strategy accurately predicts next-frame token probabilities. For the second stage, a parallel causal decoding strategy reduces the inference latency caused by sequential token decoding. Extensive experiments show that, compared with existing history-aware baselines, PAC reduces feedback overhead by approximately 72% to 84% while achieving higher reconstruction accuracy. Additionally, PAC maintains CSI reconstruction accuracy under random-walk trajectories, whereas existing history-aware baselines suffer sharp degradation in reconstruction accuracy.

papers.title: Venusian Radio Occultation Constellation Design and Reconfiguration Problems: A Benders Decomposition Approach
papers.summary: Driven by the scientific value of Venusian atmospheric studies, numerous missions, such as Magellan and Venus Express, have relied on single-spacecraft radio occultation (RO) experiments. Despite their proven success, data throughput is inherently limited by the use of a single transmitter and its relative geometry with respect to Earth-based receivers. Therefore, the literature proposes leveraging a constellation of spacecraft to increase RO measurement opportunities and improve spatial and temporal coverage; however, current efforts impose strict simplifying assumptions that limit their applicability and responsiveness to complex mission narratives. Beyond initial constellation design, evolving mission objectives may require event-based constellation reconfiguration during operations. To address both design and operational needs, we propose two problems formulated as integer linear programs: the RO Constellation Configuration Design Problem and the RO Constellation Reconfiguration Problem. Further, we address the programs' solution-space explosion with a Benders decomposition approach. Numerical experiments show the applicability of our problems for constellation configuration design, tackle the full mission pipeline, transitioning from global atmospheric profiling to on-demand regional profiling above areas of volcanic interest, and show that the Benders decomposition approach efficiently obtains high-quality solutions to large-scale instances.

papers.title: Practical Hardware-Efficient ISAC: Enabling Multi-Target Sensing With Few RF Chains
papers.summary: Hybrid analog--digital arrays reduce hardware cost in integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), but spatial compression and beam-dependent scan responses complicate multi-target estimation with few radio-frequency (RF) chains. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a burst beam-scanning multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) framework that reuses downlink reference signals for joint range, radial-velocity, elevation, and azimuth estimation. Specifically, a structured global--local dual-tensor estimator separates targets by using scanning observations and refines their parameters from selected-beam RF-chain responses, with delay--Doppler signatures maintaining cross-stage target correspondence. The recovered subarray responses yield closed-form elevation and azimuth estimates through exact sum--difference relations, avoiding small-angle approximations and fine angular grid searches. To further improve Doppler accuracy, spatial-mask-aided weighted least squares exploits the longer inter-burst temporal aperture while resolving phase ambiguity using intra-burst estimates. The joint multi-target Cram\'{e}r--Rao lower bound (CRLB) and corresponding three-dimensional (3D) positioning bound are also derived to characterize estimation performance. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves near-CRLB estimation accuracy at high transmit powers and centimeter- to millimeter-level 3D positioning with only four RF chains, while maintaining low computational cost.

papers.title: Controller-Agnostic Runtime Safety Certificates for Tool-Using AI Agents via Data-Driven Robust Reachability
papers.summary: Software agents built on large language models act by issuing tool calls, some of which cannot be undone. To control theory the model is an opaque feedback controller, replaced every few months, whose closed loop cannot be analyzed directly. We propose a runtime filter, or shield, between any such controller and its environment that certifies a bound on the probability of reaching an unsafe condition during a bounded task. Given a predicate abstraction and candidate successor sets, everything else comes from logs: the loop becomes a finite controlled Markov chain, the estimated kernel is surrounded by a distribution-free confidence region, and robust reach-avoid value iteration runs over it. The certificate is probably approximately correct and uniform over controllers respecting the filter, so one model may replace another without recomputation. In all tested datasets the true risk stayed within certificate and budget; in a file-system sandbox the filter stays sound against a hazard the logs barely covered, where a plug-in baseline certifies safety and fails; and it holds seven controllers, three of them open-weights models, to zero unsafe outcomes in 1050 episodes.

papers.title: Counterfactual Action-Conditioned Graph Prediction for Cascading-Failure Mitigation in Power Systems
papers.summary: Cascading failures develop through coupled power flow redistribution, protection actions, and topology changes, making remedial control dependent on how alternative interventions modify the subsequent trajectory. This paper develops an action-conditioned graph predictor (ACGP) for multi-step cascade prediction and closed-loop mitigation. A same-state counterfactual branching procedure replays identical post-contingency grid states under multiple legal actions while preserving the exogenous trajectory, providing direct supervision for action-dependent electrical states, line connectivity, automatic protection trips, and terminal risk. ACGP is embedded in a receding-horizon controller that evaluates five-step candidate futures, executes the selected intervention, and replans from the observed next state. The final dataset contains 2,860 counter factual roots and 22,880 action-conditioned branches. On the held-out test set, ACGP achieves a five-step line-loading MAE of 0.0369 and a redispatch pairwise ranking accuracy of 0.806; action ablations reduce the ranking accuracy to approximately chance level. In closed-loop Grid2Op experiments, terminal-failure and cascade rates decrease from 53.3% and 51.1% under do-nothing operation to 12.2% and 7.8%, respectively, close to the simulator-reference values of 11.1% and 6.7%. The results show that same-state counterfactual prediction can support effective action comparison and feedback-based cascading-failure mitigation.

papers.title: A Power-Trajectory Framework for Data Center Participation in Day-Ahead Markets
papers.summary: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) is driving substantial growth in data center electricity demand. Interval-based energy blocks in day-ahead markets do not explicitly retain predictable intra-interval demand evolution, potentially creating mismatches with ramp-feasible generation trajectories and affecting settlement. This paper proposes a power-trajectory framework in which data centers declare predictable aggregate demand evolution through continuous demand-side power trajectories before market clearing. The declared trajectories are treated as exogenous inputs for constructing generation trajectories and the corresponding price trajectory. For feasible market-clearing outcomes, physical temporal consistency is established through continuous-time power balance and satisfaction of the modeled generation operating constraints, while economic temporal consistency is established by preserving the dispatch-price correspondence in energy settlement on a common temporal basis. Under the adopted settlement definitions, a trajectory-based settlement analysis separately quantifies the monetary magnitude of representation-induced power imbalances and the supply-side compensation that may remain under temporally consistent clearing and settlement. An illustrative 5-bus case demonstrates the elimination of representation-induced power imbalance and identifies the timing and physical sources of supply-side compensation. A modified IEEE RTS-GMLC case further illustrates these compensation effects across multiple generating units under workload-driven data center demand variations.

papers.title: Scattering-Mediated NLOS Ultraviolet Communication: Channel Characterization, Modeling, and Data Transmission
papers.summary: Solar-blind ultraviolet (UV) optical wireless communication (OWC) enables non-line-of-sight (NLOS) transmission through atmospheric scattering. This work presents a comprehensive experimental and simulation study of a 100 m outdoor UVC link with comparative measurements under LOS-blocked and open-field conditions. The results show that LOS-blocked scattering-mediated links exhibit substantially higher path loss and narrower bandwidth than corresponding open-field measurements, highlighting the impact of residual LOS components in practical diffused beam UVC experiments. A photon-tracing Monte Carlo (MC) framework incorporating realistic transmitter/receiver characteristics and obstacle geometry is further developed to reproduce the measured channel characteristics with high accuracy. Despite the severe path loss and pulse broadening effects, reliable 20-200 kbps transmission is experimentally demonstrated over the 100 m LOS-blocked link using on-off keying (OOK) and pulse-position modulation (PPM), representing the longest-distance and highest-data-rate experimental demonstration of an explicitly LOS-blocked scattering-mediated UVC link reported to date.

papers.title: Wing Rock Modeling and Control for Flight-Critical Systems
papers.summary: Aircraft equipped with delta wings are designed to be aerodynamically efficient in high-speed flight. However, at low-speed flight conditions with sufficiently high angle of attack, these vehicles often have lightly damped, close to unstable lateral-directional dynamics, such as the dutch roll mode. As a result, a delta wing aircraft often exhibits the so-called wing rock (WR) phenomenon, with a back and forth rocking motion, while the aircraft sideslip angle, the roll and the yaw angular rates remain small. In this paper, the WR dynamics are defined as a lightly damped dutch roll mode excited by airmass vortical external input, acting at or near the dutch roll natural frequency. The vortical signal comes from Fourier-Galerkin approximation of the Navier-Stokes equation, with no-penetration boundary conditions and the resulting airmass velocities are calculated by the Lorenz dynamical system of three coupled bilinear ordinary differential equations. In that context, the Lorenz bilinear dynamics become the disturbance-generator exosystem, acting on the lightly damped lateral-directional aircraft mode at or near its natural frequency, and thus exciting it to produce near oscillatory wing rocking motion. Using the proposed model, a flight control design trade study is conducted to mitigate and suppress the WR phenomenon.

papers.title: Solar-Blind Ultraviolet Communication: Taxonomy and Experimental Characterization

This paper presents a taxonomy of all four fundamental solar-blind UVC channels together with representative experimental validations and a comparative performance analysis. The proposed framework provides practical guidelines for selecting appropriate channel architectures for future solar-blind UVC systems.

papers.title: A Deficiency-Based Approach for Unbalanced Three-Phase Distribution System Expansion Planning
papers.summary: Distribution planners typically characterize grid needs through power flow studies and fit upgrades to those needs by hand. More principled one-shot optimization methods either do not scale or misrepresent unbalanced three-phase networks. This paper proposes an iterative planning process that alternates between two problem classes with mature off-the-shelf solvers. An optimal power flow (OPF) problem quantifies the deficiency of a candidate portfolio by optimizing the dispatch of controllable devices and measuring thermal and voltage violations on a common scale, with an optimal value of zero exactly at adequate portfolios. The OPF multipliers give a first-order approximation of the relief each investment candidate would provide. We bound the error of this approximation and show that structural properties of the deficiency guard it against overestimation. Building on this property, a heuristic cutting-plane search uses a mixed-integer linear program to propose each next portfolio from these approximations. On six unbalanced three-phase feeders from the SMART-DS dataset, the search outperforms a linearized optimization-based benchmark, and the results agree across five variants of the deficiency.

papers.title: Coordinated Conservation Voltage Reduction and Network Topology Reconfiguration in Active Distribution Networks
papers.summary: Distribution networks rely on conservation voltage reduction (CVR) and network topology reconfiguration (NTR) to manage demand, distributed energy resources (DERs), and tighter operating margins. Yet these strategies are typically deployed independently, despite coupled effects on feeder voltages, losses, and loading. This paper addresses that gap by developing a day-ahead mixed-integer second order cone programming (MISOCP) framework that jointly optimizes feeder head voltage control and network reconfiguration. The formulation incorporates AC branch flow constraints, ZIP load models, DERs, battery energy storage systems, and multi substation radiality. Using modified IEEE 33 bus and 123 bus systems, four configurations isolate the individual and coordinated effects of CVR and NTR. On the 33-bus system under mixed ZIP loading, NTR reduces active energy loss by 2.50%, while coordinated operation reduces it by 2.91% relative to SDN and produces a 2.46% CVR induced active load reduction relative to SDNTR. Under constant impedance loading, coordinated operation reduces active energy loss by 17.65% relative to SDN, while CVR reduces active load by 14.61% relative to SDNTR. DER portfolio scaling shows a nonmonotonic coordinated load reduction response, strongest at 20% penetration and decreasing at higher levels. On the 123 bus system, NTR reduces losses by 19.3%, while CVR reduces voltage dependent load energy by 2.3 to 2.4%. Under loading stress, SDN becomes infeasible at 120% loading, whereas CEDNTR remains feasible. Overall, the results demonstrate complementary, operating condition dependent benefits shaped by load composition, DER portfolio scaling, feeder topology, voltage margins, and source constraints, highlighting the value of joint optimization.

papers.title: MSVAE: Rethinking Musical Semantics in Continuous Latent Spaces
papers.summary: Continuous latent representations underlie recent diffusion-based lyrics-to-song and text-to-music systems, yet aligning lyric conditions with these latents remains difficult: existing systems resort to generator-side machinery such as sentence-level timestamps, auxiliary alignment objectives, or semi-autoregressive decoding, while the latents they predict are still produced by autoencoders trained purely for reconstruction. We address this difficulty from the representation side. We propose MSVAE (Music Semantic Variational Autoencoder), which structures its continuous latent around two complementary semantic streams: work-level compositional content and lyric-level linguistic-vocal content. Partitioned dual-stream alignment makes both streams explicit by aligning disjoint latent subspaces with frozen lead-sheet and ASR references, while a semantic-first gated residual posterior derives its base from a frozen music-SSL encoder and admits acoustic information only through gated, bounded corrections. MSVAE achieves competitive stereo reconstruction and stronger MARBLE probing than continuous-autoencoder baselines, and improves downstream lyrics-to-song and text-to-music generation. Notably, with only an untimed phoneme prefix and no lyric timing, MSVAE yields the lowest phoneme error rate, whereas all baseline representations require sentence-level alignment to produce intelligible vocals.

papers.title: On the CSIT-Limited Delay Robustness of IR-HARQ in Finite Blocklength RSMA Networks
papers.summary: This letter studies the throughput and reliability of power-constrained rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) with variable-length incremental-redundancy hybrid automatic repeat request (IR-HARQ) under finite blocklength (FBL) transmission and imperfect channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT). While perfect-CSIT feedback-delay tolerance approaches a natural ceiling as signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) grows, we show imperfect CSIT imposes a strictly lower, finite ceiling set solely by CSIT quality, one that transmit power cannot overcome. We derive analytical expressions and tight approximations for common- and private-stream decoding failure probabilities, capturing FBL and CSIT uncertainty via a unified CSIT-degradation factor. Also, we show that residual interference saturates effective stream power at high SNR, limiting reliability and producing this delay-tolerance ceiling. Simulations validate the analysis and quantify the ceiling, offering design insights for delay-robust RSMA under imperfect CSIT.

papers.title: Reduced-Order Backstepping Control of Nonlinear Mechanical Systems with Input Delay via Galerkin Projection
papers.summary: This paper addresses trajectory tracking for a class of nonlinear mechanical systems with input delay. The delayed actuator channel is represented as an equivalent transport partial differential equation, thereby transforming the original delayed system into a coupled plant-channel representation. A finite-dimensional approximation of the delay channel is then constructed through Galerkin projection, resulting in an explicit ODE model of the delayed actuator dynamics. Using this reduced-order plant-channel model, a backstepping controller is developed, and Lyapunov analysis establishes uniform exponential stability of the nominal tracking error dynamics for the reduced-order Galerkin model. To enhance practical implementation, a command-filtered version is also introduced to avoid direct differentiation of virtual controls, for which a corresponding uniform ultimate boundedness result is obtained. Simulation studies are provided to validate the proposed design and illustrate the effectiveness of the method.

papers.title: Safety-Aware Dimension Selection for Reduced-Order Model Predictive Control
papers.summary: Model reduction can substantially reduce the computational burden of model predictive control (MPC) for high-dimensional systems, but a reduced dimension chosen for performance may be insufficient for safety-critical operation. This paper introduces a safety-aware dimension-selection framework in which the prediction model adapts to the order of the model required to maintain a certified finite-horizon safety condition. Dynamic active subspaces provide a performance-oriented ordering of reduced coordinates, while finite-horizon error bounds robustly enforce discrete-time control barrier function constraints. The controller selects the smallest prediction order for which the resulting safety-critical MPC problem remains feasible. We establish full-order horizon safety, recursive feasibility, and closed-loop invariance of the safe set under the proposed reduced-order formulation. The proposed approach therefore adapts the prediction complexity to safety requirements, avoiding unnecessary high-dimensional prediction during benign operation.

papers.title: Active noise cancellation extends the benefit of AI speech enhancement in real hearing-aid recordings
papers.summary: Active noise cancellation (ANC) is common in headphones but rare in hearing aids, and its value for understanding speech in noise is not established. Algorithms that improve signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) act only on the hearing aid's amplified path, while unprocessed sound also reaches the eardrum directly through the vent, limiting the SNR improvement that is realized. Our earlier simulations predicted that attenuating this direct path with ANC would substantially increase the benefit of such processing. We tested that prediction in three hardware conditions: a standard receiver-in-canal (RIC) hearing aid, and an ANC-capable RIC with ANC off and on. Each was fit to NAL-NL2 targets for an N3 hearing loss and recorded on KEMAR with an AI speech-enhancement algorithm (AI-SE) off and on, in seven realistic scenes above 70 dB SPL. Speech and noise spectra were estimated from each recording with a binary time-frequency mask derived from the clean speech. AI-SE produced a similar peak benefit of about 4 dB in the high frequencies in all three conditions, but that benefit stayed at or above 1 dB only above 1500, 600, and 130 Hz for the standard RIC, ANC RIC (ANC off), and ANC RIC (ANC on), respectively, closely tracking the measured attenuation of the direct path. With AI-SE on, ANC RIC (ANC on) improved SII-weighted SNR by 5.1 dB relative to the open ear, compared with 3.3 dB for ANC RIC (ANC off) and 1.6 dB for the standard RIC. With AI-SE off, enabling ANC added only 0.2 dB. ANC is therefore an enabling technology: on its own it added little, but by attenuating the direct path it allowed SNR-enhancing processing to deliver substantially greater benefit at the eardrum, extending that benefit to much lower frequencies.

papers.title: On the Geometry of Radar Waveform Design with Constraints
papers.summary: Many optimization problems that arise in signal processing applications are based around optimizing vectors/matrices of numeric sequences. These problems are often inherently non-convex due to non-linear constraints. Such problems are frequently solved through convex relaxations of the original problem to allow for computationally simple algorithms to be leveraged, albeit with the potential for appreciable performance costs in the solution space. When the constraints of a problem can be implicitly satisfied through the structure of a Riemannian manifold, optimizing directly on said manifold affords the opportunity to solve the problem in an unconstrained fashion. Therefore, when feasible, recasting the constrained optimization problem in Euclidean space as an unconstrained optimization over a Riemannian manifold offers greater flexibility and improved efficiency over convex relaxation based approaches. This paper introduces the minimal smooth optimization theory required and adapts the notation to a radar signal design context. In addition, we apply our approach to two different problems in direct parallel to contemporary convex relaxation-based signal design literature.

papers.title: Stabilizing Low-Stiffness Soft Robots at Unstable Equilibria: A Model-Based Optimal Control Approach
papers.summary: Continuum soft robots are highly nonlinear and underactuated systems, which makes stabilizing them around unstable equilibrium points difficult. This challenge becomes even greater in low stiffness regimes, where gravitational forces dominate elastic forces. In this letter, we explore whether optimal control can address these challenges using a computa- tionally efficient method suitable for real time use. We propose a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) approach based on Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), combined with an accurate reduced order Variable Strain model with analytical derivatives. This results in an efficient control framework for addressing the stabilization problem. Tested on a soft inverted pendulum and other hybrid soft rigid systems, the method outperforms traditional controllers, stabilizes more challenging configurations, and operates reliably at real time speeds (50 150 Hz), demonstrating both effectiveness and practical feasibility in experimental settings.

papers.title: Reach-Avoid Certificates for Contact-based Stochastic Hybrid Systems
papers.summary: This work studies certified reach-avoid control of stochastic hybrid systems in which a stochastic differential equation governs continuous flow and a controlled stochastic kernel governs guard-triggered resets. The input appears only in the reset kernel, where it determines the post-jump distribution. Certificates for such systems have so far assumed spontaneous or controller-chosen jump times, a finite horizon, or discrete-time dynamics; we certify, over the infinite horizon, that the target is reached before the unsafe set with at least a prescribed probability. First, we introduce reach-avoid contact certificates, whose flow and jump conditions are imposed only on a sublevel corridor, and prove that any such certificate with a compatible reset policy meets the specification; a pointwise safety filter extends this guarantee from verification to control by constraining arbitrary nominal controllers. Next, we prove that executions are non-Zeno and bound the expected settling time and reset count. We frame certificate search as a linear program over any twice-differentiable dictionary followed by independent verification. We illustrate our approach via comparisons where the certified region is a subset covering 93.6\% of the ground truth and where our certificate-based safety filter reaches the goal while reducing collisions from 68 to zero across 200 episodes of a dribbling ball problem.

papers.title: STATCOM-Based Flicker Mitigation in Electric Arc Furnace Systems Using DQ-PI and Lyapunov-Based Nonlinear Control
papers.summary: Electric arc furnaces inject stochastic reactive-power swings that cause voltage flicker at the point of common coupling. This paper compares two STATCOM inner controllers for an 11~kV, 50~Hz furnace feeder: a split-frequency DQ-PI design and a Lyapunov-based nonlinear design whose integral state is retained in the storage function, giving global asymptotic stability of the nominal unsaturated current-error subsystem. Gains for both controllers were tuned by a frozen metaheuristic campaign and then evaluated over 600~s with an IEC~61000-4-15 digital flickermeter. A post-campaign audit showed that the stochastic arc realization used for the original comparison was periodic, so the two selected gain sets were frozen without retuning or reselection and evaluated on ten independent stochastic realizations that had been specified and archived before the STO-ENS validation campaign, together with a paired uncompensated case for each realization. Both controllers reduce the mean short-term flicker severity by about 62% relative to the STO-ENS uncompensated baseline, and no statistically detectable difference in mean flicker severity is found between them. They separate instead in realization sensitivity: the Lyapunov standard deviation across arcs is roughly one third that of DQ-PI. Controller ordering inferred from a single stochastic trajectory is therefore not a reliable measure of stochastic robustness, and ensemble validation is necessary.

papers.title: Filtering for Liveness: Recurrence via Backup Reachability Control Barrier Functions
papers.summary: Liveness requires a dynamical system to repeatedly accomplish a desired objective over time. In this work, we consider a particular form of liveness known as recurrence, which requires the closed-loop trajectory to regularly revisit a prescribed set, with no more than a specified amount of time between visits. Inspired by the control barrier function (CBF) safety-filter paradigm, we develop a controller-filtering framework that makes adjustments to a nominal controller only when necessary to guarantee recurrence. Unlike conventional CBF methods, which enforce set forward invariance, our framework allows the trajectory to leave the set while guaranteeing its timely return. To achieve this, our framework combines two components: a backup reachability CBF that preserves the ability to return to the prescribed set within the allowable time, and a timing-based mechanism that invokes a reaching controller only when the nominal behavior would otherwise fail to meet the return-time requirement. The resulting framework guarantees recurrence while preserving the nominal behavior when possible, enabling control objectives that require temporary excursions from the set, such as traversal between disjoint regions. Our method is successfully utilized in a drone racing example with a recurrence constraint on beacon visibility.

papers.title: Direct Electromechanical Actuation of the Shift Drum in Non-Synchronized Motorcycle Transmissions: From Actuator Sizing and Electronics Design to Closed-Loop Position Control
papers.summary: This thesis presents the direct electromechanical actuation of the shift drum in a non-synchronized motorcycle transmission. A DC motor drives the shift drum through a self-locking worm gear, so the entire foot shift mechanism is eliminated. As a reference, 84 manual gear changes of a large-displacement series-production motorcycle were measured on a chassis dynamometer; the mean shift time is 80 ms for upshifts and 92 ms for downshifts. The system design covers the complete chain from the mechanics to the software. The actuator motor is sized from inertia, friction and gear ratio. A dedicated shift controller is developed with supply filtering, signal conditioning for the position sensor and the incremental encoder, an H-bridge motor driver and a custom circuit board based on a SAMD21 microcontroller. The embedded firmware implements position control of the shift drum with a proportional controller, without inner speed or current loops. On a gearbox test rig, a gear change is completed in less than 80 ms without overshoot in a single measurement, below the mean of the manual reference shifts. The analysis reveals a trade-off in the choice of the worm gear ratio: at a ratio of 30, about 93% of the motor torque is needed to accelerate the motor shaft and the worm. A ratio of about 8 halves the required torque, but the worm gear then loses its self-locking. The measured shift times are published as an open dataset.

papers.title: Optimal Gating for Dead-Time-Constrained Single-Photon Detectors
papers.summary: We develop a Fisher-information framework for optimizing single-photon detector gating in periodic experiments, in contrast to previous more empirical or heuristic gating choices. After each photon detection, such a detector is insensitive for a dead time, so that an early background detection can obscure a later signal. Gating preserves availability for informative photons by selectively deactivating the detector. In our high-pile-up simulation of distance-attenuated lidar, our practical data-independent gating design reduces the worst-case asymptotic range variance by more than half relative to the free-running acquisition (which does not use any gating). More generally, we characterize achievable detector-active frequencies as a convex polytope and construct an adaptive rule that asymptotically attains an optimal "oracle" design without prior knowledge of the physical parameters. We also derive practical criteria that quantify the potential gains of gating and/or photon attenuation over unattenuated free-running acquisition.

papers.title: Co-Adaptive Entropy Modeling and Rate-Distortion-Optimal Bit Allocation for Perceptual Audio Coding
papers.summary: We present a perceptual audio coder in which the entropy-coding model and the bit allocation co-adapt across blocks without model side information. papers.title: Energy-Efficient RF Chain Activation for Uplink mmWave Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems: A Minimum-Cost Maximum-Flow Approach
papers.summary: With the incessant demand for green and sustainable communications, energy efficiency (EE) has become a cornerstone of sixth-generation (6G) network design, especially for cell-free millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, which can achieve significant throughput gains by leveraging large-scale antenna arrays. Adaptive radio frequency (RF) chain activation (ARFA) is a key technique for reducing power consumption without severely degrading the achievable rate, thereby enhancing the total EE of 6G MIMO systems. In this paper, we propose a minimum-cost maximum-flow (MCMF)-based ARFA scheme to reduce unnecessary power consumption and maximize the total EE of uplink mmWave cell-free massive MIMO systems. Simulation results indicate that the proposed approach can significantly improve the total EE while maintaining a relatively high achievable rate and acceptable computational complexity.

papers.title: Input-Constrained Active Disturbance Rejection Control for AUVs
papers.summary: This paper addresses the control of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in dynamic environments, where wave-induced forces, modelling errors, and actuator limitations make reliable control challenging. Active disturbance rejection control (ADRC), together with an extended state observer (ESO), estimates lumped uncertainties online, simplifying control design using nominal models. However, existing stability analyses typically assume bounded control inputs and derivatives, which are difficult to guarantee under unknown disturbances and measurement noise. To bridge this theory--practice gap, this paper introduces an ADRC framework with active input saturation and post-saturation low-pass filtering. The saturation constrains the control magnitude, while the filter regularizes the saturated signal to ensure bounded input-rate variations. By explicitly enforcing these conditions, the proposed system guarantees semi-global practical asymptotic stability. High-fidelity simulations and experiments on an underwater robotic platform demonstrate robust control performance under severe environmental disturbances and actuator constraints. A supplementary video is available at https://youtu.be/AEFlZ69Yg00.

papers.title: Multi-Day Stochastic Dispatch for Power Systems With Long-Duration Storage Using Diffusion-Generated Weather Forecasts
papers.summary: As power systems shift toward high shares of wind and solar, long-duration storage becomes pivotal for balancing multi-day deficits and surpluses of uncertain supply and demand. Current dispatch strategies for long-duration storage either assign a fixed value to stored energy or extend the modeled horizon using a single forecast. Stochastic system dispatch with a multi-day horizon for long-duration storage remains unexplored, and existing stochastic dispatch only considers day-ahead uncertainty or Markovian uncertainty beyond one week of perfect foresight. Therefore, we benchmark stochastic multi-day dispatch against deterministic alternatives in a rolling-horizon setup. To emulate probabilistic multi-day forecasts, we combine diffusion with a semi-Markov model of weather regimes and a logistic growth model for meteorological forecast errors. At high renewable shares, stochastic operation reduces thermal backup generation and consistently eliminates loss of load. The benefits decrease with smaller shares of renewables, less long-duration storage, or higher forecast skill. Overall, our results suggest that systems with high shares of variable renewables can substantially benefit from probabilistic multi-day forecasts and stochastic dispatch.

papers.title: A Collision-Aware Predictive Rerouting Framework for Connected and Automated Vehicles
papers.summary: In this paper, we investigate the problem of mitigating non-recurrent congestion in urban transportation networks through predictive and adaptive routing for connected and automated vehicles (CAVs). We propose a collision-aware predictive rerouting framework that integrates microscopic SUMO simulation, DCRNN-based spatiotemporal traffic-state forecasting, collision-window lookahead, and multi-objective route scoring. The routing controller uses predicted congestion, live emission information, route-length penalties, and incident-window constraints to decide when CAVs deviate from their current routes. The completed simulation campaign across three urban network scenarios, five CAV penetration levels, three random seeds, and multiple benchmark rerouting strategies shows that the proposed full framework does not dominate all baselines in aggregate travel time, distance, or emissions. Instead, its principal advantage is operational stability: it maintains comparable network-level efficiency while substantially reducing rerouting frequency relative to active rerouting baselines. These results demonstrate both the promise and the tradeoffs of embedding graph-based prediction and collision awareness into real-time CAV rerouting, and they motivate further work on forecast calibration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and system-level fairness between CAV and non-CAV traffic.

papers.title: Timing Misalignment and Its Impact on OTFS and Other Delay-Based Waveforms
papers.summary: The shift towards 6G wireless networks calls for advanced waveforms to support emerging applications such as ultra-reliable and massive machine-type communications. Among the proposed candidates, OTFS, ODDM, OTSM, and OCDM share the common feature of exploiting the delay domain for data transmission. While these waveforms offer significant advantages in high-mobility and sensing scenarios, their integration into multi-user uplink systems reveals a critical challenge: timing misalignment (TM). Unlike OFDM, where residual timing offsets translate into phase rotations, delay-based waveforms experience actual shifts of resources, whose impact we investigate in this work. We show that the aforementioned waveforms can be unified under a time-invariant setup through a common input--output relation, which enables a unified analysis of TM in uplink resource allocation. The results reveal a fundamental trade-off between interference mitigation and guard overhead in the presence of TM. We further benchmark the observed behavior against OFDM under Doppler spread as a reference impairment and highlight the analogy between TM in delay-based allocation and Doppler spread in frequency-based allocation. The results show that delay-based waveforms can maintain a net performance advantage over OFDM in the considered setup. Beyond this unified Doppler-free analysis, we evaluate the joint impact of Doppler spread and TM on each waveform individually. We also investigate BER performance and show how coding can mitigate the resulting interference. This study therefore establishes a problem framework that motivates the development of future compensation and scheduling strategies for practical multi-user operation of delay-based waveforms.

papers.title: Learning or Modeling? Virtual XL-RIS Observation Reconstruction for Near-Field Sensing
papers.summary: A passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS) offers a position-sensitive aperture for near-field sensing, but its element-wise signals are not directly observed. Recovering this virtual RIS observation (VOR) from fewer base-station measurements requires prior information. This paper investigates when calibrated propagation geometry or paired training data provides the more effective reconstruction prior. For a common sensing operator and target signal, we develop off-grid near-field sparse parametric reconstruction (OG-NF-SPR) and compare it with compact and DenseNet-based deep reconstructors. OG-NF-SPR uses reflected-path projection for position initialization, followed by Bayesian estimation of all path gains and continuous position refinement. A causal extension incorporates temporal correlation without trajectory labels. Controlled simulations use near-field UAV tracking as an illustration and separately examine noise, position-distribution shift, calibration error, and propagation mismatch. Under matched propagation at 20 dB, OG-NF-SPR achieves approximately 67% lower reconstruction NMSE than the two nominal deep networks. At low SNR, statistical averaging is more effective than selecting a single geometric explanation. Under sufficiently strong repeatable mismatch, a same-size network trained on the mismatch family outperforms the nominal physical estimator, whereas nominal training does not provide this benefit. Temporal regularization also reduces position RMSE from 0.653 m to 0.225 m on a shared trajectory. The results relate reconstruction performance to measurement quality, calibration accuracy, and training coverage, providing guidance on when geometry can replace supervised labels and when additional data are useful.

papers.title: Stability Transfer for Autonomous Systems via Higher-Order Taylor-Truncated Lyapunov Certificates
papers.summary: We develop analytical sufficient conditions for certifying the local asymptotic stability of nonlinear autonomous systems based on Lyapunov functions derived from their finite-order Taylor polynomial approximations. This approach translates the stability analysis problem from the original nonlinear dynamics to a more computationally tractable polynomial domain. The derived conditions allow for the explicit calculation of a guaranteed inner approximation of the region of attraction ($\mathrm{ROA}$). We show how sum-of-squares (SOS) programming and grid search can be used to systematically search for polynomial Lyapunov functions that yield a large certified threshold radius and extract a certified invariant set inner approximation of the $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial original system. The framework is then applied to a control tuning problem: finding reduced-effort Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controllers that ensure that a given initial state of interest belongs to the certified $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial closed loop system. The effectiveness of the overall methodology is demonstrated using a pendulum with nonlinear damping and a nonlinear control system.

papers.title: Constrained Grid-Forming Control for Photovoltaic Systems: A Control Barrier Function Approach
papers.summary: This paper leverages control barrier functions (CBFs) to systematically account for constraints of voltage source converters (VSCs) and photovoltaic (PV) resources in grid-forming (GFM) control. The proposed control combines (unconstrained) dual-port GFM control with control barrier functions (CBFs) to ensure reliable and safe operation of a GFM PV system under grid faults, sudden changes in irradiance, and load perturbations. First, CBFs are used to encode physical and operational limits of the PV system, namely current and voltage limits at its ac and dc terminals. Then, CBFs are used to restrict the dynamics of dual-port GFM control to within the VSC and PV limits during both transient and steady states. To this end, a cost function is defined that encodes trade-offs between forming the ac voltage phase angle/frequency and voltage magnitude under constraints. Then, real-time optimization is used to make the least modification, as measured by the cost function, to the (unconstrained) dual-port GFM control state to remain within the safe set encoded by the CBFs. Finally, the performance of the developed constrained GFM control is evaluated through EMT simulations in MATLAB/Simulink.

papers.title: Low-Altitude Agentic Networks: From UAV Connectivity to Workflow-Driven Capability Orchestration
papers.summary: Low-altitude platforms are evolving from connected sensing nodes into autonomous agents capable of bounded task interpretation, skill invocation, and local decision making. Increasing the intelligence of individual unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), however, does not resolve the organization problem that arises when mission workflows depend on capabilities distributed across multiple platforms and provider feasibility changes with network, resource, and mobility conditions. We propose low-altitude agentic networking as a task-level networking paradigm and develop a reference architecture that separates workflow logic from executor identity. Within a validated domain-specific workflow space, each ready operation is translated into a capability requirement and dynamically bound to an agent that remains feasible under current conditions. Task contracts and structured evidence govern workflow execution, while routine provider and link changes are handled through workflow-preserving local adaptation before high-level repair is invoked. A trace-calibrated discrete-event case study identifies a bounded operating region: conventional organization remains effective for simple workflows under stable conditions, whereas agentic networking becomes beneficial when workflow dependencies are tightly coupled, capability feasibility changes during execution, and viable local recovery paths remain available.

papers.title: Service-Aware Hosting Capacity Assessment of Edge Data Centers with Workload Flexibility
papers.summary: The growing demand for edge computing, content delivery, and AI services is driving the interconnection of edge data centers (DCs) with distribution networks. Before interconnection, utilities evaluate how much DC capacity can be accommodated without violating feeder current and voltage limits. Fixed peak load representations can overlook service dependent demand patterns, cooling related facility demand, and delay tolerant computing tasks. This paper develops a hosting capacity (HC) assessment model for edge DCs with shiftable workload scheduling. Three representative types are considered: mobile edge computing (MEC), content delivery network (CDN), and AI DCs. Facility demand is modeled by combining fixed base demand, service driven demand, prescribed cooling-overhead coefficient, and a shiftable workload component. Workload execution is optimized under arrival causality, maximum delay, daily energy balance constraints, and the resulting active and reactive loads are embedded in a distribution power flow model. Compared with the baseline without load shifting, the maximum bus level HC gain on the IEEE 33-bus system reaches 4.46% for MEC DCs and 9.89% for AI DCs, while CDN case shows negligible gain under the assumed cache management windows.

papers.title: Modeling and Design of a Diaphragm-Integrated Photonic Waveguide Microphone
papers.summary: Can an integrated optical readout improve the useful operating range of a miniature microphone? We address this question with an analytical model of a diaphragm carrying the sensing arm of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI). The model links pressure-induced bending to waveguide elongation and then to photocurrent, allowing mechanical sensitivity and optical detection limits to be assessed separately. Optical shot noise and back-cavity thermomechanical noise set the pressure resolution, while a 10% total harmonic distortion criterion defines acoustic overload. Two operating regimes are examined: a compact MEMS microphone with 1 mW optical input and a measurement microphone with 100 mW optical input. For the compact case, a 1 mm diameter, 1 micrometer thick, stress-free silicon diaphragm and 100% modulation efficiency give a predicted signal-to-noise ratio of 78 dB and acoustic overload pressure of 124 dB. The higher-power case lowers the modeled noise floor and increases dynamic range relative to the selected measurement microphone benchmark. These estimates rely on favorable assumptions and do not establish a substantial overall advantage in conventional microphone applications. Remote optical interrogation offers a separate motivation for harsh-environment sensing, but the temperature tolerance of the proposed sensing head remains unverified. The analysis identifies the design tradeoffs and measurements needed to test the predicted performance.

papers.title: A Programming, Robotics and Automatic Control Intervention for Secondary Education Students in Sweden and Italy
papers.summary: This study evaluates the AutoSTEM workshop, an intervention for secondary education that combines a serious game with PID-controlled hardware. Seven workshops were conducted across Sweden and Italy. The six Swedish workshops adopted an explicitly SDT-informed facilitation framework, while the Italian workshop followed the existing educational robotics format without a formally defined SDT facilitation protocol. Self-reports, an objective knowledge quiz, and qualitative responses were analysed using multiple site-adjusted statistical approaches. Technical-specific self-efficacy increased substantially in both conditions, with large effect sizes, while objective knowledge showed only modest, non-significant gains. No significant site-adjusted differences were found between SDT and control conditions for the primary outcomes. Perceived engagement was higher in the control condition, although this finding should be interpreted cautiously. The objective knowledge composite remained positive but non-significant across sensitivity analyses. Female participants reported smaller PID self-efficacy gains than males. Qualitative findings supported evidence of PID learning while identifying technical and pacing barriers. Overall, the results suggest that the technology-rich intervention supports competence development, regardless of SDT-informed facilitation.

papers.title: Shuf-Scatter: Permutation-Based DLI Suppression for OFDM Ambient Backscatter
papers.summary: Direct Link Interference (DLI) remains a major bottleneck in Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM)-based Ambient Backscatter Communication (AmBC) systems. This letter proposes Shuf-Scatter, a scheme that applies a deterministic permutation to the reflected OFDM waveform to create a distinct correlation-domain signature. By exploiting the quasi-orthogonality between the reshuffled backscatter signal and the direct-link component, the proposed receiver effectively mitigates DLI and enables reliable detection without requiring dedicated spectral resources, or instantaneous Backscatter-Link (BL) Channel State Information (CSI). Analytical and simulation results demonstrate that Shuf-Scatter achieves superior Bit Error Rate (BER) performance under strong DLI while preserving the integrity of the legacy OFDM transmission.

papers.title: Safe Unicycle Navigation Among Multiple Obstacles Under Bounded Disturbances: A Learning-Augmented CLF-CBF Approach (Extended Version)
papers.summary: This paper presents a robust control framework for safe navigation of a unicycle robot to a goal among multiple static obstacles under an unknown, time-varying disturbance. The controller solves a single real-time quadratic program (QP) that combines a goal-reaching term with one safety term per obstacle. The goal-reaching term is a cross-track control Lyapunov function built from body-frame tracking errors rather than a bearing angle, which keeps its Lie derivatives bounded everywhere, including the goal. Safety is encoded using robust control barrier functions, one per obstacle, each tightened by a closed-form, state-dependent disturbance bound. When stabilization and safety conflict, a slack variable relaxes only the convergence requirement, so that the safety constraints remain strictly enforced. Whenever the QP is feasible, the robust barrier constraints guarantee forward invariance of every obstacle's safe set under all admissible disturbances. Complementing this safety guarantee, a Lyapunov analysis yields an explicit ultimate bound on the distance to the goal. A learning-augmented variant replaces the fixed objective with a reinforcement-learning reference, which accelerates convergence when multiple constraints are simultaneously active. We further derive the obstacle separation below which the gap between two obstacles becomes too narrow to pass through under the robust constraints. For such gaps, a learned virtual goal for the Lyapunov function steers the robot around the obstacles without compromising safety. Simulations, a Monte Carlo study, and a comparison against a sampled-data robust baseline support the theoretical results.

papers.title: Enforcing a Strict Safety Margin in LLM Text Generation via Barrier Lyapunov Control
papers.summary: Large language models are increasingly deployed without formal guarantees against toxic text generation. Existing control barrier function (CBF) based safety filters can keep the generation trajectory within a toxicity-free region, but do not enforce a positive distance from its boundary, allowing formally safe trajectories to approach the toxicity threshold arbitrarily closely and leaving little buffer against modelling errors or disturbances. We address this limitation with a Barrier Lyapunov Function (BLF) safety filter that enforces a prescribed clearance margin throughout generation while retaining the continuous-time transformer dynamics, including feedforward layers. The resulting safe input set is a half-space defined by a constraint affine in the control input, and is non-empty under certified surjectivity and classifier-nondegeneracy conditions. For margin-compatible initial conditions we prove that the clearance margin is never violated and that the prescribed clearance is restored exponentially, yielding an explicit clearance floor, and show that, as the margin vanishes, the admissible trajectories satisfy the exponential second-order CBF condition. We further derive an explicitly computable sufficient disturbance budget under which the clearance guarantee degrades gracefully. Simulations on a small transformer illustrate the resulting improvement in safety clearance.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Source-Filter Model of Speech Production
papers.summary: Deep learning models of speech seldom represent the source-filter process by which speech is produced, relying instead on latent features with no physical correspondence to articulation or phonation. We propose SoFilNet, a self-supervised, differentiable Source-Filter Network that estimates the parameters of speech production directly from the raw waveform: a source, specified by fundamental frequency (F0), voicing and the aperiodicity of five frequency bands, and a filter, specified by ordered formant poles, additional poles that shape the rest of the spectral envelope, and antiresonance zeros. The model is trained only to reconstruct the input speech; no formant or pitch annotation is used. Since per-bin spectral losses favor blurred spectra wherever the model is uncertain, we train F0 and voicing against autocorrelation pseudo-labels refined with the model's own filter, aperiodicity against the periodic fraction of each band, and formant sharpness against spectral contrast. On VTR-FORMANTS, the estimated formants attain the lowest mean error among the reported methods, including supervised trackers, and on the unseen PTDB-TUG corpus the F0 frame error matches the best classical tracker and is lower than that of all learned trackers. The parameters are also consistent with speech production theory: aperiodicity rises with frequency and orders phone classes by the turbulence of their excitation, and the zeros deepen on nasal consonants, the lower one rising with place of articulation.

papers.title: Preliminary Exploration of Large Models Based on Self-Supervised Learning for Health Monitoring of Power Electronic Converters
papers.summary: Current artificial intelligence (AI) methods for power electronics converters make limited use of the abundant unlabeled data generated during real-world operation. This underexplored resource holds significant potential for advancing model performance. To address this gap, this paper presents PE-TSFM, a time-series foundation model tailored for power module health monitoring. The model adopts the PatchTST architecture combined with self-supervised learning and is trained on more than 143 million timestamps, where over 98\% of this training data is unlabeled and collected directly from an operating traction converter. In degradation classification tasks, PE-TSFM achieves an accuracy of 87\%, considerably surpassing five conventional time-series AI models whose performance ranges from 27\% to 45\%. These results demonstrate the model's strong few-shot learning capability and generalization across different operating conditions. This work promotes a shift from narrowly focused models in power electronics toward unified, scalable foundation models that can unlock value from large-scale unlabeled operational data.
